Michael learned a lot from Primal Xerx's memories as well but it was clear that the Primal never fought each other seriously. Primal Xerx was aware of a few basic things about the other Primal but that was about it.
Thus, Michael was at a disadvantage even though he was given years to grow stronger. The Untamed Jungle expanded, and Michael's people summoned millions of subjects on a daily basis, but it was unclear if that was enough. That was why the gods, Rebels, and others instructed their Awakened to either surrender and become part of the Untamed Jungle by binding themselves to the Primordial Tree Spirit, which would retain their Lord Powers while still granting Michael some of their soul power and faith or to give up their Lord Powers altogether and have everyone establish Links of Loyalty with Michael directly.
Everyone relied on Michael's success to change the universe permanently. Therefore, it was important to strengthen him as much as possible, granting him power through the Links of Loyalty's Soul Power, but also Godly Faith.
Most believed in Michael's power, but those subjected to him in the Origin Expanse provided much more faith than others. After all, he was the strongest entity in the Origin Expanse. Nobody could rival him there since not even the Primal discovered a way to enter the Origin Expanse.
Michael's prowess increased quickly, but he was still not satisfied. He was certain his strength succeeded Primal Xerx's power, which was great given he was actually weaker than Primal Xerx when he fought the Primal, but that wasn't enough. Maybe he could beat one of the Primal, but all of them when they fought together? Michael was not that powerful. Maybe he would never be.
'No, I can do it. I can defeat them. They're already afraid of me. They fear me. I can make use of that. As long as I drain their Essence, I can do it. But that requires the Weave Seal or something to sever the weave's connection to them. Or are there places without a connection to the weave? A place I can forcefully pull them? Is there something like that?'
Michael needed to research more. There had to be a way to defeat the Primal when they fought him together. But while defeating the Primal was one of his priorities, the highest priority was – and would always be – to survive. As long as he was strong enough to survive the combined onslaught of six Primal for an unknown timeframe, Michael would be strong enough to defeat them…at some point, at least.
But that meant he needed more power for now.
'My territory is already expanding rapidly. Everyone is helping me with the Untamed Jungle's expansion and to establish more settlements. The number of Summons and subjects entering my service exceeds ten million every day, and it is above 10 billion in total now. I'm stronger than ever, but something is still missing to upgrade the Untamed Jungle back to a Primal Region. What is it?'
[What about your War Rune? How about you check it? That way, you at least get to know whether the War Rune can help you or not.]
His War Rune had been bothering him for quite a while now. It stirred inside his Energy Vortex and tugged at him. However, Michael had been certain the War Rune's tugging and stirring was because he had already accumulated more than enough energy to advance to the 10th Tier. However, the 10th Tier was usually the threshold used by the Will to throw the Awakened out of the Origin Expanse. Michael couldn't afford to be thrown out of the Origin Expanse. Not before he wasn't certain the last condition to upgrade the Untamed Jungle to a Primal Region wasn't hidden in the Origin Expanse.
What if he was thrown out only to find out way too late that the last hidden piece was actually well-hidden in the Origin Expanse for nobody but him to reach? That would crush his plans, ending the battle with the Primal before it even began!
Still, the tugging of the War Rune had been bothering him for a while now. Since the Primal Essence had been inserted into the War Rune, the tugging and stirring inside the deepest parts of the Energy Vortex had started, but it got worse when Michael began to integrate more and more Primal Essence into the War Rune. Maybe that was a sign, a calling from someone. That was what his gut feeling told him.
However, at the same time, his gut feeling told him to be careful. After all, advancing to the 10th Tier might push him toward godhood, but it would also expel him from the Origin Expanse!
"You know?" Michael murmured after he had thought about it for more than 500 days.
"This is driving me crazy."
He murmured, accessing the War Rune once again.
It reacted, but it didn't push him toward the 10th Tier. No. The War Rune didn't force him toward godhood. Something else happened.
[End of Volume 19]

chapters.title: Chapter 1070 Meeting
chapters.content:
Chapter 1070  Meeting
The Runic Gate opened in the Origin Expanse. However, it wasn't a normal Runic Gate.
The Runic Gate opening before Michael was almost ten meters high and six meters wide. It tore through the fabric of the Untamed Jungle and released a soothing energy. The energy was alive and wiggling wildly as it spread into the surroundings. It was almost like the Essence of the Nature Divinity. Only that it was much more pure and potent.
Michael frowned, but on the inside, he was glad that the War Rune didn't push him to the 10th Tier. He did not want to get expelled by the Will just yet.
'The Will…' Michael tilted his head, 'Why does this Runic Gate feel like an invitation?'
He wasn't forced to enter the massive Runic Gate, but the War Rune pushed him forward while the Runic Gate tried to pull him closer. It was a request to come. Michael had no idea where he was invited to but the Runic Gate hardly gave Michael a chance. He had to enter.
Michael called out for the God Curses, but they were gone. The moment he accessed the War Rune, all connection with them had been cut. He tried turning around and calling out for others, but nobody was there.
'Should I use force?' He considered for a moment but shook his head. There was no need to use any violence. This is only an invitation to…some place. Maybe it is the Will. But why would the Will call for me? Does it want me to leave? No. The Will could have expelled me long ago. That can't be it. Is it about the upgrade to a Primal Region?'
Michael thought about it and hoped the Will would upgrade the Untamed Jungle to an Primal Region soon. Or maybe the Primal Essence inserted into the War Rune triggered something. What if it triggered the upgrade of the Untamed Jungle, and he had been postponing it by ignoring the War Rune's pleadings? 'That would be annoying. Please, don't let it be that. If I wasted our precious time because I didn't follow my gut feeling for once…'
Michael cursed inwardly and stepped through the Runic Gate. He expected to step out on solid ground, but the scenery changed drastically. He was suddenly high up in the air, thousands of kilometers above the ground, staring at the Origin Expanse.
He looked down and saw countless territories and regions. The Untamed Jungle stretched far. It was dense at its core, but small empty spots and remnants of large battles could be found on its outskirts. Michael smiled. Massive mountain ranges, an Ancient Region called Tundra of the Everlasting Winter – one-eighth of the Untamed Jungle's size – a massive ocean, and a Grand Region called Earl Plains surrounded the Untamed Jungle. The Untamed Jungle wouldn't have a problem expanding further, conquering the Arcane Ocean, the Thirteen Peaks, and the other regions. Still, Michael doubted anyone would invite him to this place high up in the sky to see how far the Untamed Jungle stretched.
He looked around but continued focusing on the ground to see the true extent of the Origin Expanse for the first time since forever. "Why does it look like everything is flat from up here? I expected the Origin Expanse to be like a massive planet." Michael murmured, studying the massive map before his eyes. There were countless massive regions, but only some were as large as the Untamed Jungle. Only two belonged to the latter. An endless plains region and a swamp.
"The Arcane Ocean is also larger than the Untamed Jungle," A resonant voice called out from behind, "As for the Origin Expanse's shape, I chose to keep it leveled like an expanse or a map if you want to think of it like that because the Origin Expanse is ever-expanding. The Origin Expanse contains half of the Essence accumulated by the weave. In fact, it produces as much Essence and energy as the weave since they're both part of the Creation. They were once one until I noticed what the Primals were doing."
Michael spun around, and his eyes widened. His lips parted, but no word escaped his lips. There was 'something' before him, but he couldn't put it into words.
The being talking to him looked like a human. No. It was made of pristine white essence and glowed brightly. All that looked human was the being's frame. Even then, Michael couldn't help but frown. The frame looked just like this.
"Yes, I do look like you. No. This is not a coincidence. No, I cannot read your mind. Yes, I like this play a lot. And yes, I do have emotions." The being was made of Essence, the purest form of Essence he had ever seen. Michael couldn't even be certain if Pure Aether was strong enough to cut through it. He could certainly test it out right here, but he didn't want to. He looked at the being and instinctively knew that it wasn't his enemy. The being was the Will.
The Will's pristine glowing frame fluctuated sometimes and ripples washed over the creature. Every ripple sent more Essence into the surrounding, overwhelming michael.
'His form is not stable, but the amount of Essence within him… It is much more than the Primal can contain. Is he also a Primal? How can I defeat someone like this if the Untamed Jungle has yet to reach the threshold of a Primal Region?'
Michael could tell that he would never have to fight the Will – he was unsure why he felt like that, but it was an instinctive thought – but he wondered if he had to be as strong as the Will to defeat the Primal. Or would he have to be stronger?
"It doesn't matter," The Will responded lightly to the question forming in Michael's mind.
"You will be strong soon enough. The Untamed Jungle is still growing even though it has regained its old glory. It regained the Primal Essence that was once taken from it – and me." Michael tilted his head, various questions forming in his mind, but he didn't get to ask any of them.
"The Warlords achieved their goal. Or as the beings of the new era call them. The Lords. They achieved their goals." The words of the Will stirred something within him. Or was the Essence filling the air around him? Michael was not sure, but something changed…about him and the Untamed Jungle.
"The Primal are not yet dead. I'm growing stronger but I am not strong enough," Michael commented, but the Will ignored him.
"The Origin Expanse regained their four Primal Regions. It regained its former glory and expanded further than I've ever expected it to grow. All I've wanted was to weaken the Primal. Then, everything changed. The Beginning and the Massacre of the Origin occurred. I had to change my plans. I had to start anew. Plan the start of a new era. But all of this required time. Lots of time. Eons."
The Will looked at Michael. At least, he felt like the Will was looking at him.
"Why do you think you are not strong enough? Your territory is, by far, the greatest territory of all time. You are also the first to ever create an Ancient Region, conquer an Ancient Region, to form a bond of souls with a Primordial creature in the Origin Expanse, bond with a Region, create a Primal Region, and conquer a Primal Region. You achieved much more than anyone could dream of. Why do you think you're too weak to handle what awaits you?"
Michael had a lot to say, but he was too stunned by the realization. While he was up here in the sky, talking to the Will, his territory was changing. The Untamed Jungle. It…was growing stronger. His Links of Loyalty to every being in the Untamed Jungle were growing tighter and more intimate. The Untamed Jungle was just being upgraded to a Primal Region!
Still, Michael didn't feel strong enough. The strength within him was skyrocketing rapidly. His body would probably require months to finish adapting, but he was certain to feel inadequate even then. After all, he was barely strong enough to defeat the weakest Primal. Maybe he could fight the other Primals head-on now, but defeat and kill all of them simultaneously? He couldn't do that.
"Is it necessary for all of them to die?" "How else am I going to stop them? The Primal will keep coming if I don't grow stronger. They might be afraid now, but I'm still not strong enough to handle them once they dare to fight back."
"Is that so?" "Yes!"
"If you say soo…"

chapters.title: Chapter 1071 Part of the Plan
chapters.content:
Chapter 1071  Part of the Plan
Michael quickly realized that talking to the Will was difficult. But what did he expect from a lonely being like the Will? He couldn't expect it to be sociable or to talk logically.
Still, he'd hoped the Will wouldn't be a social wreck and confusing.
"So…what exactly am I doing here? Is this some sort of necessary process to upgrade the Untamed Jungle into a Primal Region, or did you pull me away from the Origin Expanse to look at everything from above to tell me how well I am doing? If it is the latter, why? Or maybe I'm just missing out on something. I don't know. This is very confusing."
Michael sighed while studying the form of the Will again. The more he looked at it, the more the Will looked like him. The Will looked just like Michael. The frame, at least.
That was also confusing, forcing Michael to think about something else to get distracted. After all, the Will did not even think about answering his questions. It looked at him, not uttering a single word. That was how Michael ended up thinking about the things the Will had said. 'Wasn't there something about a plan? A plan about the new era and the time it would take to get started with everything?' Michael wondered.
He learned from the Will that the Origin Expanse possessed as much Essence as the weave. That was shocking, to say the least. It pushed Michael's mind to think about how powerful he would be if he had been in control of the entire Origin Expanse. If he conquered the entire Origin Expanse…would he be given access to the Expanse's Essence? Would he be strong enough to beat the six Primal simultaneously if so?
Michael was unsure about the former, but the latter seemed feasible. At least, it would be easier to defeat the Primal if he had as much Essence as the universe, the gods, and the Primal shared.
"What exactly was your plan? The plan that took eons to take off? You said the Lords achieved what you have been hoping for. Does that mean the new era has started?" Michael asked, but Will did not answer with a single word. It didn't even utter a single noise.
Instead, the Will gathered something in its hands that took Michael by great surprise. It was an Essence, pristine as the remaining Essence accumulated within the Will. However, something about it was different. It felt oddly familiar through Seer. Something about its consistency, properties, and structure was oddly familiar.
Maybe if Michael didn't possess a secondary body for a while, he wouldn't have noticed anything. But with Seer used at maximum power and great memories, which had engraved everything he ever witnessed in his mind, Michael remembered where he had seen it. Through Seer, Michael had seen something rooted in the deepest parts of his secondary body. However, this 'something' did not belong to the secondary body. It was a minuscule share of what had accumulated within Michael. The secondary body, as it was constructed after the image of the main body, cut a tiny portion of the things it couldn't copy. That was how an unknown Essence, rooted in the secondary body, entered Michael's vision.
He never knew where the Essence came from but researched it a little. He tore his body apart once he learned his body contained the same unknown Essence, but never learned much about the Essence. His research ended without any results. He didn't discover anything of use. But that was okay. Having something unknown in your body was odd, but Michael had never noticed it. The Essence wasn't hurting him either, and the God Curses considered it a good omen that his body contained a trace of the purest Essence. They even said the pure Essence might have been why they picked him as their vessel. Maybe the Will decided Fenrir was the perfect fit for Michael because of that. That was what Micheal thought at first, too. He'd listened to the God Curses and decided the unknown pure Essence was his fortune. It was a little piece of fortune.
That was what he'd thought. But when he saw the same Essence forming in the Will's hand, Michael's confidence crumbled. It shattered when he thought about the Will's plan of a new era and that the Lords had achieved what he wanted. Last but not least, there was the Will's shape. The pristine frame of pure Essence looked too much like Michael. Even a blind Awakened could tell that.
"What…is that? No, don't answer the question…I think I know the answer," Michael murmured, his eyes widening as the pieces came together.
He never thought about it that way and considered himself lucky. After all, he had been very lucky. The Will had always played in his favor. Always.
Every single time.
Everything was…almost like it was perfectly executed to push Michael to his limits mentally and physically. As if something or someone was trying to push him above and beyond his limits through the challenges thrown at him, inside and outside the Origin Expanse. He had always considered it a coincidence and part of the Curse thing everyone had been talking about. After all, Curses were pursued by misfortune, but Michael could turn misfortune into fortune via Extraction. That was why he started considering himself as extremely lucky at some point.
But now everything felt like the result of a well-oiled plan—a perfect plan to create someone capable of fighting the Primal head-on.
The color drained from Michael's face as realization struck.
He was part of the Will's plan. He had always been.
And everything went down like the Will had devised. The new era had started, just like the Will wanted.
Michael's eyes narrowed to tiny slits. Had he always been a marionette of the Will? If that was the case…where did his decisions start, and where did they end? Had he ever been in control of his actions in the first place, or was everything planned from the beginning?
Michael started doubting his existence.

chapters.title: Chapter 1072 Perfect Target
chapters.content:
Chapter 1072  Perfect Target
"Why did you do that?" Michael asked, "Why did you choose me? Why did you create me?" The Will did not exactly create Michael, but it sure created the man Michael had become through various events that shaped his character. All it took was tiny pushes here, some pulls there, and nice gifts at the right moment. Everything he had obtained from the Origin Expanse was orchestrated to turn him into the man he had become. He was born with Fenrir's Curse. Michael would have considered it as a coincidence since the Will couldn't have known Michael at that moment, but it was too much of a coincidence to be one. At least now that Michael was aware of the last pieces of information. The pieces he was missing to understand the big picture…the grand scheme of the Will.
'Extraction changed Fenrir's powers. They didn't alter the powers, but Extraction allowed me to acquire Soultraits like candy and upgrade them. That is something nobody has ever done. Nobody has even been capable of it. Except for the Will. It must have altered Fenrir's power, but not enough to attract any attention. Fenrir is prideful enough to consider his powers supreme. He would have never noticed anything wrong, even though he had never been capable of extracting Soultraits. But that's easy to hide. Fenrir is a god and has always been. He was never interested in Soultrait Symbols in the first place. Thus, he never even considered trying extracting Soultraits as they're considered inferior…'
Michael swallowed hard, and he tilted his head.
'Fenrir has been revolting against me a lot. Was that because of Extraction's slight alteration, or was it because of something else? In fact, when Extraction grew stronger, it became harder to control Fenrir for a long time. Was that also because of the changes infused by the Will?'
He stared at the Will, the pleasant and soothing feeling he'd felt when around the creator of the Origin Expanse replaced by confusion and sadness. There was no anger, even though he would have loved to be angry at the Will.
'The Lord Rift must have also been part of the Will's plan. My encounter with Taros as well. Danny's death against the Undead Pharaoh…was that too planned? And Masked Saber's death in the Lord Rift, followed by his return in the Miniature Coffin Keychain?'
Too many coincidences aligned, especially his arrival at the Untamed Jungle and his perfectly suited powers. The discovery of the Temple of the Forgotten. Throwing the Dragys at him, forcing him to enter the Temple of the Forgotten in a timely manner. Everything that happened in the Origin Expanse could have been the Will's scheme.
In fact, it was probably the Will's scheme.
"My plan was set in motions countless years ago when I offered the Primal to seal gods in Soultrait Symbols. I reached out with a finger, but they grasped the whole hand, which was exactly what I had been hoping for. They were greedy but also desperate to remove the threats without killing them. After all, their deaths would have altered the weave IF they were killed by the Primal themselves. While that does not matter anymore, given the recent deaths of Primal and gods, it did matter hundreds of thousands of years ago.
I devised several plans and came up with the idea of waiting for the strongest mortal vessel to appear in the Origin Expanse. However, even after hundreds of thousands of years ended, nobody suitable appeared. That was when I decided to intervene more actively. I spread more rewards and created Ancient Ruins, Dungeons, Lord Rifts, and special rewards for attaining seemingly impossible tasks. Creating everything was easy. All it needed was enough Essence."
The will sighed.
"Unfortunately, the plan didn't work out. Mortals acquired enough power to transform into gods. They conquered ruins, dungeons, and rifts, thus accumulating the Essences stored within these places. That was part of the rewards I was willing to give them. The Essences produced by the Expanse were used to spread the expanse, create Lords, and help everyone grow stronger. I was trying to increase the potential of all living beings to create The One.
But even that wasn't enough. My subtle actions weren't enough to create the changes needed to create an almighty Lord. That changed subtly when I started using the bloodlines of those with the strongest potential…those feared by most people. I merged the Curses of sealed gods into their souls. It started with fractions of their sealed essence, amplified by the Essence of the Origin Expanse, to create stronger beings. Their power skyrocketed, but the Curses were too powerful and wreaked havoc in the minds and souls of the first Curse Users.
I was forced to seal the Curses within the targets and allow the Curse Users to become Cursed Children, adapting to their curses and expanding their souls slowly before the Curses could be unsealed. It was difficult to pick suitable bloodlines, and many fell victim to powerful entities subordinate to the Primal. However, after painstaking efforts and some great fortune, the first Curse Users containing and controlling Beast God Curses were born. I started fusing curses with my essence into the bloodline's descendants, allowing the Cursed Children to get used to their curses in their mother's womb. The survival rate was the highest, and I was able to infuse stronger curses as time passed.
Not everyone was suitable, but things were getting better. That was when you arrived. My last prospect, Cleave Fenrir, died miserably. He was arrogant and self-centered, thinking of himself as the strongest entity in the universe even though he still had a long way to go and died long before he could attain what I had planned for him. He was my last failed prospect and the reason I decided to get involved even more in the growth of the next prospect."
Michael swallowed hard, "That's me. I was the next prospect. For…whatever reason."
The input of information was a lot, but Michael tried digesting it all.
"You were the perfect target. I didn't even have to do much. Your personality was great, and you worked hard from the start. The only issue was your gentle nature. Your kindness isn't bad, but I had to ensure you wouldn't fail your task. A soft heart is great, but if you are too soft, you will die miserably. That was my biggest fear. Thus, I got involved. It was necessary." The last words should have angered Michael, but his entire being was void of emotions at this point.
"I still don't understand what your plan is. Why did you need a prospect in the first place? For what reason do you need a prospect? What did you plan to do with me?"
Michael was simply too confused and overwhelmed to feel emotional. That did not make any sense but the myriad of thoughts and words he had to digest made it hard to get angry, feel sad, or to throw a tantrum. "My body is breaking apart. In fact, it has been breaking apart for a while now. I might be the creator of the Origin Expanse, and I am bound to it. Like everything else, it is connected to the weave at some point, but the Origin Expanse has been expanding too fast. It was a slight miscalculation on my side. When I created the Origin Expanse, I failed to establish a perfect connection to the Origin. You know, the weave is still connected to the Origin and countless other entities. However, I am the only one properly connected to the Origin Expanse. That means every Essence, no matter how little, goes through me first. The amount of Essence used to maintain the Expanse is great but both the weave and the Origin Expanse produce more Essence since the beginning of everything. The weave uses this to empower the Primal but also to create more gods, stronger gods. It increases its inhabitants' potential. That is not something I can do with Summons. In the first place, Summons is an asset used to drain the Essence of the Expanse. Every Summon uses a trace of the purest Essence to be resurrected. Unfortunately, that isn't enough to drain everything.
Either way, I was in need of someone born outside the Origin Expanse to bind to the Origin Expanse and become the link between the Origin Expanse and the Origin. You, born in the universe, are naturally connected to the Origin. You are part of the Origin Universe's population. Therefore, you can do what I couldn't. I needed someone to fix my mistake and reconnect the Origin Expanse to the Origin, where it belongs."
"So…what are you planning to do?" Michael asked, still frowning deeply.
"Me? I am going to die. You, on the other hand, will replace me. You will become the Lord of the Origin Expanse. The Supreme Lord, if you want to put it like that!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1073 How Much?
chapters.content:
1073  How Much?
Michael swallowed hard. His world turned upside down, and nothing seemed to make any sense.
"I only have one question…" That was a lie. Michael had numerous questions. In fact, his head was overflowing with them. However, there was only one thing the Will had to answer. If Will wasn't willing to answer or the answer was even more unpleasant than Michael expected, Michael would…do something. He wasn't sure what exactly he would do or what he could do against a being with more amassed Essence than the Primal and all gods together.
"How much did you influence my life?" Michael asked. The question was simple, yet not. Depending on how much the Will intervened in his life, something within Michael may or may not break. The Will knew that but it didn't even do something against Michael when he used Mind Watcher on him. On the contrary, the Will acknowledged and embraced Michael's vigilance. "It's good that you're vigilant, but it is even better for you to know that everything I say is nothing but the truth," The Will commented.
"But to answer your question, I didn't do too much. That doesn't mean I didn't intervene much in your life, but compared to how much I tried creating other prospects, you can be considered a pleasant ride…with the best results I've yet to create," The Will answered, but that wasn't enough for Michael. The Will noticed that and nodded slowly, his pristine white form rippling again and again.
"I created a system to infuse Curses into the respective Cursed Children. I didn't infuse Fenrir into your soul. That was something I didn't do. However, I did get informed about it and decided to insert a trace of my purest Essence into you as a mark. I had to mark you to watch your growth. Since you were suitable enough to become the Holder of Fenrir's curse, I was aware of your potential. You had the potential to grow into a powerful god. Therefore, you, alongside Taros and a few more children, turned into my potential successors. I haven't made a final decision yet, but I've prepared your starting Soultrait Symbols and suitable territories to ignite your growth."
The Will stopped for a moment before continuing.
"I had nothing to do with your actions outside the Origin Expanse, and I never changed the probability of obtaining a Soultrait Symbol, nor did I ever think about influencing you to accept certain Soultrait Symbols. However, I did create the Lord Rift for you and Taros to meet the Librarian. Taros didn't meet the Librarian and focused on the Red Dragon egg instead. That was fine, but I had to intervene again when Masked Saber died to protect you. I had to rescue your brother, otherwise, your gentle nature would have been fully replaced with uncontrollable fury. The Undead Pharaoh, on a side note, wasn't resurrected by me. Your brothers' blood, infused with little curse power, was at fault. He was betrayed by the Blaze Patriarch's underlings, which you have realized a long time ago. I didn't stimulate them to do anything. I did allow the Dragys to enter the Untamed Jungle, which is out of character for their starting territory, to push you closer to the Temple of the Forgotten. After all, it looked like you were neglecting the temple because you were…not scared, but you respected the danger of the temple and your brother's warnings enough to ignore it for a long time. Too long considering what awaited you.
I was also responsible for your encounter with Siegfried. I let you summon him, but not because of the Sacred Knight Temple. No, I needed him to tell you about the danger of possessing Aethyr and that it is dangerous to grow it too quickly because too many powerful beings would be interested in obtaining it. It was a pleasant surprise to find out the Tritan Alliance possessed Aethyr. If not for the Aethyr gifted by the Tritan Alliance, I would have been forced to gift you Aether in a subtle way.
Probably by pushing you to search for your family heirloom. Fenrir's Fang is actually a small fang made of Aether. Cleave Fenrir procured it from an Ancient Ruin, a creation of mine specifically for him, and he gifted it to his daughter before his final battle. The Fang must be somewhere outside the Origin Expanse. Maybe your Aethyr was made from the fang through some coincidence, but I do not know if that is actually the case or not. It doesn't matter either way.
Once Siegfried was there, I found Jormungandr. He'd been trying to enter the Origin Expanse for a while, but I always blocked his access. Only a few beings with Divinities were allowed to enter the Origin Expanse. Their connection to the weave created an instability that was hard to control. However, I needed Hel and Jormungandr at the right spots. They were perfectly suited for you and great teachers. Their wisdom, experience, and powers were all things you needed."
The Will approached Michael slowly, "Other than that, I didn't do anything."
Michael was about to step back but hesitated. Mind Watcher reassured Michael that everything was nothing but the truth. Everything the Will had said was shown through the Will's memories as well. In fact, Michael saw his entire life through the Will's eyes and how 'little' the Will intercepted. There were a few points the Will left out, such as his subtle interception when the Blaze Patriarch and his people decided where they were going to rebuild their territories, but everything was to help Michael. That included when the Miniature Coffin Keychain was created to contain Daniel Fang. The Miniature Coffin Keychain might not have been created for Danny's sake but rather to ensure Michael's personality wouldn't spiral down the wrong path, yet that didn't truly matter. The Will didn't really do anything bad to him.
Michael was glad to have encountered Jormungandr and Hel. He was also happy to have defeated the Supreme Human Alliance.
"You were always strong and hard-working. All I did was push you a little, revealing the opportunities you needed. I never forced you to go down these paths, either. Even though I created them, you choose them!"
The Will said, and Michael knew it was nothing but the truth.
Still, he swallowed hard as the Will stepped closer.
"I also know you want to grow stronger. Strong enough to beat the Primal. I grant you the opportunity as long as you accept the Origin Expanse. If not, the Origin Expanse will implode and cease to exist once I cannot control it anymore."
Michael wanted the Will's power. He needed it.
He swallowed again, but his train of thought slowly shifted.
The corners of his lips tilted upward.

chapters.title: Chapter 1074 Primal
chapters.content:
Chapter 1074  Primal
The whole situation was a little bit too much for Michael and he was clearly overwhelmed with the input of information, but he digested the intel and summarized it in a few simple notes.
The Will was dying and tried creating a successor to fix the only mistake the WIll did when creating the Origin Expanse, and it picked Michael. Michael was a being born in the Origin Universe and thus bound to the Origin. Therefore, he met the requirements and could become the Will's successor. Michael would become the ruler of the Origin Expanse. He wasn't given much time to decide what he wanted but that wasn't necessary. Michael was in dire need of more power. The Will granted him exactly that.
"Don't worry about anything. You are the right choice. I couldn't have hoped for a better successor." The Will said, while stopping right before Michael.
It raised one of its hands slowly, pressing his fingers gently against Michael's forehead. The Will stirred for a moment and Michael flinched. He was about to pull back when he saw something that resembled a smile on the Will's lips.
Was the Will smiling at him? Michael could tell what was happening, yet he couldn't fathom it. Was this really happening to him just now? He shuddered, goosebumps spreading across his arms up to his shoulders and down his back. Michael smiled, but the tension filling his body reflected his true feelings. He was nervous and uncertain of the future.
Still, he didn't retreat further. Michael stood strong and accepted his fate. He embraced it.
"I have watched you for a long time. You might still be young but a young ruler is exactly what the new era needs. They need you," The Will said, but his voice was crumbling. His form rippled and expanded slowly as the pristine Essence holding the Will together spread outward.
The Will's form wasn't stable anymore, but Michael didn't have the luxury to watch the Will dissolve. He was too busy enduring the power that entered his body through the forehead.
The Will's pristine Essence infused into Michael, yet instead of fusing directly into his Energy Vortex of Divinities, the Essence nestled in his War Rune. The War Rune responded by expanding rapidly. It unfolded and transformed. As it unfolded, the Energy Vortex expanded forcefully. The War Rune was too big to be contained by the Energy Vortex, stirring the energy accumulated inside his body to give Michael the final push.
His Energy Vortex roared and expanded, creating a suctioning force to absorb the surrounding Essence. Instead of devouring more pure energy, the Energy Vortex replaced all storages with the Essence flooding him. He devoured the Essence and spread it through his body before integrating it into the expanding Energy Vortex.
Something about Michael changed quickly. His cells burst and were repaired under the constant influx of supreme healing serum and Essence. The pristine Essence fused into every single cell in Michael's body to invigorate them and push them above their designated limit. His cells seemed to mutate and evolve simultaneously, pushing Michael to the next level.
To the level of a proper god. At last, he advanced to the 10th Tier. However, instead of only containing some Essence within his Divinities and energy otherwise as a mortal, who'd attained godhood, Michael's Energy Vortex was filled and overflowing with Essence. Every corner of his body contained much more Essence than his body was supposed to handle. However, instead of crashing down and dying, Michael's body broke apart, only to be healed rapidly.
Several hours, maybe even days or weeks, filled with agony passed. It was horrifying, but Michael smiled through the pain. Every single time his body broke apart, his body regenerated and grew back stronger than he had been. His cells may be filled with Essence now, but that might as well be Michael's greatest advantage. Even without his Divinities, Michael might be stronger than the Primal at this very moment.
The pristine Essence of the Will filled every portion of his existence. It flooded his Soul Sphere, augmenting his Soultraits and upgrading the Soul Power accumulated within the Soultrait Symbols, but that was only the beginning. Far more crucial than the changes to his body, soul, and mind was the new Link that had been established with his War Rune.
The link was an ocean, whereas the Links of Loyalty were droplets of water. There may be billions of Links of Loyalty, but even that was, at most, a bathtub compared to the ocean.
Yet, instead of looking like an actual ocean, the new link was more of a massive pillar of pristine light. It was the Origin Expanse and the link Michael needed to gain access to everything. The pillar was the administration system of the Origin Expanse.
As the Origin Expanse's Pillar took root within his War Rune, Michael felt the changes happening to him. He did not only advance to Tier-10 through the final push of the will but every bit of his existence was filled with Essence now. And it didn't even look like the Essence infused into his body was decreasing. On the contrary, his body absorbed everything like a dry sponge. Meanwhile, the Origin Expanse provided Michael with as much pristine Essence as he could contain. It was almost like the Origin Expanse was eager to find out his limit.
However, there didn't seem to be a limit. His cells changed, his Soultraits improved and transformed as pristine Essence filled every bit of his Soul Sphere and even the Aether within him expanded and transformed. The Pure Aether was growing stronger.
Michael swallowed hard. He'd gained full control of the Origin Expanse and attained godhood. But that was only the beginning. The Links providing Michael with the Soul Power of every being in the Origin Expanse had yet to reach him.
Still, Michael felt stronger than ever.
Essence filled his every action. Even his mind worked faster through the Essence fueling him.
Michael realized something, a chuckle escaping his lips.
He was a Primal.
The first of the new generation at that.

chapters.title: Chapter 1075 Supreme Lord
chapters.content:
Chapter 1075  Supreme Lord
Michael looked down at his body and scanned with Seer and True Vision how much his body had changed. He couldn't see everything, but the things he saw were better than expected. His cells were filled with Essence, which gushed more out of the War Rune. The Origin Expanse provided him with as much Essence as he needed. As for the amount of Essence he would need to finish growing stronger, Michael had no clue.
All Michael could say for certain was that the Essence within him was already enough to rival the Primal.
Yet, the Origin Expanse continued infusing more Essence into him even after he reached the threshold of the other Primal. He was as strong as the Primal at some point. It didn't make any sense to the remaining beings of the universe, and even Michael was having a hard time figuring out what was happening to him, but the answer came to him out of nowhere.
Michael was growing stronger, bit by bit, slowly but steadily. No. It wasn't even that slow. He was growing at a steady pace, surpassing the power he'd sensed from the Primal…and grew truly powerful.
Michael Fang was suddenly stronger than the Primal, given the Essence surging into him. No. He was more than the Primal.
It was shocking, to say the least, but it was also necessary. Michael understood that he needed as much strength as possible. If he didn't grow strong enough, the Primal would regain full control of the Origin Universe, and everything he had worked for would be crushed. Michael did not want that to happen.
The connection to the Origin Expanse opened several doors for him. First, he gained access to the Expanse's Essence. Second, he was not the ruler of the Origin Expanse, and last but not least, the Origin Expanse connected him to every entity of the Origin Expanse. The connection was a lesser version of the Link of Loyalty, but it increased his Soul Power tens of times nonetheless.
Something interesting happened when the Links of Loyalty arrived. It wasn't a sudden motion but a slow but steady process. Hundreds of millions of Links of Loyalty were established every ten seconds, slowly increasing Michael's strength. Once more than a trillion Links of Loyalty had been established with Michael, the Origin Expanse stirred for the first time since the change of ownership.
Michael was prepared for the worst, even though the Origin Expanse would reject him, but it rejoiced instead. The Origin Expanse wiggled in excitement as if it had been restrained and in pain all this time. It was almost like the Origin Expanse regained freedom for the first time since the beginning.
'Maybe the Will's mistake was worse than expected.' Michael wondered while sensing how the Origin Expanse's feelings swept all across its lands. Michael didn't have to be the owner of the Origin Expanse to perceive how happy it was with Michael Fang. That was also what the Origin Expanse shared.
It shared news of the ownership change and urged everyone to welcome their new Almighty God. Michael didn't like the way the Origin Expanse shared the news, but he accepted it regardless. There was nothing he could do about it.
In the first place, it was a lot more helpful to spread his existence and the change of ownership thorough the Origin Expanse. But that was only owed to one of his Soultraits.
Godly Faith responded to the Origin Expanse's outcall. To be precise, beings listening to the Origin Expanse heard the news and discovered something about the owner of the Origin Expanse for the first time…ever. To most creatures of the cosmos, the Will had been an almighty creature. Therefore, the Origin Expanse's choice of words and pictures was well-suited when it introduced him as an Almighty God. He was the strongest being in the Origin Expanse and could do anything. Nobody was even close to strong enough to stop Michael, no matter what he desired to do in the Origin Expanse.
He was almighty.
Those intelligent enough to listen intently to the Origin Expanse realized that. They believed the Origin Expanse's words and had faith in his power. There was no doubt the new owner of the Origin Expanse was powerful enough to expel them if he desired.
This faith and belief was numerous enough to trigger Godly Faith.
Godly Faith strengthened Michael's Essence and his divinity, but it also increased the limit of his physique, mind, and soul. It allowed him to surpass the limits of all living things. Michael could transcend the universe's limits after he had already reached the top. He could grow stronger than any other being in the universe.
The limiter increase was also why Michael was still growing more powerful by the second. It wasn't an immediate increase, but Godly Faith also strengthened all aspects of him by a bit. However, the most important factor was the limiter, which was being tested over and over again by the Expanse's pristine Essence.
As more pristine Essence flooded into him, Michael was growing stronger. Under normal circumstances, Michael would have long since reached his limit. In fact, he wouldn't have grown as powerful as the Primal because he had just ascended to the 10th Tier. But that was not a problem anymore. His body was forced to adapt rapidly when his cells burst and regenerated.
He was already at the peak and still growing stronger. After all, the pristine Essence kept pushing him in an attempt to push his body until it could no more. Until it reached the limit of his existence's potential.
Sensing the billions upon billions of Links of Loyalty and the faith they provided, Michael swallowed hard. It was terrifying to think how much had changed in the last few days, or was it weeks? But at the same time, it was terrific. The corners of his lips tilted into a self-satisfying smile.
The Will was no longer there, and the Origin Expanse accepted him as its new owner. It was exciting.
And so was Michael.
After all, he was the Supreme Lord!

chapters.title: Chapter 1076 Fight the Primal?
chapters.content:
Chapter 1076  Fight the Primal?
Michael was in no rush to fight the Primal. His body was still getting used to the changes, and it would probably take a while to finish everything.
Nonetheless, he told the Rebels to check the Beginning and observe the Primal. If the Primal split up, Michael would attack them, but not before that. Not now, at least.
He left the Will's home in the sky above the Origin Expanse and returned to his territory.
The energy permeating the Untamed Jungle was several times denser than it used to be as an Ancient Region. This didn't surprise Michael as the Origin Expanse's Pillar, the Expanse System, provided Michael with enough intel about everything revolving around the Origin Expanse. Michael was also fully aware of the things he could do with the Expanse System, the Expanse's Essence, and the Origin Expanse. If it was his plan to expel everyone from the Origin Expanse, Michael could do so. That was an easy task. He could also provide his Subordinates with enough Essence to return their Lord Powers. But Michael didn't do that. There was no need to return their Lord Powers. Not at this point, at least.
For now, taking care of the issues ahead was more important. He had to tell the God Curses what he'd learned.
[Talk to us!] Fenrir roared for the Xth time. The Beast God Curse had been tormenting Michael the moment he returned from the Will's office in the sky. He, just like Jormungandr and Hel, wanted to know what had happened.
[I'd appreciate some information as well. You are much stronger than you used to be. Our presence within you is only a fraction of what it used to be, yet it feels like we are growing stronger without doing anything. This Essence…]
"That's the Expanse's Essence. Just like many thought, the Expanse and the weave are two sides of the same coin. The Will ceased to exist. It dispersed shortly after transferring the Origin Expanse's ownership to me."
[That…sounds weird. Does that mean you've replaced the Will? You are the owner of the Origin Expanse now?]
"That's a fat yes to both questions. The Origin Expanse is in my grasp, and so is its Essence. Did you guys know that the Origin Expanse produces as much Essence as the weave?"
[No, but doesn't that mean you have access to far more Essence than all the Primal put together?] Jormungandr asked, to which Michael responded with a glimpse of the Essence that had been infused into his body, followed by his estimation of the Essence his body would consume as long as Godly Faith continued growing.
[Fight the Primal now!] Fenrir roared in excitement when Michael opened his memories to share everything that happened since they were separated by the Will. Apparently, six months had passed since his disappearance, and a few things had happened. News of the new ownership in the Origin Expanse spread far. The rumors spread like wildfire, and it was shocking, to say the least.
Not everyone was surprised about the turn of events, but the majority of Awakened was taken by surprise. Many Awakened didn't even know Michael. After all, he was a human from a faraway place. Almost no one from backwater galaxies and billions of galaxies spread across the cosmos didn't know him, but that was fine. Not everyone had to know Michael. There was no need for that.
Still, news spread like wildfire until they reached the Altors Union, the Thorn Merchandise, whatever remnants of the Supreme Human Alliance, and various other organizations who had considered going against Michael's words when it came to his decision about the Supreme Human Alliance.
They changed their mind quickly, unwilling to go against the new owner of the Origin Expanse. After all, they were still in need of the Origin Expanse. Many beings in the Core, inner region, and even medius zone of the universe could gain access to energy without the Origin Expanse. However, the weave produced less energy thas the Origin Expanse.
One reason for that was that the weave was unwilling to split as much Essences into origin energy as the Origin Expanse. It would much rather create new lifeforms and objects to expand with its Essences, which also included more galaxies, stellar systems, and planets. The Origin Expanse, on the other hand, had always been creating origin energy in the hope of creating powerful Awakened. Awakened powerful enough to solve the Will's problem. That wasn't necessary anymore, but Michael didn't see a reason to stop creating origin energy. He may not be in need of anymore energy, but the Expanse's Essence storage was filled to the brim. There was no reason to stop the Origin Expanse's way of working.
Breaking the system without any reasoning would be foolish. He didn't want to use the Expanse System too often either way, but he would access it if changes or his intervention were needed. Still, he hoped it wouldn't be necessary.
[Don't ignore me and fight the Primal!] Fenrir roared, but Michael clicked his tongue in annoyance as a response.
[There is no need to rush into anything. The Primal are still fighting each other, but it shouldn't take long before they find out about the things that happened in the Origin Expanse. I'm curious how they'll respond to the changes. Will they keep running away in the hope of escaping your iron-tight grasp?] Jormungandr commented
Michael shrugged. "I don't know. But what I know is that I can help you with something.]
[Help us?] Hel asked.
"Yep."
[With what do you want to help us? Our mission has been completed. We helped your soul expand, strengthened you, and installed our Divinities inside your Soul Sphere. I don't think we have anything else to do, especially given your newly acquired powers.] Hel pinpointed the obvious, but Michael only smiled.
"So, you guys want to stay inside me for the rest of your lives? I expected y'all to be more eager to leave my body."
[Leave your body… You mean…] Fenrir forgot about the fight with the Primal.
"Yes, I can break your seals and free you. I'm not sure what will happen with your Divinities because my Divinities are stronger than yours, but there shouldn't be a major issue. After all, I'm not connected to the weave. The Origin Expanse is equivalent to the weave."
[You're willing to do that?]
"Of course. So, how about it?"
[Yes!]
[I would appreciate that.]
[Since you no longer need us, that would be great.]

chapters.title: Chapter 1077 Breaking the Curse
chapters.content:
1077  Breaking the Curse
It was important to note that the three God Curses never lost their physical body. Not even Fenrir's body was taken away and destroyed when he was caught and transformed into a Curse. The bodies were pushed into the Curse's Essence, where they were kept and maintained. Another interesting fact was that the Curses couldn't escape the seal without destroying their bodies. Each Curse had certain conditions to unlock its first seal, but all of them had one thing in common:
They could break out of the Curse if they were willing to cripple their bodies. Fortunately, Fenrir hadn't been pushed this far before encountering Michael, otherwise, the following events would be a little bit more difficult than they had to be.
Michael accessed the Expanse System and searched for the Curses sealed in the void of the Expanse. He saw a handful of God Curses and a lot more lower-ranked Curses but didn't pay too much attention to them at first.
[Can you free them?] Jormungandr asked Michael, pulling him out of the train of thought. Michael thought about it for a moment, his head tilted in uncertainty.
"I know your opinion of the Primal, and I think they're pieces of shit too, but some of the beings sealed in this place don't deserve to be alive. Maybe you won't believe me when I say this but some of the Curses here did things worse than anything the Primal did, excluding two or three incidents maybe. I don't think it would be a good idea to free them. The universe is better off with some of them remaining sealed or dead."
[What about the others?] Fenrir commented.
"I can release them," Michael shrugged, waving his hand to release a surge of pristine Essence. The Essence filled the void in the Expanse to infuse into the Curses, who regained their form slowly. Michael tapped into Slipstream, which – just like his other Soultrait Symbols – felt more like a Divinity since his Soultraits had been infused with pristine Essence and created enough portals to release the Curses who regained their shape. They were brought back to where they came from. At last, the Curses regained freedom. Some were mortals who attained godhood a long time ago, but most gods forced into Curses were born as gods. They didn't have much of a family, let alone brethren, to return to. Still, everyone was happy about the return to the weave.
Of course, that excluded the Curses, whom Michael didn't give a second chance. Some people did not deserve a second chance.
[What if I check on them? Once I have my body back, I can check on all of them and make sure they will never commit the same heinous massacres they've committed in the past.] Jormungandr suggested, which attracted Michael's attention. Michael was about to start dissolving his connection with the God Curses to return them to the void where it was the easiest to remove the seals, but he stopped at Jormungandr's commentary.
"Someone you hold dear is still sealed in here." He figured.
[I…wouldn't say I hold them dear.]
'Multiple?!' Michael nearly burst out, but he held back, his mind isolated from the God Curses since pristine Essence filled every part of his body.
Silence filled the void, and Michael's mind was filled with no more comments from the World Serpent. It remained silent, unwilling to go into detail.
[Jormungandr's children are still here. It is complicated.] Fenrir broke the silence. Michael was surprised but he didn't have time to ask anymore questions. Jormungandr cursed his brother and hissed at him, telling Fenrir he would tear him apart once they were out of there.
"Your children are here?" Michael asked, but Jormungandr still couldn't answer.
He sighed but decided to give the World Serpent the benefit of the doubt. Since Jormungandr had been on his side, protecting and enhancing him wherever he could, Michael wasn't going to betray him. They were friends. Some would even say they were closer than family. They were part of each other, even if that would only last for a few minutes.
"It would be unfair to free only your children. Maybe nobody would say anything, but I don't want to be known as a biased ruler. Either I'll free all of them or none. And IF I free everyone, you will have to carry the responsibility for the actions of everyone I'm freeing. Do you know what that means?" Michael asked Jormungandr in a dead-serious tone.
[I do know. I also know what it means to free them. They…No, I. I failed raising them well. They were born gods and considered themselves better than anyone. They killed too many gods and devoured entire civilizations. I know what I'm asking from you. Especially given their tremendous strength. But I wish to set them free and give them a second chance.] Jormungandr commented. He hesitated for a moment and added.
[Give me a second chance. I want to be a better father.]
Michael nodded, but his expression remained dead serious, "As you wish. I hope this doesn't turn out to be a grave mistake."
[Me too.]
[Can we start now] Fenrir commented impatiently while Hel reminded him.
[Calm down, will you? I think you can wait a little longer!]
Michael chuckled while Fenrir winced, but he jumped into action after that.
He closed his eyes and gathered his pristine Essence to remove the most vital points connecting him to the God Curses. This was easier said than done and consumed more Essence than most Major Gods could control at a time. But Michael handled the pristine Essence fairly easily.
Still, the pain of slowly removing the God Curses was painful. Not only physically but also mentally. The God Curses' voices in his head dimmed slowly as the connection died down and a somber feeling replaced the emptiness in his head.
But then again, Michael felt free for the first time since he awakened Fenrir. No. Even before that. Fenrir had always been inside Michael. He had been there since birth. While that also meant Michael and Fenrir were closer than the others, it also indicated that Michael had never been truly alone. He had never been himself.
Not entirely, at least.
That would change now.
Michael severed his connection with the God Curses, freeing not only the siblings but also himself.

chapters.title: Chapter 1078 Freedom
chapters.content:
1078  Freedom
Fenrir, the great wolf of the Origin Universe, returned. He was still in the void where he had been sealed by the Primal and the Will's help, but the fearsome and awe-inspiring appearance returned to the surface of the universe for the first time in eons. Fenrir was massive, towering over men and beasts alike. His body was so large that he seemed to darken the sky when he moved. Of course, there was no sun—or sky, for the records—in the void, but Michael imagined Fenrir traveling across the cosmos, his body covering the sun. He had thick, wild fur that was as black as the night, with streaks of silver running through like flashes of lightning in a raging storm. His fur coat was rough and untamed, bristling along his spine. It rippled with vigor, golden bolts bursting out of them as the excitement within the great wolf increased.
His legs were also thick and powerful, muscles rippling under his fur, almost like they had been moved and refined for the eons of confinement. His claws were also a threatening sight. They were long and sharp, digging through the fabric of the void, which had isolated him from the cosmos for longer than he could remember. He left crushing prints as he stepped through the void, attracting Michael's interest.
'Is he using the Power of Extraction to weaken the void's fabric?' He wondered while continuing to study the wolf.
Fenrir's eyes glowed with an eerie, fiery light, a deep red that burned like molten lava. The eyes were full of fury and intellect, always watching the surroundings as if afraid to encounter the Primal again and to be confined once more. However, the fury in his eyes showed Michael also that Fenrir was willing to fight the Primal head-on again. He was ready to fight them once more to determine the final victor. However, this time, Fenrir wasn't alone. Fenrir's eyes gave him a terrifying, almost unnatural presence. His mouth was enormous, filled with sharp, jagged teeth that looked like tiny mountains. They were capable of tearing through anything in his path. Michael didn't doubt the legend of Fenrir being strong enough to swallow the sky itself.
However, Fenrir wasn't the only one with a big mouth. Well, the wolf was the biggest chatterbox among the gods Michael had met until now, but he meant it like that. Jormungandr's mouth was at least as big as his brother's.
Instead of releasing one God Curse after another, Michael simultaneously released Fenrir, Jormungandr, and Hel. However, Jormungandr was probably the most impressive. He was the thickest and longest, after all
Jormungandr was as fearsome as Fenrir, but it was far more monstrous, capable of circling entire worlds with its massive body. His body was covered in thick, scaly armor, with each scale shimmering in a mix of dark green and black, like the depths of the sea. These scales were as tough as void iron, and they made the sound of metal scraping when he moved. Jormungandr's size was beyond imagination. Michael had seen a portion of the World Serpent's size before, but it was only a portion. Michael had yet to see the true extent of Jormungandr's body. Today was the day. The day Michael saw how massive the World Serpent was.
His length stretched from horizon to horizon, the massive body twisting and curling in endless loops. The void was endless, yet it looked like Jormungandr was just as endless. Michael swallowed at that. Jormungandr's head was also gigantic, with a wide, flat skull that looked ancient and powerful like it had seen the Laws of the universe change over countless ages. The World Serpent's eyes were cold and glowing, a fierce yellow like a pair of burning suns, filled with deep ancient wisdom and dangerous, watchful hunger.
Jormungandr's fangs were long and sharp, curving down like deadly hooks. Venom dripped down the fangs, potent enough to tear through the fabric in the void. The World Serpent's maw was wide and terrifying, capable of swallowing entire continents in a single go. The earth would tremble whenever it opened its mouth, and Michael could see faint crackling in the fabric around Jormungandr as he slithered around.
It was no surprise the Primal had been hunting Jormungandr. The World Serpent was terrifying. If Michael didn't know better, he would consider Jormungandr on the same level as the Primal. Unfortunately, the Primal had more access to Essence. If not for that, the World Serpent may actually be as strong as Primal Xerx had been.
Michael was unsure whether Jormungandr or Fenrir had been stronger in the past, but given Fenrir's confinement as a Curse, it was clear who was stronger now. Jormungandr had grown stronger while Fenrir stagnated. But it was interesting to note that the difference in power between them wasn't high. It was smaller than expected.
Hel was not much different. She was the goddess of the underworld and acquired the authority of Death upon birth, yet she was not much stronger than her siblings. The only thing she was better at was using her techniques. She could probably defeat her siblings as long as enough people around her died to replenish Death Essence.
Just like before, Hel had two sides. Her living side, with pale but smooth skin. She looked coldly at Michael, but her ghostly beauty overshadowed everything. Her hair fell loosely to the ground, shadowy waves swirling around her shoulders. Her eyes on the living side was sharp and pierced deep into Michael as if she could see through his soul. She wore a dark, flowing robe draped over her body, made from materials that seemed almost like shadows, blending with the gloom of the underworld realm. But actually, her clothes were made from Undead Souls and Wraiths. Michael noticed that immediately.
The dress covered most of her dead side as well. However, it was still easy to see the stark contrast between the living and the dead side. Her skin on the dead side was withered and gray and tightly strapped against her bones. It was almost like she was about to become a skeleton. In some sports her flesh was rotting, decaying like the body of a deceased.
Still, Michael didn't budge. He smiled at Hel and greeted her friendly.
"Looks like nothing changed."
[Nothing about me has changed, indeed.] Hel pointed out casually, [But you have changed.]
Michael nodded. That was true. He had changed. Quite a lot at that.

chapters.title: Chapter 1079 Hel's...Love
chapters.content:
1079  Hel's...Love
Watching Fenrir was interesting. The great wolf was excited like a little puppy and showed that quite clearly. He jumped through the Slipstream portal the moment it opened and traveled across the planetary systems like he had never seen them. In fact, that might be true. Fenrir had been sealed so long, he must have missed the creation of countless galaxies.
But while Michael let Fenrir play around, Jormungandr and Hel waited patiently. To be precise, Hel was the only patient one, whereas Jormungandr couldn't wait to reunite with his children. Michael released the seals on the other Curses via the Expanse System and observed the return of more than a dozen Beast Gods. He sighed, deeply looking at a crimson and an ocean-blue serpent, and glanced at Jormungandr. The serpents looked around, and one of them charged at a nearby dragon. The Calamity Dragon, a black dragon with enough Essence to trample the serpents, was their target. Their fangs were about to tear into the Calamity Dragon as it regained its composure – it had been sealed away the longest – but Michael was faster.
He conjured two Imperial Barriers right before the serpents. Their snouts crashed into the Imperia Barriers and were nearly crushed if Michael hadn't weakened the Imperial Barriers after a second.
The serpent duo hissed in pain while the Calamity Dragon's head flicked to them. The Calamity Dragon's pitch-black eyes flickered eerily, and it gathered void flames in its maw, ready to kill the serpents without hesitation.
"I know you're angry, but how about you leave them alive? Consider it as good advice from someone who has given you a second chance at life." Michael commented lightly when he teleported in front of the Calamity Dragon.
"Who are you, puny creature? Why do you smell like the Will?" The Calamity Dragon's hoarse voice roared through the void.
"The Will is no more. I took on his job. That's why you're free now."
"What if I never wanted to be freed?" Michael shrugged. He didn't care.
"I can seal you again. I couldn't care less about you. If you don't want to stay alive, I might as well kill you."
The Calamity Dragon released the void flames upon Michael, who devoured them with the Wolf Divinity. His Divinities were still as strong as before. Even if the God Curses weren't with him anymore, their powers certainly were. In fact, he was stronger than ever, given the pristine Essence fueling the Wolf Divinity.
The void flames dispersed as Michael consumed the power of the void within them. He stored them in the storage he'd recreated when he decided to return the World Serpent's freedom.
Maybe the Void was going to be useful in the fight with the Primal.
"I know what you've done and that you deserve to be sealed in here. However, I also know that the eons must have been hard on you. You were sealed in the void not even a thousand years after the Massacre of the Beginning. The Primal must have been harsh on you and your beloved. Still, you are alive. Don't you seek revenge?" The Calamity Dragon roared.
"I don't care about the Primal."
Michael raised an eyebrow, "What do you care about then?"
"I don't care about anything! All I want is the calamity!" The Calamity Dragon roared.
A heavy sigh escaped Michael's lips, and he considered killing the Calamity Dragon on the spot. That would certainly be less annoying and time-consuming than leaving the Calamity Dragon alive. However, Hel stopped him.
"Can I take him?" Hel asked, a tinge of interest flashing through her eyes. "What do you want to do with him?" "Tame him, or something like that," Hel shrugged, "He is a challenge, and I like challenges."
Michael was unsure what to think about that, but he kept his lips sealed when Hel added,
"He is rather cute as well. I like his presence."
Michael's lips parted, but he shut them after a second. It might be better to keep his mouth shut before he would utter something stupid. But seriously? She fell in love with the Calamity Dragon? Or was she only interesting? One way or another…this promised to be interesting.
"Take care of him if you think you can handle him. If he does something stupid, beat him up. Tell me if he is too strong for you to handle. I will sever a limb or two and only regrow when he behaves properly," Michael responded.
Hel smiled at Michael, but it wasn't a kind smile. Quite the contrary, he felt Mel's smile was devious and sadistic. Somehow, he pitied the Calamity Dragon, who didn'T seem to realize what was happening.
"I'm not some sort of pet. Fuck off!" He roared, but Hel had already indicated to him to create a Slipstream portal. Death gushed from Hel, pushing the Calamity Dragon out of the void. "That was weird," Michael murmured, turning to the other Beast Gods.
"I don't really have a lot to say. I'm giving you a second chance because Jormungandr asked me to. I don't believe everyone has changed for the better, but I surely hope there won't be a need for me to meet you guys again. Please behave properly, and don't start annihilating entire planetary systems and civilizations again. Not without reason, at least."
Michael shrugged, "Do as you please but don't stir any trouble. I don't like trouble!"
He would be busy with the Primal and couldn't afford to mess with the Beast Gods. Most Beast Gods didn't say anything and disappeared through the Slipstream portals that appeared near them, but Jormungandr's children stayed behind. They hissed at Michael and were ready to attack until the World Serpent intervened with his Power Authority. He crushed the presence of the two massive serpents and roared at them, unleashing the myriad of emotions he had been accumulating for who knows how long.
Impressive.
Michael watched the serpents for a while but decided to let them be after throwing them into a massive Slipstream portal. He hurled it at the serpents and shoved them into a near-empty planetary system filled with dead stars. Jormungandr's lectures could start there, where they could inflict the least damage.
"Now that this is done…let's take care of the factories."

chapters.title: Chapter 1080
chapters.content:
Even though Michael did everything he could to grow as strong as possible, he was nervous. Only one fight separated Michael from changing the universe forever. It was weird to think about it that way, but that was exactly what the current situation was. Michael would fight the Primal soon, and by defeating them, he would change the universe forever.
Michael sighed deeply and searched for some distraction. A few minutes of distraction would be more than enough for him.
That being said, Michael visited the factories working on the Anti-Blood-I serum. Billions of potions had already been prepared, but that was only a fraction of the serum needed to cleanse the Supreme Human Alliance from Blood Incursion once and for all.
Michael traveled through the factories and studied the faces of the employees. Everyone worked hard on the Anti-Blood-I serum. The employees' faces were filled with strain, which was given since the workload was too much for anyone to handle, but nobody complained. Their help was needed to rescue dozens of human races from the remnants of the Supreme Human Alliance.
If not for them, the remnants of the Supreme Human Alliance would surely feast on the human races, devouring them slowly and steadily.
"Why did I know you would be here?" A familiar voice rang from the right, and Michael turned around to greet Alice with a tight embrace. He took a deep breath and smiled at the woman whom he loved dearly. His love for Alice was greater than his desire for power and the addiction power provided. He loved Alice more than anything. However, that was also why he had to grow stronger. She was the reason Michael had to go through all of this—not directly, of course. Nonetheless, Michael felt the need to acquire more power to defeat the Primal and protect Alice and everyone else he loved. There was no time to waste, either.
"The Primal will soon stop fighting. It looks like they're slowly getting used to each other's fighting style," Michael said even before Alice could ask anything. His voice was quiet but filled with confidence. He wasn't afraid of the fight ahead, yet the nervousness filling his entire being contradicted this sensation.
Was it possible to be incredibly nervous without feeling any fear? Michael told himself that it had to be this way. After all, he wasn't afraid of fighting the Primal. Right?
"Everything will be fine. You are not alone. You have the Rebels by your side and can ask everyone else for help. The fight against the Primal is not only yours. It's everyone's fight. That's simple, isn't it?" Alice chuckled, patting him gently on the back.
She looked at him with pure love and kissed him on the cheek.
"All you have to do if you need help is to ask. Reach out with your hand and accept everyone's help. There is no need to be afraid of help. You can be nervous, afraid even. But you should never think of your fight against the Primal as something you have to carry alone. This is a responsibility the whole universe has to carry. Together!"
Michael released Alice from the tight embrace and kissed her on the lips.
"I love you. You know that, right?"
"Of course, idiot~" Alice chuckled.
"And you know you're a genius, ain't you?" Michael smiled vibrantly at Alice, but she merely shrugged.
"My parents considered Kaleb as the genius in our family. I was always excellent, but Kaleb was the golden goose."
Michael chuckled.
"Is that so? I think you're much better than Kaleb," He laughed and kissed Alice again, "But I'll have to go now. I have an idea!"
Alice hugged Michael once more after saying a few words. She released her lover after that and watched him disappear as he teleported somewhere outside the Origin Expanse.
"You will be fine. You can do it!"
**
"You want WHAT from us?!" One of the present Titan Gods asked Michael, his thunderous voice reverberating across the massive plateau.
Michael had created the plateau with some of the Expanse System's help to show the present Gods and Beast Gods that he planned to treat them nicely.
He had gathered all Beast Gods, Major Gods, Minor Gods, Demi Gods, Rebels, and many more beings with some sort of connection to the weave – and enough Essence to be of help – to ask them for a favor.
"Not everyone present wants to defeat, let alone kill, the Primal, but I am here to ask you for a little favor. If you don't want to listen to it or dislike the idea of going against the Primal, so be it. But let me say one thing…" Michael cleared his throat, his voice is as heavy as the weave.
"I will fight the Primal today and defeat them whether you help me or not."
**

chapters.title: Chapter 1081 Agreed
chapters.content:
1081  Agreed
"If you can defeat the Primal without us, why are you asking us for a favor? Doesn't that mean you need our help to defeat them?"
Michael shook his head. "While it is true that I want, maybe even need, your help, it's not for my sake."
"You need our help for…our sake?" One of the present Beast Gods asked, his frustration rising rapidly.
"Exactly," Michael nodded and raised his hand to stop the present Gods, Beast Gods, and other beings before they could say anything.
"How much of the universe will be destroyed when the six of the strongest entities of the weave fight the Supreme Lord and owner of the Origin Expanse? How many galaxies will fall victim to our fight? How many races will our Essence annihilate by accident? A single astray attack can destroy entire planetary systems." Michael's words were heavy, but they had to be said. He had to speak them aloud.
"How much of the universe do you want to sacrifice for the final battle?" Michael asked everyone present.
Nobody answered. Not even the Titan God, who'd thundered earlier like he had the power to speak up for himself, dared to utter a single sound.
"I can bring everyone I love to the Origin Expanse. In fact, I've reorganized the Realms of the Exiled Races to create an entire planetary system for the Tritan Alliance, the Nest, and the Thorn Merchandise. I don't care if you know these organizations and alliances. Just know that those I protect are nowhere near the battlefield. As for the rest of the universe…"
Michael shrugged.
Jormungandr looked at Michael but didn't say anything. Michael had already offered the World Serpent, Loki, Fenrir, and Hel to bring them into the void of the Expanse for a few days, weeks, or as long as his fight with the Primal would last, but they had rejected. They didn't regain freedom, only to keep running away from the Primal. They lusted for a final battle with the Primal. A head-on fight.
"What do you want?" One of the Beast Gods controlling the Bestikal Galaxies asked. It was a long-winded dragon with five claws. The dragon was silver, just like Eren's dragon curse had been. Thinking about Eren, Michael smiled lightly.
'This guy reminds me of Eren. Where the hell is that guy in the first place?' Michael shrugged inwardly while everyone else waited for him to proceed and answer the question.
"I don't want anything special from all of you. All I need is your full concentration and Essence for as long as the battle with the Primal lasts," Michael said in a matter-of-fact tone. The Gods and other beings stared at him for a while, but Michael had already answered.
A full minute of silence passed before the first Gods murmured and cursed Michael. Still, he didn't say anything and let the tension grow until Loki answered.
"You want us to use the Weave Seal again?" Loki asked, which Michael affirmed with a nod.
"That's the point, but not exactly. I hope you guys can create a Weave seal from the outside of the Beginning. The entire galaxy is already destroyed and won't take anymore damage from my fight with the Primal. That said, I want everyone present to create an arena where I'll fight the Primal. If they kill me, so be it." Michael shrugged.
He doubted the Primal were strong enough to kill him now that he owned the Origin Expanse, but miracles happened often enough. Michael knew that well enough.
"From the outside? So…you don't want us to become the Primal's targets but still hope we can keep the Primal in the Beginning." Loki murmured but it was Jormungandr who shook his head, "The Weave Seal is too strong and complicated to be used on an entire galaxy, especially if the pillars of the seal – aka everyone present other than you – is outside the Weave Seal.
