Furthermore, the Primal will try to break out. We cannot block them like that if you want us to transform the Beginning into an isolated galaxy severed from the weave."
Michael nodded. If one or two Primal focused on blocking his attacks, the remaining Primal could try and break out to regain access to the weave.
"I understand that point. That's why I hope you can restrain their movements and block them from escaping the Beginning. It would be best if you can sever their connection to the weave as well, but if you cannot do that…" Again, Michael hinted at a shrug. "I don't think we can seal the Beginning completely. However, since most of us are present…I think we can restrain the flow of the Weave's Essence entering the Beginning for a while. At the same time, Sleipnir, Fenrir, Jormungandr, the Calamity Dragon, Hel, and a handful of Major Gods will block the Primals if they're trying to run. We can intercept their fissures and stall them if they try to escape the Beginning," Hel pointed out, ignoring the Calamity Dragon's anger and frustration.
However, hearing that it could fight and possibly tear the Primal apart, it didn't say anything. "Is that enough?" Hel asked, her rotting eyeball flicking to the Calamity Dragon for a second before her attention returned to Michael.
"That should be more than enough. We won't even need the Weave Seal if everyone helps."
The neutral Gods weren't pleased with Michael's plan, but the idea of letting the six Primal and Michael fight across the entire universe was even worse. Michael wouldn't hold back because there was no need to. Everyone he loved was somewhere secure in the Origin Expanse. That being said, the Primal didn't have to hold back either. On the contrary, they would go above and beyond to kill Michael and regain their seat at the top of the Origin Universe.
Even if the Gods, who had yet to pick a side, didn't favor Michael over the Primal…Michael was the one who offered them a solution to the upcoming problems. By containing the Primal within the Beginning, the rest of the universe would be protected.
Maybe that meant they would have to pick a side, but at least Michael warned them about what was going to happen. The Primal never cared about them. If anything, they restrained everyone's freedom and killed the unpolished gems they feared.
If it was necessary to replace one evil with another, the neutral gods would much rather pick Michael.
He might not be the greatest ruler, but he would certainly be better than the Primal.
Someone new was needed at the top.
"We agree."

chapters.title: Chapter 1082 The End of the Beginning I
chapters.content:
1082  The End of the Beginning I
Everything was set in stone – or the fabric of space and reality – in no time. The Gods went into position and accessed the weave, actively draining it to pull the streams of Essence around the Beginning in different directions.
The streams of Essence weren't severed, nor did anyone remove the Beginning from the weave. Instead, hundreds of Gods – Beast Gods, Major Gods, Minor Gods, and Demi Gods – controlled the Essence under tremendous pressure and pushed it toward the Gods who had been chosen as 'Fortress Guards.'
These Guards were deployed around the Beginning to block the Primal with their comrades' supply of Essence. The Essence filled the Guards to the brim and let them overflow. In some cases, that would have been considered problematic, but the Guards would need every bit of Essence once the Primal attacked them.
In the meantime, their allies used some of the excessive Essence, which would have filled the Beginning under normal circumstances, to use an altered version of the Weave Seal. They didn't cut the Beginning out of the weave but used the altered version to disrupt potential manifestations of fissures and most other spatial movements. Even Slipstream would consume a lot more Essence than the energy it had consumed in Michael's fight against Primal Xerx. However, that was within Michael's calculations. He was already prepared for the increased expenses for any spatial movements. The Primal stopped fighting when the weave rippled. The arrival of dozens of gods attracted their attention. However, it was only when more than one hundred gods circled the Beginning that they did something. One of the Primal tried opening a fissure to leave the place when he discovered Sleipnir and his siblings – it was the chubby Primal who'd been fighting Sleipnir head-on.
He didn't lose against Sleipnir and would have won against him if they'd fought a little longer, but Sleipnir's arrival with his siblings meant something had gone wrong. After all, Hel, Fenrir, and Jormungandr weren't supposed to be alive at this point. They were supposed to be Curses and fused with Michael.
But here they were, their appearances stable and not the slightest sign of curse power left within them. It was almost like Loki's children had never been the God Curses of Michael.
The chubby Primal, Gluvos, had a bad feeling and tried to leave, but Loki and more than a dozen other Major Gods interrupted him. They tapped into the weave's Essence and blocked the disruption of the Beginning's fabric, destroying the Primal's tactic of using fissures to move across the cosmos. In a fit of rage, Gluvos released a series of bullets made from Essence to attack Loki, but Sleipnir and his siblings destroyed them.
Loki's children spread out, their attention lingering on Gluvos. The Calamity Dragon was somewhere nearby, but his attention lingered on Primal Kytos. Kytos was slightly skinnier than Gluvos, but the Calamity Dragon's fury lingered on him. Kytos was the last Primal the Calamity Dragon saw before he was sealed in the Expanse's void. He was the first who'd receive a taste of his power now that he was back in the Origin Universe.
The other Primal looked around, their bodies coated in Essence. Weapons made from Essence formed around them, and the corners of their lips curled upward. However, they didn't look overly happy with the situation. The tension spreading through the Beginning was palpable.
"Everyone has betrayed us," One of them murmured.
"Even the cowards picked a side at last?" The second added.
"But they've picked the wrong side. That was a stupid mistake. A grave mistake." A third thundered, only for the fourth to spit out,
"Can't we just kill them all? Who cares whether the weave will change. These bastards are getting on my nerves," Kytos bellowed.
"No. We cannot kill everyone. But we can eliminate the most annoying children of the weave. There is no need for some of them to stay alive. We accepted their existence for long enough." Gluvos transformed into a flash as his words reverberated throughout the Beginning, and he appeared before Loki. He moved faster than before, after consuming a considerable amount of his Essence to push his acceleration and top speed to the limits, and was about to pierce Loki's chest when hundreds of paper-thin barriers conjured before him.
His attack was already full in motion, his right hand transformed into a razor-sharp blade sharp enough to cut through the fabric of time and space. But even that wasn't enough to cut through hundreds of Imperial Barriers.
Each Imperial Barrier was conjured with pristine Essence, unraveling the true potential of the 10-Star Soultrait and the Soul Power each of his Soultraits had accumulated at this point.
The Essence Blade pierced through a few dozen Imperial Barriers before it slowed down, forcing Gluvos to disperse the blade and transform into a flash again. If not for his quick reaction, Loki's children would have reached Gluvos, hitting him with a myriad of Laws and Authorities.
Even though Gluvos wasn't too worried about the impact of the siblings' attacks, he perceived the scarcity of the weave's Essence in the surroundings. Something was happening to the Beginning, and it wasn't good for him and the other Primal.
Someone with the power of a Primal attracted the attention from the corner of his eyes. Gluvos turned to the figure, his eyes narrowing to tiny slits when he realized who had appeared in the beginning.
"Shouldn't you be more worried about your safety? I don't think you're strong enough to kill anyone present with that kind of power," The familiar man chuckled. He smiled at Gluvos, but it wasn't a generous or kind smile. The smile on the man's lips was devious. It was overflowing with emotions like hatred and wrath, yet at the same time, it was void of any emotions.
Gluvos shuddered and returned to the other Primal, but everyone was looking at the newcomer. Everyone looked at Michael as if their eyes and full attention were drawn to him.
Michael's devious smile widened as he stepped forward, the pristine Essence of the Origin Expanse oozing out of him. For the first time since the separation of the weave and the expanse, the Essence of the Origin reunited.
It collided and ignited sparks in the fabric of space and reality, which looked like the fabric of the universe bent around Michael. It almost looked like the universe bent to Michael's will as he strode toward the Primal, his gait overflowing with confidence.
"Our safety?" Kytos snorted, "You're the one dying today!" The Primal's rang through the surroundings but it sounded like an empty threat to Michael, who disappeared before the Primal's eyes. He reappeared in their midst and unleashed the pristine Essence he had gathered in his chest.
The Essence burst out of him in all directions and swept the Primal away. Their eyes widened in surprise at the power gushing from Michael. Yet, even though they could have reacted, the Primal didn't do anything. They were hurled halfway across the Beginning and thus separated even before they could react to Michael's attack.

chapters.title: Chapter 1083 The End of the Beginning II
chapters.content:
1083  The End of the Beginning II
The Primal were forcefully separated, their bodies flung through the galaxy. The Calamity Dragon ignored everything they'd decided earlier and attacked Kytos. Mythical void flames burned Kytos, forcing the Primal to respond with a wave of Essences. The void flames reached the Essence and tore it apart. It wasn't fast or anything, but the void flames were strong enough to inflict some damage.
Kytos appeared next to the Calamity Dragon's head with a massive Zweihänder in his hands. The Zweihänder cleaved down and cut deep into the Calamity Dragon's cheek. Interestingly enough, the Essence Zweihänder wasn't strong enough to sever the dragon's head, let alone to chip his skull. On the contrary, the Calamity Dragon responded with void flames gushing out of its cheeks. The flames melt the Essence Zweihänder, forcing Kytos to change his tactic.
He jumped from the Calamity Dragon's head and conjured a pair of Essence Daggers in his hands instead. He pierced the daggers into the dragon's neck, using more Essence to push his body downward. The injury inflicted on the Calamity Dragon wasn't small. It was a lengthy cut that would take weeks to heal. After all, injuries inflicted through a Primal's Essence couldn't be healed so easily. Either you had to remove the Essence lingering in the wound or use a similarly powerful or stronger Essence to wash it out.
Michael did just that. He released a bullet made of supreme healing serum, which he'd conjured through his pristine Essence, and hurled it at the Calamity Dragon. The Calamity Dragon may not be like Michael, but it nonetheless accepted the supreme healing serum.
Michael observed the other Primal and nodded slowly. No one dared to attack him head-on. They were too afraid to become his main target. At least after realizing how much stronger Michael had actually grown.
His attention was drawn toward something in the wide-open space, and he frowned. The weave tried to attract his attention. It was an invisible pulling force, but Michael could instinctively tell where it came from. The weave was doing something. It tried telling him something.
However, Michael wasn't given the luxury of paying much attention to the weave. His focus returned to the remaining five Primal, whereas Kytos fought the Calamity Dragon.
The Primal didn't move one moment, yet they appeared around him in the next second with several Essence Storms brewing around them. They unleashed their Essences in an attempt to suppress Michael and attacked him with countless projectiles. First, Essence Spears and throwing knives came his way. However, it didn't take long before the throwing knives were replaced by Essence Bullets and the Essence Spears with massive blades.
Michael mantled his body in gold. He used the Wolf Divinity to extract the Essence within their attacks and forcefully annexed it by fusing the Essence with his pristine Essence. Michael ignored the sparks and distortion in the fabric around the forcefully merged Essences and conjured lightning bolts made of pure Essence instead.
The lightning bolts zapped through the Beginning and struck three out of five Primal in the back before dispersing. It didn't look like the bolts had inflicted any damage, but the opposite was the case. The lightning bolts inflicted a lot more damage than Michael had hoped for.
'Fusing the Expanse's Essence with the Weave's Essence seems to create an even more potent Essence. That's good. It makes sense as well. The weave and the expanse are part of the same: They were once one and the same and were forcefully separated. It is no wonder they work well together.' Michael concluded, his expression easing up even though the speed at which he got attacked increased drastically.
Michael had a hard time evading all attacks. However, Michael gained a minuscule advantage by devouring bits and pieces of the Primal's Essence through their projectiles and fusing it with his own Essence. He used the merged Essence via the Galaxy of Elements to conjure wind and fire simultaneously.
The wind and fire coated him, pushing him through the space much faster than he could move through the wide-open space under normal circumstances. Of course, Michael never stopped channeling pristine Essence through his body to move through space. However, he added the fire-attributed Essence and the wind-attributed Essence to accelerate.
The boost was exactly what Michael needed to evade most incoming attacks. Some Essence Blades and Bullets struck him, a few Essence Blades even exploded the instance they touched him, but the damage was not too great. The exploding blades were blocked by a few Imperial Barriers, which Michael operated instinctively. Only a minuscule amount of mental power was needed to call upon his Soultraits. He could bend them as he desired and use their powers to the limits.
The Primal could do something similar. However, their access to these powers was not that simple. The Primal could do the same as Michael, but they weren't capable of doing it as easily as Michael. Galaxy of Elements granted him full access to all Elements in the cosmos. The Primal had the same access, but they had to go down a far more complicated path to conjure a blazing inferno than Michael.
That didn't mean it was difficult for them. It was just that the time and effort needed weren't worth it for the Primal. For Michael, on the other hand, it was simple. And he would certainly make use of every little advantage he held over the others. He didn't have more than a dozen Soultrait Symbols, Pure Aether, four Divinities, pristine Essence, and billions upon billions of Links of Loyalty for no reason.
He would make use of everything until the Primal were defeated.
"Is that all?" Michael laughed into the wide-open space, silver liquid gushing from his body as the Primal combined their forces to injure him. He was healing rapidly, but that was not what the silver liquid was there for. The liquid wasn't healing serum, after all.
No. it was the Pure Aether Michael had amassed.
It coiled around his arms and legs like a silver serpent, engulfed his chest, and covered his head tightly. Only his vibrantly glowing golden eyes were left unprotected.
After all, the Primal had to look into the eyes of the man who was going to kill them!

chapters.title: Chapter 1084 The End of the Beginning III
chapters.content:
1084  The End of the Beginning III
The Pure Aether armor fused into Michael's body while shrouding him tightly. Michael infused pristine Essence into the armor and did the same as two lengthy sabers made from Pure Aether formed in his hands. But just like in his last fight with a Primal, Michael wasn't done here. First, he infused the Power of Extraction, the Law of Poison, and Death onto the Pure Aether Sabers before adding the Power Authority on the Pure Aether armor and sabers.
Once that was done, Michael could activate Unlimited Enhancement to push his body and the Pure Aether to their limits and beyond. Michael severed Gluvos' arm, who was forced to catch the arm before cutting a portion of his shoulder and arm to start the regeneration and reattachment process. The Pure Aether weapons were now strong enough to pierce deep into the Primal, leaving permanent marks that had to be cut out alongside the Essence around it to avoid complications in the future.
Michael took advantage of that when he severed Gluvos' arm, and he continued doing so by inflicting a myriad of smaller injuries. The smallest scratches didn't cause a commotion, but every wound inflicted with Pure Aether pained the Primal. It showed them that they weren't invincible and that their lives could end with a few precise hits.
One mistake and everything would be over.
That fact was far worse than some measly scratches. It was enough for deep-rooted fear to blossom in the Primal's hearts of essences.
Michael had to endure a wild series of attacks as well. He wasn't the only one dealing damage. However, his damage was more consistent and lasted much longer. The Primal used similar attacks as Michael, but they relied on destructive Essence attacks to inflict as much damage as possible, hoping to decimate the Essence at his disposal. Unfortunately, Michael healed way too fast. Most of the time, he didn't even use the healing serum he'd created with Essence. There were still some leftovers of the Essence he'd created as a Demi God. They were potent enough to tend to most of his wounds.
Michael continued using Unlimited Enhancement even though it drained his lifeforce rapidly. He replaced some lifeforce with pristine Essence, which drained his Essence reserves, but it wasn't like he lacked Essence. The Primal bled more Essence than Michael, and he would make sure that wouldn't change. In the worst case, Michael would bleed as much Essence as the Primal. Even then, the Primal were bound to die long before Michael would 'bleed to death'. Michael unleashed a burst of electricity-attributed Essence into the surroundings, swallowing two Primal in the event. The electricity-attributed Essence was pulled toward them and entered their essence bodies, damaging them. But there was more to it.
Michael noticed something through Seer. Something he didn't anticipate when he first merged the expanse's essence with the weave's essence.
'They can fuse our Essence as well?' A deep frown replaced his calm smile.
'My Essence fuses more smoothly into their bodies. Why though? Because they're born from Essence, and their entire existence was created by the Essence of the weave? Or is there more to it? Wait a moment…'
Michael's eyes widened as information surfaced. Intel he had never considered important.
'The Primal were born with the universe. They're not exactly the children of the weave but the Origin. That also included the Will. But…if that's the case, the Primal were born with the Essence of both the weave and the expanse…right? So, how was it possible for the Will to separate the weave and the expanse in the first place? And why is the Essence of the Primal different now?'
Various thoughts flashed through Michael's mind as he continued the fight. He slashed the Primal a few times and lost a few limbs in the process. Or he would have lost some limbs if not for the Pure Aether Armor and the enhancements from Unlimited Enhancement and pristine Essence. The explosions of Essence Blades were as annoying as ever. However, the Pure Aether armor protected him well.
Michael regenerated rapidly, allowing him to keep fighting at full power, but his mind was elsewhere.
'The expanse and weave were separated for eons now, and the Primal never stopped using their Essence. Every motion uses Essence, no matter how little it uses. Doesn't that mean the Primal's natural essence – the mixture of the weave's essence and the expanse's essence – has been replaced and substituted by the weave's essence.' Michael didn't know whether to cry or to laugh.
The Primal had been part of the Creation, but they weren't full members of the creation anymore. In fact, neither the weave nor the expanse could be considered creations of the Origin anymore. They were only part of the creation, respectfully.
'How can I take advantage of that? Would it be helpful if I filled the Primal with the Expanse's Essence? Will that change their minds? It shouldn't, right?'
Even though Michael was deep in thought, he never slowed down. On the contrary, thinking about ways to deal with the Primal helped him accelerate. He severed a few more limbs of the Primal and beheaded one of them. However, the attacks weren't strong enough to kill them. All the attacks did were three things.
First, the Primal's Essence was drained rapidly, which was a good thing.
Second, Death, Extraction, and Poison entered the permanent wounds inflicted through Pure Aether, forcing the Primal to use up even more Essence. That was also a good thing.
Third, the Primal's bodies attracted the pristine Essence, which filled Michael's body naturally. He was still in full charge of the Essence inside his body and the Pure Aether, but the weave intercepted in his control of the expanse's Essence once it left its body.
No. Once it entered the weave!
That was not great.
The weave was doing something that harmed Michael and slowed down the battle. He was probably fast and strong enough and could have killed one of the Primal already, but the weave intercepted.
Yet, it didn't feel like the weave was trying to work against him, even if it urged him to stop killing the Primal.
'What the hell do you want from me?!' Michael roared in his mind, not expecting an answer.
However, that was exactly what Michael obtained.

chapters.title: Chapter 1085 Balance of the Origin
chapters.content:
1085  Balance of the Origin
Michael didn't know what was going on when the weave stirred, but he noticed a subtle change in his surroundings.
The weave breached the defenses created by the Gods and attacked him. No, that wasn't the right word. It didn't attack him. The weave was trying to tell him something.
It consumed a shocking amount of Essence to breach the defenses and invade the Beginning with a stream of golden glowing Essences. Michael noticed the breach first and was about to call out when he noticed that the breach had been repaired…by the will. Instead of breaking through the defenses of the Gods once and for all to flood the Beginning with its Essence, the weave blocked itself. It ensured the Beginning wouldn't contain more Essence than necessary. Necessary for what? That was something Michael had yet to find out.
The golden glowing Essences created by the weave were the solution. Or so Michael hoped. Gluvos was the first Primal to notice the highly compressed Essences whirling through the wide-open space. His expression was filled with glee as he reached out for it.
"The weave hasn't abandoned us! Let's get rid of this piece of shi—..." The Primal's voice died down as something unexpected happened. The golden Essences created to aid the Primal – or so they thought – passed through Gluvos. They slipped through the Primal and impacted Michael's forehead with shocking velocity. The stream of Essences was fast enough to take Michael by surprise, and it took enormous willpower not to do anything. He could have avoided the Essences but didn't do it because he felt the good intentions of the weave.
The golden Essence struck Michael and pulled him somewhere. Meanwhile, his body continued fighting as if everything was normal. His attack pattern didn't change much, but that wasn't necessary. The Primal were too confused about the weave's sudden actions and feared being betrayed again.
The same fear they had buried around the Beginning resurfaced after eons. It filled them to the brim and forced them to retreat. Three Primal turned around to flee. They were ready to sacrifice their brothers and sisters to survive, only to end up in a battle against Hel, Fenrir, Jormungandr, Sleipnir, and other Major Gods.
The Primal were at a numerical disadvantage and didn't have much access to the weave. If anything, they didn't dare to access the weave, fearing something bad would happen like it did the last time.
Just like the incident when the Expanse and the Weave separated.
'Where am I? Where did you bring me?' Michael tried shouting, but no word escaped his lips. The words remained stuck in his mind as something stretched out within him.
The pristine Essence of the expanse and the golden, compressed Essence of the weave created sparks in his mind as they clashed. They battled bravely for several seconds until Michael's mental power surged forward to suppress the sparks. He forged the Essences to merge, creating a clearer image of what the weave was trying to tell him.
However, Michael could only depict a few images. The first image showed the Beginning and how it once looked. It showed the beginning of time and the lives that had once occupied the now barren galaxy of the Beginning.
The second image showed the Primal, their bodies filled with brightly shimmering and dark, gloomy energies. The dark, gloomy energy was clearly the essence of the weave. The weave's essence wasn't as dark as it used to be during those times but Michael didn't doubt for a second that the dark energy was the weave's Essence. In the same breath, Michael realized what the brightly shimmering energy was. It was the expanse's essence.
'It is exactly like I feared. The Essences of the Expanse and the Weave belong together.' Michael cursed inwardly while trying to piece the remaining pictures together. The remaining pictures were mostly of the Primal, smiling from one ear to another as they helped each other…as they helped all creatures of the Creation.
But there were also more pictures. Images showing how magical the evolution of the Origin ought to be and what the Origin Universe had always been supposed to evolve into. Images of a balance…the balance between the two monster-powerful energies in the universe.
Finally, two pictures indicate the event the Will had called the 'Inevitable Separation' and the 'Void Call'.
The Void Call and the Inevitable Separation occurred simultaneously. The former was an attempt of other universes to hijack the Origin Universe. They sensed something from the Origin Universe and decided to attack in an attempt to conquer the Origin Universe before it could grow. However, their invasion failed. The Primal sacrificed the balance in their Essence to devour the invaders. This resulted in the Inevitable Separation.
09:26
Something about the Primal changed after the Void Call. They lost control of the pristine Essence of the expanse and were forced to rely on the weave to mend their wounds. The pristine Essence had been used to destroy the invaders, which decimated the Primal's power drastically. However, they did not only lose their pristine Essence. The balance of their entire being was lost, just like half of everything that transformed the Primal into what they were…what they had always been.
The Void Call destroyed everything, forcing the Will, the only Primal who'd expelled the weave's Essence, to be with the Expanse as they separated. The Will altered the Expanse and shaped it according to his will, sealing the power of the invaders from the Void to keep it away from the Weave and the Origin Expanse until the end of time.
Michael was dumbfounded at the massive flood of information he acquired through mere pictures, but he should have expected it. He still missed some intel to know every little detail of what had happened, yet Michael didn't have to know everything to understand what he had to do.
The aftermath of the Void Call had been cleansed and the mistake of the Will had been removed with Michael's help.
The Will's mistake was also related to the creation of the Void in the ORigin Expanse. Instead of perfectly sealing the power of the void creatures who'd invaded the Origin Universe, the Will had been forced to create a space where the void power could reside. The same power had drained the Will's Essence, yet it didn't affect Michael.
That was important to know, but it wasn't crucial for the following two factors.
First, the Primal could be treated. Only half of their existence was evil. They needed the pristine Essence of the expanse to return to their rightful spot as the Guardians of the Origin Expanse. After all, that was what the Origin had created them for. To guard all beings of the Creation.
But doing so was difficult. Michael wouldn't have bothered thinking about the possibility of rescuing the Primal if not for one factor.
The weave wasn't certain that an incident like the last Void Call wouldn't repeat itself.
What if it happened again and the Primal weren't present? Could he handle problems like the Void Call alone? The Will's memories of the Void Call surfaced in the worst possible moment and Michael's confident plummeted.
The Primal had been created for this purpose. Michael, on the other hand, wasn't made to deal with the power of the void. He would die. That was a fact.
'Fuck this shit! Why the hell do I have to save them?!'

chapters.title: Chapter 1086 Together, Not Alone
chapters.content:
1086  Together, Not Alone
They needed the Primal. To be precise, the universe needed its Guardians to protect it from potential invaders from the void. Attackers from outside the universe invaded the Origin Universe only once, but that had been enough to change the course of events up until now. The Primal, the only beings who could contain, merge, and harness the Essence of the Expanse and the Weave were the only beings with the powers to fight void creatures efficiently. The Will was certain Michael was strong enough to deal with the issues at hand, but it was also fully aware of how inefficient his powers would be against the void. Only the Origin – together, not separated – would work efficiently.
That being said, Michael had to spare the Primal. Killing one of them was already bad for the universe, but it would be fine. Maybe it was also fine to kill another Primal. Unfortunately, it was a fact that the Origin needed as many Guardians as possible if the void creatures were to return.
No, that wasn't an 'if'-question. The Will, expanse, and weave were certain the void creatures would attack again. The only questions were "when" would the void creatures attack, and "what" did the Origin prepare to deal with the void creatures?
Michael couldn't answer any of those questions, but he could influence the latter…by leaving the Primal alive.
'Fuck this shit. Killing them would have been much easier than this bullshit!' He cursed in his mind as a plan formed in his head.
The main problem wasn't that Michael had to defeat the Primal without killing them. The crucial point was that Michael had to defeat the Primal and drain their Essence while the Gods and the Weave decreased the influx of Essence in the Beginning before infusing the pristine Essence surging through his body inside them.
The latter would weaken him while simultaneously strengthening the Primal because the two strongest Essences in the universe would merge and create Origin Essence – the Essence that created the Primal. Origin Essence could only be harnessed by the Primal, which was also why Michael's body had been going crazy since the golden Essence of the weave had forcefully entered his mind. Another problem was that Michael had to create a stable influx of Essence within the Primal. That being said, the Primal needed a perfectly balanced amount of Origin Essence. After fighting for eons, they were either weakened and skinnier than before or contained too much of the weave's Essence. Removing the weave's Essence was possible, but not without permanently injuring the Primal. Michael had to insert his pristine Essence into the Primal while simultaneously draining their Essence.
That required far more precision and focus than Michael would love to pay to such a task. After all, the Primal would grow stronger with every bit of Origin Essence forming inside them, forcing Michael to pay even more attention to their actions.
"One at a time," Michael mumbled, shooting toward Gluvos. The chubby Primal lost his limbs several times in his fight with Michael. His Essence wasn't drained just yet, but he'd lost the most Essence among the remaining Primal.
Michael took advantage of that and focused on Gluvos while sending a message to the other Gods.
[I need you to up your game. Try to refrain from the other Primal while I take care of Gluvos. If everything works out fine, we'll have another Primal fighting on our side in a few–...soonish.]
Michael didn't explain what was happening, but Loki's children responded instinctively. Beelzebub joined Loki's children and attacked the Primal. Gaia, Chronos, and more than a dozen Titan Gods, who'd been holding back for a while now, charged into the beginning. They unleashed their Laws and Authorities, ready to thrash the Primal for everything they'd done.
Michael could tell the disparity in strength between the Gods and Primals via Seer, but he hoped the gods were strong enough to stall five Primals long enough. 'Fenrir and the others should be strong enough to stall two of them with some help. If the rest cannot even handle three Primal…maybe it's for the best if they die. Their Essences would be wasted on the–...' Michael shook his head and cursed himself, 'Since when did I start thinking like that? This much power is getting to my head.'
The sensation of power itself wasn't too bad. It allowed Michael to stand up for himself and protect those important to him. However, it also gave him the power to oppress others and force his opinion onto them. That wasn't a good thing. If anything, Michael hated himself for thinking he could force everyone to do as he pleased.
'Maybe it wasn't that bad that the weave told me to keep the Primal alive. This much power is getting to my head. I need someone to stand up against me. A few beings capable of restraining me if something goes wrong.' He couldn't tell if the Primal were the right choice, but the images he'd received of them and what they'd looked like in the first few days of their existence were rather convincing. Michael was convinced that if the Primal regained their balance, everything would end on a good note.
He sure hoped so.
Gluvos attacked Michael several times, but Michael let them through instead of evading the attacks. Nonetheless, he used the Wolf Divinity with pristine Essence and Unlimited Enhancement to drain as much of the Primal's Essence as possible.
Hundreds of projectiles pierced through Michael, but none of them escaped through the other side. The projectiles were devoured, transformed to Death, Poison, and Extraction with a simple use of Permute – which Michael could still use through the Wolf Divinity – and fired back at Gluvos.
He reached Gluvos and grasped his arms tightly, ignoring the Essence Blades stabbing into his chest and stomach. Dozens of tiny explosions resounded, but all Michael paid attention to was to infuse pristine Essence into the Primal.
'What did I do wrong? Where is the mistake? Where did I go wrong?' Michael cursed all while Gluvos' strength increased steadily.
10:45
Michael's stomach was torn apart, his chest ripped into chests. His heart exploded, and even his Nature Heart suffered greatly. Michael had to stay alive with Ocean World, the perfect Soullife Arts of the River of Vigor, alongside the Nature Divinity. That worked out well, and he survived, but his strategy didn't work out as well as he'd hoped.
Gluvos devoured the pristine Essence rapidly and started creating Origin Essence, but nothing changed. The Primal's personality didn't even change after half of his being was made of Origin Essence. 'What did I do wrong? Where is the mistake? Where did I go wrong?' Michael cursed all while Gluvos' strength increased steadily.
Together.
Not alone.
'Thank you for nothing. I know that as well. The Primal have to stay together to act as the Guardians. The universe needs all of them. I KNOW!' Together.
Not alone.
"I KNOW!!!" Michael roared, "The Weave and the Expanse belong together. I know that!"
TOGETHER!
NOT ALONE!!
The words thundered in Michael's head several times, but something in his mind clicked only now. Only after he heard himself answering, he'd sought.
The Weave and the Expanse belong together. They're the sides of a coin. The sides of the Primal.
A moment later, Michael did something he might regret later.
His hand landed on Gluvos' forehead, pressing tightly against it to send a stream of pristine Essence into him.
However, the Essence was different. It accompanied a Link to the Expanse.
Michael connected Primal Gluvos to the Expanse.

chapters.title: Chapter 1087 Connected
chapters.content:
1087  Connected
For the first time since the Separations, a Primal reconnected with the Expanse.
For the first time since the Void Call, a Primal regained a portion of his true being.
The Origin Essence strengthened him, while the changes to his personality pushed Gluvos to fight more ferociously than before. It was almost like the Primal had realized Michael's hesitation. Maybe that was the case. Maybe the Primal noticed Michael stopped trying to kill him and his siblings. That allowed Gluvos to fight without care for his defense. Michael was the one who was forced to pay more attention to his attacks if he wanted to keep Gluvos alive.
10:46
Michael instinctively sensed a drastic change in Gluvos' Essence. The silverish-dark Essence was replaced by the bi-colored Origin Essence in the Primal's reserves. That change, even if it wasn't visible from the outside at first, was enough to ignite a domino effect of changes. Gluvos roared at the top of his lungs, uncontrollable pain sweeping through his cells. And that even though Michael had long since let go of the Primal.
Gluvos' roar transformed into an ear-deafening scream. It filled the Beginning and took the Primal by surprise. They initiated a second attempt at fleeing but the Gods restrained their movements. Michael was glad they did because it would be difficult to finish the sacred mission given by the weave if the Primal were to flee now. Maybe he could fix Gluvos and the Primal fighting the Calamity Dragon, but the rest would be troublesome to deal with if they'd managed to flee.
'Stop thinking about things that haven't happened yet. Focus on the task ahead!' Michael urged inwardly while trying to retaliate against Gluvos.
Gluvos was overflowing with emotions, sensations, and the accumulated pain of millions of years. Maybe most Primal would react to this by fleeing but Gluvos' eyes were crimson and filled with bloodlust. The Primal was changing but as the changes were introduced to his retaliating body, he also transformed into a fierce and bloodthirsty combatant.
The Origin Essence strengthened him, while the changes to his personality pushed Gluvos to fight more ferociously than before. It was almost like the Primal had realized Michael's hesitation. Maybe that was the case. Maybe the Primal noticed Michael stopped trying to kill him and his siblings. That allowed Gluvos to fight without care for his defense. Michael was the one who was forced to pay more attention to his attacks if he wanted to keep Gluvos alive.
Michael cursed his fate once more, but a trace of hope ignited in his heart when he noticed something unfamiliar flickering in Gluvos' bloodthirsty eyes. The Primal was angry, confused, and overflowing with a type of energy he'd only felt for the first few days of his life. He missed the Origin Essence and embraced it tightly, ignoring how much the addictive sensation of the strongest Essence in the universe affected him. That increased Michael's challenge considerably, but he watched Gluvos come to his mind slowly.
It would take a while, but Gluvos would come to his mind.
'I'd appreciate a little bit more speed. How about you transform back into that smiling pushover faster?' Michael asked the Primal inwardly, but Gluvos didn't answer. That was probably for the best. Gluvos attacked Michael hundreds of times in a second. He blocked most attacks, using Pure Aether, Extraction, Poison, and Death to rebalance the amount of Essence within the Primal. It was a slow process, but most of the weave's Essence had been drained or transformed into Origin Essence under the Expanse's pristine Essence. 'If not for Seer, balancing their Essence would be impossible.' Michael grumbled, 'I would have to kill the Primal if not for Seer. There is no way for me to perfectly balance their Essences mid-battle if I cannot see it. Even now, I cannot be certain everything is fine. It doesn't feel great to give someone else access to the Expanse and its reserves, either. Bastard! Get back to your senses. Now!!'
Michael transformed Pure Aether into a massive hammer the size of a spaceship and smacked Primal Gluvos firmly. The Primal's skull cracked, but the damage was far less than anything Michael could have hoped for. Even though it didn't look like Michael was growing weaker, Primal Gluvos' power was clearly increasing.
'I still have full access to the Expanse, whereas Gluvos has only a strong enough connection to gain exactly the amount of pristine Essence I'm willing to give him. That has to be good enough.'
The tip of Gluvos' Essence Blade pierced the Pure Aether armor and scratched his throat, but Michael teleported behind Gluvos. Slipstream consumed too much Essence for it to be worthwhile most of the time, but Michael was tired. Tired of getting his body torn apart. Tired of the fight with the Primal.
But even more so… Michael was tired of getting used.
The Will had used him.
Fenrir, Hel, and Jormungandr had used him.
Even Loki and everyone else made sure to take advantage of him once they found out that he was the perfect vessel. Everyone wanted something from Michael.
But Michael was tired.
"Get your act together!" Michael roared, his hands transforming into claws that reached for Gluvos neck.
"Stop that!" Gluvos roared, speaking the first few words since the Expanse Link had been forced upon the Primal.
"Only if you get your act together!" Michael rumbled.
A moment later, he snapped Gluvos' neck. It broke just like that. It was almost too easy.
…
The cracking noise resounded through the Beginning. It was much louder than expected, but neither Michael nor Gluvos paid attention to that.
Gluvos gurgled something incomprehensible, which Michael ignored as he infused just enough pristine Essence into the Primal to transform the remnants of the weave's Essence into Origin Essence.
Once the Primal's body was filled with Origin Essence, Michael sealed his access to the expanse's essence. Only a quarter of a second later, the Primal tried absorbing the surrounding Essence, but Michael had been expecting such a move.
Pure Aether surged out of Michael and engulfed both, isolating Michael and the Primal from the outside.
"Remember who you are," Michael thundered.
"Remember what you are," He added, his voice resounding in the perfectly sealed cage of Pure Aether.
"Remember your mission."
"Remember how happy you have been."
"Remember your love."
"Remember your responsibility."
Michael took a deep breath.
"Remember everything you can become…everything you can change."

chapters.title: Chapter 1088 Salvation
chapters.content:
1088  Salvation
The Gods struggled against the Primal. They had a numerical advantage, and the Primal were restrained by the lack of Essence in the Beginning, yet the Gods didn't gain on the ground against the Primal.
Fenrir transformed into a flash and pounced the nearest Primal, his massive claws coated in the power of Extraction. However, before his claws could hit the target, the Primal either disappeared, evading the attack, or an Essence Wall erupted before him. The Essence Wall wouldn't last long against Fenrir and his Extraction-coated claws, but they were strong enough to stall him for a few seconds.
That gave the Primal enough time to counterattack or to deal with the other Gods. The Primal chose to do both. He created hundreds of Essence Spears on a whim and attacked Fenrir with half of them, forcing the great wolf to retreat.
Fenrir compromised his size while evading the Essence Spears, but he had been a little too late. Three Essence Spears pierced his sides before the great wolf could transform into a horse-sized monster. The Essence Spears didn't explode, but they released the Essence that held them together into the surroundings while disintegrating.
The Essence filled Fenrir, slowing the great wolf. Fenrir was forced to retaliate by sending waves of Extraction's power through his body. However, even that wasn't a perfect solution.
Fenrir was forced to throw his Essence against the Primal's Essence to expel it from his body. That required both attention and energy – or Essence – and wasted precious seconds.
Jormungandr and Hel weren't in a good position either. Their situation was not as bad as their brother's, but it was only a matter of time before more problems arose. Jormungandr blocked more than one hundred Essence Spears with his body. He was forced to use the Power Authority through his scales, which was enough to block the incoming attacks.
If the situation had been a little different, Jormungandr would have focused on attacking, using the Power Authority and the Law of Poison to deal devastating damage to the Primal and the surrounding land, but instead of switching to the offense with mindless attacks, the World Serpent focused on the defense. He stalled the Primal and let his siblings deal proper damage.
Fenrir may not have inflicted much damage, but the great wolf's attacks forced the Primal to retaliate against the projectiles made by Essence. The more Essence the Primal used, the better. That was something everyone had learned about the Primal the hard way. The Primal would be problematic enemies as long as they possessed enough Essence to do something. Only by draining their Essence to a dangerously low level would their prowess drop considerably.
Hel focused on that task just like Fenrir. She cast Death upon the Primal before them to weaken their enemy. However, the Primal blocked Hel's Death much easier than other beings could. As beings who weren't afraid of death – or rumored to be fearless in the face of death –, the Primal weren't prone to Death Afflictions. Mortals and the present Gods, Demi Gods, and other beings were easier to inflict with Death. After all, everyone present other than the Primal was either forced to face death occasionally or had been standing on the brink of death too long in the past.
One way or another, the three siblings were forced to combine their power to stall one of the chubby Primal. Even then, it was obvious that the Primal wasn't at a disadvantage. On the contrary, the Primal had the time and enough concentration left to attack the World Serpent at the exact same spot. Nothing important happened at first, but after the 10th or 20th Essence Spear struck the same serpent scale…it shattered. Even the Power Authority wasn't capable of augmenting the World Serpent's natural regeneration. He needed Michael's Soultrait and Nature Divinity to heal him instantly. However, the Beast Gods and Michael weren't part of the same anymore. They had been separated.
The Essence Spear shattered one serpent scale and dug deep into Jormungandr's flesh. The World Serpent hissed in pain and anger and switched to offensive. However, that was exactly what the Primal had been hoping for. Three of Loki's children attacked the Primal together, but all the Primal did was smile.
It was a devious smile, which should have been warning enough. The Primal summoned a Storm of Essence and accelerated. Instead of using his Essence sparingly, the Primal had chosen to unleash their fury. After all, they could only use their Essence as long as they were still alive. Even if they may change the weave by using massive amounts of Essence, they would survive. That was their highest priority.
After all, they had to survive no matter what.
As for the reason they had to survive…they had forgotten. Did they ever have a reason to stay alive? Wasn't it normal to desire staying alive?
Jormungandr's Poison Law infested the Storm of Essence just like Hel's Death attached to the storm. At last, Fenrir's Extraction power joined the fray and feasted on the Storm of Essence flooding the vicinity. The Laws and Authorities worked well against the Storm of Essence. They tore apart the Storm of Essence, even though it was a slow process.
Unfortunately, by paying attention to the Storm of Essence, the three Gods forgot about the Primal.
He appeared in their midst, waving a massive blade across Hel's stomach while a massive lance pierced through Jormungandr's shattered serpent scale. Hel's stomach burst open and a fountain of blood spilled out of the World Serpent's massive body.
Simultaneously, massive chains made from Essence coiled around Fenrir's neck and legs. Fenrir roared in fury and reacted quickly, but the Primal had already appeared next to him with a spear in his hands. He pulled the spear back and was about to drive the spear deep into Fenrir's eyeball when something unexpected happened.
A familiar Primal appeared before the Primal the siblings had been fighting.
"That's enough." Gluvos murmured, stretching his hand out.
"We've suffered long enough. Salvation has come."

chapters.title: Chapter 1089 The Guardians
chapters.content:
1089  The Guardians
The other Gods weren't faring well against the Primal either. The first hours hadn't been a problem. Instead, the problems started when something about the Beginning was changing. Michael was doing something to Gluvos, but nobody could tell what exactly he was doing. But whatever he did, it also affected the other Primal. Their fighting style changed drastically, and it was only a matter of hours before the Primal started using more Essence.
Their reservation of using Essence was replaced by excitement. The Primal were now excited to use as much Essence as possible to fight and gain the upper hand. That was what they did. They gained the upper hand slowly, pushing the Gods over the edge.
The defending Gods were having a hard time, but they stalled for enough time. At least, that was what they were hoping for. Stalling for a few more hours was possible, but how long could they survive the constant assault? No. More importantly, was the question…How much longer was Michael going to take to finish his job? That was a good question, but nobody had an answer. Michael and Primal Gluvos had been sealed and isolated in the Pure Aether cage for hours now, and they couldn't even be certain that Michael was still alive.
The uncertainty of Michael's condition ate the Gods alive. It increased the pressure put on those Gods who'd already been injured and planted a seed of fear in their hearts. What if Michael was already dead, and they didn't know about it? What if everything was over? In the first place…what was happening to the Primal? Why did their fighting style change so suddenly?
The only one without any doubts was the Calamity Dragon. It had sustained various injuries fighting Kytos, but the Calamity Dragon had yet to start struggling. If anything, the Calamity Dragon's rusty muscles had yet to loosen up properly. The Calamity Dragon's power increased with the Primal. Not because Kytos was growing stronger but mostly because the Calamity Dragon regained his former power.
The Gods' confusion was about to reach a peak, and some even considered leaving the Beginning to flee and seek asylum somewhere secure when the Pure Aether cage burst open, revealing Michael and Primal Gluvos.
Both were still alive and well. In fact, Michael and Primal Gluvos looked too well. It was almost like they hadn't been sealed in a small cage of Pure Aether for several hours.
However, something about them had changed. Primal Gluvos was the first to move. He appeared before his brother with a simple kick in the open space and stopped the Essence Lances that were about to rain down on Loki's children.
"That's enough," Gluvos murmured, the corner of his lips turning into a sad smile.
He stretched his hand out to the Primal while relying on the vibrant glow engulfing him to spread further and reach his brother.
"We've suffered long enough. Salvation has come."
It didn't take long to realize what had happened to the Primal. Theoretically, at least.
Primal Gluvos' Essence had been altered. His Essence and, thus, presence were different. Therefore, everything about the Primal was changing. After all, Primal Gluvos, just like his siblings, existed because of their Essence. The Essence stored within them was their everything. It was a crucial factor and determined EVERYTHING about a Primal.
But…was it possible to change a Primal's Essence permanently? It had to be. After all, that was exactly what had just happened. Or were they mistaken? Was something else happening?
"Primal Gluvos has returned to the Creation!!" Michael roared at the top of his lungs. He didn't care whether the other Primal could hear him, but the other Gods had to understand what was happening.
"The light of the expanse returned to the Origin. The Primal…returned to the Origin," he rumbled. Welcome Primal Gluvos back into the Origin and allow him to make amends. Allow him to return to his sacred duty."
"Welcome the Guardians of the Origin Universe!!"
The Gods were having trouble processing what was happening, but seeing Primal Guvos and perceiving the Essence burning fiercely within him was enough to alter their tactics. Hel, Fenrir, and Jormungandr pulled back and joined the other Gods in their ordeal against the remaining Primal while Gluvos fought his brother.
Origin Essence filled the Beginning when Primal Gluvos made his move. The fabric of space and reality distorted right before his fist crashed into his brother. Ripples of Origin Essence filled the surroundings and surged into the brother.
That was the first time anyone saw the Primal fight each other seriously. Their earlier battle hadn't been like that. Something had changed. Everything was changing. Even Gluvos physique changed slowly. His stomach retracted, muscles replacing the Essence that had needlessly amassed around his stomach. The safety ring transformed into muscles.
Michael inspected Gluvos' changes but only for a moment. He arrived next to the Calamity Dragon, who eyed Michael for a moment.
"You're boring. Why would you stop fighting them? There is no need to return them to the Creation. They had one chance to pick their desired path, and everyone, other than the Will, messed up." The Calamity Dragon roared in anger, but Michael shook his head.
"Even the Will made a mistake, and it took the Will way too long to fix it," Michael smiled sadly, "I don't really care how you think about this, but if you don't want the Void Call to repeat itself, you better help me. The Guardians will be needed in the future."
The Calamity Dragon roared, but it wasn't as ear-deafening as earlier. Michael patted the Calamity Dragon on the shoulders and transferred enough supreme healing serum to the dragon to heal him.
"How about you help me here? Once we're done with Kytos, you can beat up the others. Is that not what you want?" Michael teased the Calamity Dragon, who roared again. The dragon swiped Michael with his claws, but only one Imperial Barrier was needed to block the measly attack.
Michael responded with a smile rather than anger.
The Calamity Dragon didn't like him or the thought of giving the Primal a second chance after everything they'd done.
However, he forgot that Michael did the same thing for him. Michael gave the Calamity Dragon a second chance. It was obvious that the Primal deserved an opportunity to make amends, too.

chapters.title: Chapter 1090 More!
chapters.content:
1090  More!
Michael and the Calamity Dragon fought Kytos together. He might not need any help from the Calamity Dragon, but the ancient creature didn't want to leave Kytos alone. He told Michael that he was going to kill Kytos if he failed to regain his fated position as the Guardian of the Origin Universe.
Michael didn't like the way the Calamity Dragon spoke, but he accepted the condition. He would have to kill the Primal if they didn't return to their sacred duty either way. They were too dangerous if let loose.
Michael arrived behind Kytos after the Calamity Dragon's void flames burned through his Essence membranes. He embraced Kytos tightly and infused one of the Expanse Links into the Primal. Primal Kytos tried blocking the Expanse Link, but Michael infused the link with enough pristine Essence to overwhelm him. Furthermore, Unlimited Enhancement and the Soul Tears of Soul Grimoire boosted the Expanse Link and pristine Essence, elevating their potency and efficiency to a higher level. That was barely enough to establish the connection with the Expanse Link and start infusing pristine Essence into Kytos. The first traces of Origin Essence were produced within Kytos, starting the Salvation process of the second Primal.
Kytos transformed Michael into a half-dead porcupine with hundreds of Essence Spears but Michael ignored the onslaught. He relied on the Expanse's Essence to fuel his Divinities, which worked together in unison. Four Divinities worked at full power within Michael alongside more than a dozen Soultrait Symbols. No matter how strong Michael was, the mental power drained from multitasking with so many powerful abilities was far from easy. If anything, it was one of the most challenging things he'd done until now.
It was impossible to evade all attacks, especially now that Michael had to supply two Primal with enough Essence to stimulate their production of Origin Essence.
Gluvos used too much Origin Essence against his brother, infusing Origin Essence into the Primal to remind him of his sacred duty. That was great and all, but it consumed too much Origin Essence, which urged Michael to open the floodgates of Expanse Essence. Michael had to share his Essence with two Primal, with one of them growing stronger as more and more Origin Essence nestled in his being.
"Go faster!" The Calamity Dragon cursed Michael, but he ignored the dragon after sending him a wave of supreme healing serum. There was no need to pay any more attention to the Calamity Dragon. The ancient creature would be fine as long as he didn't sustain any grievous injuries.
Michael evaded a series of Essence Blades that exploded as they whizzed past him. The explosions were massive and destructive enough to destroy entire planets, but Michael blocked the explosions with a single Imperial Barrier. He used his Soultraits, Seer, and Primordial Vessel, to their limit via two Soullife Arts and added Galaxies of Elements by altering his Essence to move even faster through the open space.
He may not rely on Beast Halo and Taming right now – the Soultraits were useless in the given situation – but Imperial Barrier, Perfect Enhancement, Death Call, Extraction, Slipstream, Emperor Qi, Godly Faith, and even Mind Watcher were incredibly useful.
Primordial Vessel, Death Call, and Extraction could be considered his strongest Soultraits because of the Divinities that grew from them, but Godly Faith was at least as useful. In fact, it was how Michael acquired enough power to fight the first Primal. Of course, River of Vigor and the Nature Divinity couldn't be ignored either. If not for his terrific fast recovery, Michael would have died tens of times already.
But he was still alive and well.
He overshadowed his enemies and survived. Michael wouldn't go down quickly.
"Die!" Kytos roared, severing the Calamity Dragon's wing with a several hundred meter long saber made of Essence. The Calamity Dragon roared in pain and anger but he couldn't retaliate. But Michael could. And he did. The Law of Poison, Power of Extraction, and Death Authority pushed forward, augmented by Unlimited Enhancement. The Laws and Authorities shrouded the massive saber and feasted on the Essence.
"How about you start paying attention to me too? I'm so lonely without any attention," Michael teased Kytos, whose head flicked to Michael in fury.
He tried retracting the Essence Saber but it was already too late, Michael appeared before Primal Kytos, large blades made of Pure Aether calmly resting in his hands. Michael swept past Primal Kytos, the Pure Aether blade drawing blood and essence as one blade severed the Primal's arm while the other cut through the Essence Saber.
Primal Kytos roared aloud and spun around, releasing waves of Essence Spears where Michael had been at. But he'd slipped away. Using Slipstream, Michael arrived next to the Calamity Dragon with the dragon's wing in one hand. He infused supreme healing serum into the wind and the severed stump, put them back together, and returned to Kytos, who welcomed him with Origin Essence.
Creations made from Origin Essence were more stable, stronger, and…more painful. Michael didn't like how much pain they inflicted, but he could accept the pain if it meant that the Primal started utilizing the Origin Essence reserves within him.
After all, the use of Origin Essence indicated that the Primal was changing and that he recognized the potency of Origin Essence. It was stronger…better.
'Go on. Attack me. Try to kill me!'
Primal Kytos used more and more Origin Essence, which drained his reserves rapidly. However, Michael was already ready for that. The more Origin Essence the Primal used, the easier was it to infuse more pristine Essence into him. The Expanse Link connecting the Primal to the expanse made everything so much easier as well.
As Kytos attacked with a flurry of projectiles and blades, Michael focused on the infusion of pristine Essence and the destruction of the weave's Essence. It was a slow process, but that was fine. Primal Kytos was slowly pushed toward the perfect Balance. That was all Michael needed!

chapters.title: Chapter 1091 Return
chapters.content:
1091  Return
"What is going on?" Kytos asked, his voice void of the same old fury that had accompanied him and his siblings since the Separation.
"You're getting back to your senses. That's good," Michael commented in between two heavy breaths.
It had been a while since he felt this tired. In fact, since he acquired power rivaling Gods, Michael never felt like that. It was a first, but it didn't scare him.
On the contrary, Michael welcomed the exhaustion. The soreness spreading through his body. It showed Michael that he wasn't omnipotent and that a trace of mortality was still left within him.
"Back to my senses?" Primal Kytos glanced at Michael before his eyes drifted to the Calamity Dragon.
"I wanted to kill him! Why did it work?!" The ancient creature roared, turning around to sweep his tail across the Primal's face. Michael created an Imperial Barrier and snickered, "Help the others if you're bored."
The Calamity Dragon growled but obeyed. He traveled to the other Gods and helped them fight the remaining three Primal.
"How about you help Primal Gluvos? You must be confused but we have to end this battle soon. The seals won't last much longer and I don't think the weave can hold back much longer," Michael pointed out, his eyes trailing the leaks in the altered version of the Weave Seal. it was a powerful seal but would have shattered if not for the weave holding back as much as possible. Unfortunately, holding back was not an option anymore.
The amount of Essence, especially Origin Essence, forming in the Beginning stirred the weave. It forced the weave to press against the Weave Seal and attempt to breach the defenses.
"O…okay…" Kytos answered after gathering his thoughts.
The events of the past were deeply imprinted into his soul, but the Origin Essence wiped away the anger and frustration that had fueled him since the Separation. It cleared his head and helped him reminiscent everything he had to know. He recalled everything. His sacred duty as the Origin's Guardian, and how they had failed to protect the universe properly. The Void Call destroyed everything.
But most importantly…the Void Call destroyed them. It transformed the Primal into beings they were never supposed to be and pushed them further away from the Creation. They transformed into evil beings…beings working against the Creation. That was not what ought to be. It was never supposed to be like that.
Fortunately, not everyone had been consumed by the darkness of the Void Call. The Will had escaped.
It protected the Creation and everything it stood for.
The Will granted the Primal a second chance. Even if nobody else would grant them a second chance, the Will prepared everything necessary to rescue them. It worked with the Expanse and trusted the weave's loyalty, and…survived long enough to transfer the fiercely burning flame of justice to someone else.
Primal Kytos' memories were a mess. The Origin Essence churning through his body was the source of all trouble. It released the mess of negative emotions from Kytos into the surroundings, cleansing the Primal from all evil, while positive emotions and the memories of the time before the Separation entered his mind.
But there was more to it. The Will's memories could be found in Primal Kytos' mind as well. They had been transferred to Kytos through the expanse's pristine Essence and ensured Primal Kytos would know what the Will had achieved. How much the Will helped the Creation by not doing anything and what the remaining Primals had to do to protect the Origin Universe and its Creation.
Nothing.
That was all they had to do for the Creation to strive.
The Guardians had to watch over the Creation and protect it, but there was no need for them to intervene.
They weren't supposed to refrain the Gods from altering the weave with their Divinities, and it was also not within the norms of their sacred duty to force anything upon others. They should watch and enjoy the Creation while protecting the universe from harm.
At last, Primal Kytos understood that.
He understood everything.
Kytos took a deep breath and kicked the space underneath him. The Primal transformed into a flash, leaving Michael behind to appear beside Gluvos.
Primal Gluvos was about to attack Kytos when he sensed the Origin Essence within his brother and smiled.
"You are finally back?" Primal Gluvos asked Kytos, who snored.
"Shut up and get working!"
"I missed you too, brother!" Gluvos commented.
Michael raised an eyebrow and jumped into action, following the two Guardians.
He appeared next to them as they restrained their brother and infused enough pristine Essence with the Expanse Link to overwhelm the Primal.
The Guardians restrained their brother while channeling Origin Essence into his body, and Michael fortified the link by channeling more pristine Essence into him.
Simultaneously, he stabbed the Primal, draining the weave Essence as quickly as possible.
The first traces of Origin Essence formed quickly in the Primal's chest, and he screamed aloud, but neither Gluvos, Kytos, nor Michael paid attention to the screams.
They focused on their task ahead and forced the Primal back to the Origin and the Creation. This time, it didn't take long to overwhelm the Primal. With two Guardians by his side, Michael could focus on the Expanse Link and the drainage of weave Essence. The Guardians blocked the Primal and slowed him while also infusing Origin Essence into their brother. It came to no surprise when the third Primal regained his senses. The Guardians infused their Origin Essence with memories, their intentions, and reminiscence of their sacred duty, pushing the Primal over the edge long before they reacted.
The third Guardian returned to the Origin Universe, leaving behind three more to convert.
The suffering of the past and the damage inflicted by the Separation ceased. The Primal returned to their sacred duty and would soon watch over the Origin Universe and protect it.
Everything would be back to normal.

chapters.title: Chapter 1092: Your Mission Is Done
chapters.content:
’Is it finally over?’ Michael wondered, tightly holding onto the growing hope.
Everything should be over soon. The fourth Primal had been rescued and returned to the Creation, leaving only two Primal left to deal with. Four Guardians pinned down the Primal, creating the openings Michael needed to plant the Expanse Links inside them.
The Expanse Essence flooded the Primal, slowly altering their Essence. Origin Essence was created.
Simultaneously, Michael struggled to keep up with the Guardians and Primal. It wasn’t that they were stronger, but the Essence fueling them came from Michael’s reserves. He provided them with the masses of Essence that had been at his disposal.
The Expanse didn’t belong to Michael for a long time. At least, not the Expanse’s Essence. Michael still had full access to the Origin Expanse and the Expanse System, but the Guardians required a constant supply of Essence to retain the balance that transformed them into Guardians. Once the balance was broken, the Guardians would lose their status as complete creations again and revert to bad habits.
Since Michael couldn’t afford something like that, he was forced to share the Expanse Essence in seven ways. He had only been enjoying the full pool of Essence from the expanse for a few months, and most of it had already been taken from him. That didn’t seem fair, but Michael would have been fine about it…if his body didn’t revolt against the scarcity of Essence like a fish on land.
Despite the struggles, everything was fine. The Guardians caught the Primal, and the Expanse Links had been established in the last targets, and the Gods pulled back, leaving enough space for the battle between Guardians and Primal.
Fortunately, there was not much of a fight. The Primal were caught, and Origin Essence was forcefully infused into them, slowly but steadily changing them.
If not for the Gods’ arrogance, everything would have been fine.
The Gods maintaining the altered Weave Seal was certain the final battle would end in the next few minutes and watched the scene unfolding before them intrigued. They focused on the Primal’s final struggles and missed the Weave’s reaction. The sentience behind the weave tried to hold back its Essence, creating the perfect environment to return the Primal to their sacred duty. However, the natural order was too strong.
Everything the Weave held back crashed into the Weave Seal when it lost the battle against its nemesis. The course of time and the might of time.
The Gods weren’t prepared for the tidal waves impacting all over the border to the Beginning and suffered the consequences. They tried retaliating, but to no avail.
The Weave breached the Beggining’s borders, flooding the Beggining with its Essence.
"You are too early!" Michael cursed the weave and visualized the weave, apologizing to him.
He wasn’t sure if that was the weave’s doing or if it was an illusion, but the truth didn’t matter. The crucial factor was that only four out of six Primal had returned to their duty. The weave’s Essence flooded the Beginning, but it only entered the bodies of the two remaining Primal, filling up the Essences Michael and the Guardians had used up to replace with Origin Essence and pristine Essence.
Their hard work was shattered, and the Primal retaliated by gathering the surrounding Essences in a single swoop. The flood of Essences spreading through the Beginning was overwhelming. They were highly potent and had been compressed by the weave in an attempt to spare the Beginning a little bit longer.
Not only did that not work, but the compressed Essence was exactly what the Primal needed to escape. They absorbed the compressed Essence, fused it with the original essence they’d accumulated, and released everything in one go.
The Guardians were hurled through the air, some more injured than others, but Michael was hit the worst. His limbs were severed, and his chest was mangled badly. Not even the Imperial Barriers had been strong enough to protect him.
But the fight wasn’t over. Michael tapped into the Nature Divinity and the supreme healing serum to regenerate rapidly while using Slipstream to retrieve his limbs.
Michael was about to shout something when he sensed how little Essence several Slipstream portals had cost.
’The spatial restrictions have been lifted!’ He cursed in his mind and spun around, where he saw the Guardians charge at their brothers.
However, the Primal didn’t pay any attention to their siblings anymore. Their expressions were distorted in pain and anger, but they tore the fabric of space and reality apart and created a fissure.
The pair of Primal looked back one last time before hopping through the fissure.
They escaped.
…
Time seemed to slow down after the Primal disappeared. Michael’s lips parted, but no word escaped from them. He didn’t have anything to say. What…was he supposed to say in the first place?
The Gods messed up, and the weave swamped the Beginning, allowing two Primal to escape before they created enough Origin Essence to return to the Origin and their sacred duty.
The Guardians looked at each other, and Kytos sighed.
"We’re going to handle this. They didn’t sever the link to the expanse yet, right?" He asked, to which Michael nodded slowly.
The Expanse Link of the two Primal hadn’t been touched. It would be difficult to remove the Expanse Link without losing more than half of its power and Essence, either way. And that would be a permanent loss.
Michael doubted the Primal would remove the Expanse Links.
Kytos looked one last time at Michael and smiled, "That’s good. Thank you for helping us. Without you, we would have never been strong enough to escape this. However, your task is done. You’ve rescued us. This time, we have to rescue our brothers. You have fulfilled your Fate. No, you have done much more than that. You went above and beyond to fulfill the Origin’s mission. The Origin will always be grateful for your sacrifices!"
Michael didn’t feel like his mission was done. It didn’t make sense. The Primal had been the greatest threat to the universe a few days ago, and suddenly, they were the Guardians of the Origin. How did that make sense?
"Let’s go!" Kytos declared, ripping the fabric of space apart to create a fissure.
The Guardians nodded at each other and jumped through the fissure to pursue their brothers.
Meanwhile, Michael was left behind. Kytos’ words rang through his head, but nothing made sense.
"So…I’m done?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1093: The Supreme Lord
chapters.content:
The Guardians could search for their brothers and fix their Essences. They had the means to return them to the Origin and their sacred duty.
The Guardians didn’t need Michael anymore.
"Is it over? How did you turn the Primal into…whatever that was?" Loki asked Michael, who could only sigh deeply, "I reconnected the Primal to the expanse. The expanse and the weave are their parents. They needed the balance of the expanse and the weave for a stable state. Unfortunately, they lost this stability during the Separations."
"So…you’ve solved that by giving up your control of the expanse?"
Michael shook his head, "I’m still connected to the Origin Expanse. The Origin Expanse’s owner is still none other than me. But I share the expanse’s Essence with the Primal. That’s also why I know where the Primal are currently…and that they don’t need me. My task is done here…" Michael’s voice was somber, a trace of disbelief surfacing.
"What’s happening now?" The other Gods gathered around Michael, who shrugged heavily.
He had no idea what would happen now, either.
"I helped with the return of four Guardians. Either the Guardians will help their brothers to return to the Origin, or they will be killed. I hope we can prevent the latter, but…this is not my business anymore. This is the Guardians’ responsibility now."
Fenrir, Jormungandr, and Hel studied Michael in silence. They had been long enough with Michael to imagine the turmoil of emotions ravaging his mind.
Michael had been pushed to grow stronger, forced to go above and beyond not only to survive but also for the sake of his family. However, now that he had achieved everything, nothing more was left for him to do. He was strong enough to fight the Primal and Guardians, the Origin Expanse was subordinate to him, and his existence had changed.
Michael was not human anymore.
He was a Primal of the new generation.
"You can spend time with your family now. You deserve some rest," Loki told Michael, patting his shoulder before he turned to his children.
"You know where you can find me," he said lightly, casting another glance at Michael. You did a great job. We are all proud of you."
The God of Trickery disappeared a moment later, and it didn’t take long before the other Gods started leaving as well. Some thanked Michael for his work, while others left without a word. However, Michael didn’t pay any attention to them.
His mind was blank, and not a single thought interrupted the state of nothingness until Michael was alone with the Gods who had once been part of him.
Hel, Jormungandr, and Fenrir stayed behind to talk to Michael and to be with their friend.
"What will you do now?" Fenrir asked, licking the massive tears in his sides.
Michael looked up and released a small stream of healing serum to tend to his friend’s wound.
"Now?"
Fenrir thanked Michael for the healing serum and added, "Now that the Primal have returned to their place. Most Gods may still hate the Primal, but they must have sensed how much the Primal has changed. They might have many questions and will bother you or other people to figure out what actually happened, but it is a fact that their Essence is different."
"I don’t think their hatred toward the Primal will disappear entirely, but most Gods won’t bother about attacking the Primal," Jormungandr added with a nod, "That being said, let me repeat Fenrir’s question. What will you do now?"
Michael winced and looked away, but his friends stared intently at him.
"I don’t know," He responded, the uncertainty in his voice palpable.
He wasn’t needed anymore.
Michael succeeded fixing the Will’s mistake and rescuing the Primal. He was done.
"You are the owner of the Origin Expanse now, aren’t you?" Hel asked rhetorically, ignoring Michael’s bad expression.
He nodded slowly while the corner of Hel’s lips curled into a vibrant smile, which looked beautiful but also deadly.
"How about you keep going then?"
"Keep going?" Michael asked, "What are you talking about?"
Hel chuckled, her eyes staring deep into Michael’s soul. She stepped forward and pushed her finger deep into Michael’s chest.
"You are the rightful owner of the Origin Expanse. You are the heir. Of course, you have to lead and control the Origin Expanse like the Will has done. Or do you want to abandon the Origin Expanse now that everything is over?"
