"I…didn’t think about abandoning them. But do they really need me?"
This time, it was Fenrir who interrupted.
"It doesn’t matter if they actually need you or not." He grumbled, but Jormungandr hit him with his snout.
"Of course, it matters whether they need you or not. But even if some civilizations might not need you, others certainly need your help. Look at the Forest Elves and Silverfang Tigerfolk. You helped the Forest Elven tribe grow strong enough to rival the High Elves, and you’ve been the reason the Silverfang Tigerfolk has a place in the Origin Expanse. Maybe not everyone needs you, but what if you use the Origin Expanse to create places to help those who need help?"
Michael wasn’t sure if that was what he wanted. However, the thought of expanding the Origin Expanse, reorganizing it, and adding his seasoning to the configurations made by the Will didn’t sound bad. On the contrary, Michael’s expression lit up at the thought of transforming the Origin Expanse into his place.
The Guardian may connect the weave and the expanse within them, creating Origin Essence, but that didn’t mean the weave and the expanse would reunite anytime soon. The Guardians would protect the Creation but that didn’t mean the dangers within the universe would cease.
"Are you not interested in observing the legends of others as they grow in the Origin Expanse? Create challenges for your Awakened and watch them as they create their own epic?" Jormungandr asked, and Michael’s expression lit up the more he thought about it.
Maybe Michael Fang’s legend ended today.
However, the legend of the Supreme Lord had just begun.
[End of the Main Story]

chapters.title: Chapter 1094: The Curses’ Desire I - The Nest
chapters.content:
"What are you doing here?" Evee asked her father, "You shouldn’t be here after…you know."
"After my partner decided to leave me, you mean?" Eren responded to his daughter with a sad smile.
Evee was uncomfortable. She had been very close to her Curse, but the relationship between Eren and his Curse was different. And, to make things worse, Evee’s Curse decided to stay with her. The Rainbow Dragon might not be a Curse anymore but she stayed with Evee for research purposes. The Rainbow Dragon wasn’t present right now. It was out visiting some of her distant family – those who were still alive – but Evee didn’t mind. She was busy either way.
"I feel useless," Eren grumbled, "I still don’t understand why the Curses left us or how some of them stayed with Curse Users. Even Selena’s Hydra didn’t separate its full Essence. Some of it stayed behind with the Nest Leader. So why did my friend and lifelong partner leave?"
Eren’s life had been a mess, specifically because of the Silver Dragon. If not for the Curse manifesting within him, Eren would never have an outfall with his family. Nothing bad would have happened, and he would still be with his family. Maybe their family would have struggled in recent years since the Supreme Human Alliance was having issues, but Eren wouldn’t have minded.
But for the Silver Dragon to abandon him just like that. It was unfair.
"You feel inadequate and as if something important is missing, but that is fine. It makes sense. I would feel like you as well. Unfortunately, you cannot change what happened. The Silver Dragon is not with you anymore. It chose to leave you. It didn’t even leave behind means to contact you or vice versa. That is a fact," Evee didn’t like talking to her father like that, but someone had to do it. If not for her, the Nest Leader would crush her father’s spirit instead.
If she did the talking, Evee could pick what to say. Though it wasn’t like she was a born chatterbox. Talking was never her fort.
"Do you think I should do it?" Eren asked his daughter.
"You want to take Selena’s offer? Do you like her proposal?" Evee asked, but Eren could only shrug.
"I don’t know. I think it’s an interesting proposal. Becoming the Guardian of a planetary system with humans from a backwater galaxy seems like a noble task."
"It’s dangerous—..."
"I know, but I am not afraid of danger. Everyone views humans so negatively after the outfall with the Supreme Human Alliance, but that doesn’t mean everyone is at fault. There is not enough Anti-Blood-I Serum, and it might take decades before every Hyuman is freed. Michael is doing his best, and you are, too, but I want to be helpful as well. Protecting innocent humans in backwater galaxies from hostile races doesn’t sound like a bad idea. Someone has to protect them; otherwise, some races will take revenge on Lesser Humans even though they have never been in contact with the Supreme Human Alliance."
"You are right…but I don’t like it. I…won’t be able to see you often once you are off to take care of an entire planetary system. I know you, so I also know that you will do more than be a silent guardian. You cannot be silent or have a low profile. That’s not in your blood. Sometimes, I’m wondering if you kept that portion of your personality when I was born. I still don’t know why I am like that while you are…anything but low profile."
Eren chuckled, the strain on his features lifting for the first time in years, "You are more like your mother. But then again, you inherited enough of my features to make me worry. I’m more worried about you worrying about me than anything else."
"If you didn’t give me so many opportunities to worry about you, we wouldn’t have this problem," Evee commented bluntly.
"Probably," Eren nodded, "I’m still thinking about taking the post. The other former Curse Users are thinking of doing something similar. Everyone knows the Nest is connected to the Supreme Lord, so they will have to think about it multiple times before they attack one of the Curse Users. Not that most of us have a Curse left, but whatever."
"You’re still calling him Supreme Lord? I don’t think Michael likes that name," Evee asked, but Eren shook his head.
"I think Michael loves it. The name fits perfectly with Michael. He is the Supreme Lord of the Origin Expanse. The one and only proper owner, though the Guardians are also connected, but we can ignore that, I guess."
"Either way," Eren cleared his throat, "Thanks for talking to me. You helped me with my decision. I will take Selena’s offer and help with the Zelgon Stellar System’s issues."
Evee groaned, "They already have issues?"
"Oh, nothing major," Eren responded with a smile, "Only a plague of Insectoids, probably a race born from the survivors of the Tekur race. They’re mutating much faster than the Tekur but look quite similar. They’ve been haunting the Zelgon Stellar System for a few years now."
Evee had a lot to say to her father, but she could tell Eren was about to leave. That being said, she hugged her father tightly.
"Good luck," She whispered, tightening her embrace until Eren groaned, "If you keep embracing me like that, I will need some good luck finding a healer to break a few broken ribs."
Evee released her father but punched him in the sides, tears welling in her eyes, "You better use my communication devices. If not, I’ll come for you in the Zelgon Stellar Systems. Not even your connection to Michael will help you then!"
"Yes, yes, I love you too," Eren said before leaving Evee alone in her laboratory.
Evee sighed deeply, looking at the massive entrance to her laboratory, only to hear a voice behind her. Evee turned to see Hesta.
"Looks like everyone is leaving to take care of the Lesser Humans spread across the cosmos," Hesta said, organizing some of the documents sprawled all over the tables.
"It makes sense, it really does," Evee mumbles, "Michael doesn’t want others to suffer just becaues the Supreme Human Alliance messed up everyone’s view of the human races."
"Yeah…Michael has high hopes," Hesta mumbles, "I think I will help him a little."
"You too?" Evee asked, cursing softly, "Is everyone I love leaving?"
Hesta snickered but didn’t say anything aloud. She embraced Evee tightly and whispered into her ear.
"I would never leave you. How about coming with me? A lovely vacation in a small backwater galaxy. Bashing a few Higher Lifeforms and helping the humans there, and other races if they want some help, to get right back on the tracks."
Evee sighed deeply, "I would love to, but Rebecca asked me if I could finish analyzing this until next week. I’m taking longer than expected.
"That’s because you’re stressed. You’re pressuring yourself too much. You should relax a little and get back to work after that."
"Or…" Evee added, "I will take work with me."
"That works, too, but you should relax a little bit."
"Work is relaxing," Evee commented with a smug smile, "Don’t worry about that, honey!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1095: The Curses’ Desire II - The Nest
chapters.content:
"Mom, how can you be such a hypocrite? You should stop praying for Michael’s forgiveness if you don’t do anything about it. What did you expect to happen?" Hesta asked her mother, Evalynn Fang, trying to understand what was on her mind.
"He will return. Michael has always been a good child. He will return to me," Evalynn said with unfounded confidence in her voice.
Hesta shook her head. She hadn’t been around Michael much in the last few years, but the few times she’d seen him were enough to tell that he didn’t even think about his mother. Michael did not waste a single thought about his mother, and he wouldn’t know if she died. Even if she died, Michael would probably not even mourn. Hesta couldn’t blame him for that.
If she had been in Michael’s stead. She would hate her to the core and wish her death. Michael, in comparison, was much more generous. He forgot she existed and left it at that.
"No, he won’t. But if you want to see him again or hear from him again, you need to do something about it. How about joining the Human Protection Service? Eren and the other former Curse Users joined the program and will receive some funding from Michael. They’re given control of one planetary system in a backwater galaxy, some even multiple, and are tasked to protect the Lesser Human races there.
You do not have to do anything else, but I’m sure Michael hopes we can help them grow up into a responsible race. Michael wishes to avoid another disaster like the emergence of the Supreme Human Alliance. What do you say, Mom? Do you want to give it a try? We could work together and guard one of the larger, lesser human tribes. If our results are good enough, we might meet Michael and talk to him. What do you think?"
Evalynn Fang hesitated, but she was thinking about it.
"He hates me?" Evalynn asked, "But I only wanted to protect you. How can he hate me for that?"
’She still doesn’t understand his point? Even after so many years? Are you serious, mom?’ Evalynn wanted to scream, but she was aware of how efficient that would be. It would be useless. She took a deep breath.
"You followed your adult child alongside father, leaving my brothers, both minors, alone in the Tritan Alliance. Neither of you tried messaging them often. All you did was send a few messages once every three months. But even those messages weren’t genuine. They were no better than saying, ’We know you exist, but we still don’t care about you.’ That is fucked up, Mom!"
Hesta sighed. She glanced at her father, but Peter Fang didn’t budge. He looked stone-cold at her as if she’d killed a bunch of children before them, tearing their limbs apart right before their faces.
"If you want to mend your relationship with Michael in this lifetime, you have to work for it. Michael is already incredibly busy as it is. He’s trying to take care of the Origin Expanse and change parts of it for the better – that works so-so, but he is trying –has a family to take care of, friends to be around, and numerous other duties to take care of. He is a Primal, the Supreme Lord, Father, and still takes care of stuff like the Anti-Blood-I serum."
Evalynn nodded slowly, "Maybe I should do something. I would love to see my granddaughter…"
Hesta smiled at that. She may not have a child and would probably never get one given that she was already a Divine Lifeform in a relationship with Evee, but she knew how effective it was to use her niece against her mother.
"Let’s put Lucia aside. What is this about the funding? Will Michael give us a few Soultrait Symbols if we play along with his Human Protection Service?" Peter Fang spoke up at last, but the content of his words was infuriating. As always.
Enjoy new adventures at empire
"You always speak about Soultrait Symbols, powerful Artifacts, and stuff like that. How about you start working for them instead of demanding them?" Hesta hissed at Peter Fang, who reacted by unleashing a flurry of origin energy. He circulated origin energy through his body and stomped toward Hesta, whose eyes narrowed to tiny slits.
"Don’t you talk to me like that, Hesta! Know your place!" He bellowed, but Hesta didn’t budge. Her father had been scary in the past, but not anymore. He was a pushover, if anything.
Hesta released her War Empress Soultrait, unleashing an overbearing aura that smashed straight into Peter’s face. Peters wasn’t even at the same Tier as Hesta anymore. She was at a higher Tier than her father at this point. Yet, Peter Fang still thought he had the most power in the family. If Michael heard about that, he would probably laugh his ass off.
"You keep forgetting what it means to know your place," Hesta sighed deeply, "I’ve long since decided to cut ties with you, father. Even if my mother is wrong for following me and abandoning my brothers for me, at least she did it to protect me. I don’t condone her actions and will probably lecture her for neglecting Michael and Daniel, but you followed Mother, hoping to acquire a curse in the Nest. You weren’t even here to take care of me when my Curse threatened to swallow me. Nope, you stalked other Curse Users, trying to get your hands on a Curse."
Hesta gave her father the middle finger as she continued, "You acted like a self-centered piece of shit while I was on the verge of death and my brothers had been abandoned. Everyone was helpless, yet you could have stayed with Danny and Michael to be there for them and raise them. You can count yourself lucky that they turned out like this. If not for them being well and all, I would have ripped your heart out!"
Hesta’s eyes glowed dangerously as the power of the War Empress filled her, "You better leave now. I don’t care if you join the Human Protection Service or if you die. You better get out of my sight! And don’t even think about bothering Danny!"
Peter scurried backward and his eyes bulged in surprise. He had never seen his daughter like that. However, that was not why he was so surprised. He was more surprised about the powers leaking from Hesta.
"You have more than one Soultrait Symbol?" He stammered.
"Of course. Michael gave them to me to help him with the Tekur. Our relationship is still a little bit…rough around the edges, but I worked hard to improve my relationship with him. He’s a loving child, you know? Michael doesn’t hate me. All he ever wanted was some love and care. That is why he holds so tightly onto the people he likes. After experiencing what it feels like to get abandoned, Michael would never force the same face upon anyone. Everyone he holds dearly is growing with him. And he makes sure nobody feels neglected. That is tiring, but Michael loves it."
Hesta cleared her throat after the Xth tirade and smiled at her father.
"Did you know that Daniel worked hard to buy Mother a Soultrait as well? He gifted her two Soultraits, though rather weak ones because he still loves her even after everything she did to him and Michael," Hesta explained,
"The only one everyone hates is you, Dad. You did not only make one wrong choice. You didn’t stop going down the wrong path, father."
"You are a disgrace."

chapters.title: Chapter 1096: The Curses’ Desire III - The Nest
chapters.content:
"I am a disgrace?" Peter repeated what his daughter had thrown at him in anger. His face was beet-red, and he had to release his anger somewhere. That was when he ended up in the Nest’s training room. Peter stayed there for several hours until he was lying there, cursing himself and his fate.
"What would have happened to me if I had never met Paul Fang? Would everything be fine?" He asked himself quietly.
His meeting with Evalynn’s father hadn’t been great. He was a Lord in the Origin Expanse and in a fierce war with a Hyuman Lord, who’d nearly killed him. Peter Fang desperately grasped the last thread of his life while the Hyuman Lord had been looming over him. The Hyuman Lord was just about to kill him when Paul Fang arrived.
Continue reading at empire
At that time, Paul Fang was already an old man. Still, the man was a powerful Curse User who loathed Hyumans more than anything. He killed the Hyuman Lord and every Hyuman Awakened and Summon. Paul didn’t care if they were combatants, children, elderly, or pregnant women. Paul killed every Hyuman after losing his beloved wife to a powerful Hyuman.
Their encounter wasn’t all that nice for Peter, but instead of being afraid of Paul, Peter was exhilarated. Witnessing the power of a Curse User for the first time was exciting. Peter was over the moon and asked Paul to teach him what he did. That moment changed everything.
Paul accepted Peter as his disciple and trained him. However, the training was anything but nice. It was torture, quite literally. Still, Peter prevailed and moved onward. He wasn’t talented but possessed the determination to prevail and keep going. That was what he did. Peter gave his utmost and overcame everything. He survived and grew stronger.
He…got to know Evalynn.
Paul continued torturing Peter, while Evalynn didn’t know anything about it. All she could see was her beloved father. The same strong and independent man who had raised her all by himself. He was alone and had to raise a child while fighting both inside and outside the Origin Expanse. But he prevailed.
At some point, Paul returned from the Origin Expanse with Peter. They used a high-quality Teleportation Token and met. Evalynn fell in love with Peter’s determination. She was proud of her father and had always dreamed of finding a man who worked as hard for his goal as her father. Peter was someone like that. Evalynn fell harder and harder in love with Peter, not realizing what her father was doing to Peter.
Paul was never satisfied with Peter, and his dissatisfaction with Peter’s talent intensified when he noticed that the only person he held dearly had fallen in love with him. Evalynn fell in love with Peter, thus sealing the young man’s fate. Paul increased Peter’s training program to an even higher level. Peter tried to overcome it, but the training was inhuman. Still, he found a liking to Evalynn as well and prevailed when he saw the love in Evalynn’s eyes.
Peter survived Paul’s training sessions, but something within Peter broke. He used his raging emotions to survive and grow stronger. That was necessary to survive. He had to survive. He had to grow stronger. If not, he would soon die.
Peter’s desire to survive transformed into an obsession to grow stronger…born in the hands of none other than Paul Fang.
The years passed in the blink of an eye, and Peter attained enough strength to rival Paul. That day – the day he grew strong enough to face Paul Fang head-on – was also the day his master died. Peter killed his master. It wasn’t merely for revenge and to repay the pain he had to endure over the decades. No. It was for freedom. Peter had to be free. He could not survive any longer in Paul Fang’s control.
Neither should his children grow up like this. They didn’t deserve a grandfather like Paul Fang.
Peter chuckled in between a few heavy breaths. He stared at the ceiling, his expression distorted in pain and confusion.
"I killed him to protect my children from a monster, but I didn’t turn out better than him. Abandoning my own children. If not for Paul, I would have never done that. He crushed me… He…" Peter knew it was useless to seek excuses. It was already over. Neither Michael nor Daniel cared about him. They grew up well, even if they had to struggle at times. The brothers didn’t care for their father. Why would they?
"Everything was great until Hesta awakened the White Tiger. If not for that…" Peter mumbled again, only to hear footsteps behind him. The clattering of heels tapping on the training chamber’s ground rang out, pulling Peter out of his train of thought.
"This isn’t Hesta’s fault either. Your obsession to grow stronger returned the moment you recalled the roots Paul planted inside your essence. He planted the root of obsession inside you to make you grow stronger. To forcefully accelerate your growth. He planted it inside you, but the depth of your desires is the reason the root spread through your entire being and blossomed. It is difficult for the root of obsession to grow into majestic flowers, but Paul achieved it with you."
Selena had entered the training chamber when she heard someone mumbling but didn’t expect it to be Peter Fang. She heard about his ’chat’ with Hesta and Evalynn Fang.
"What do you want from me?" Peter snarled.
"What do I want from you? Is there something you could give me?" Selena laughed, "I don’t think I need anything from you."
"Can you fuck off then?" Peter cursed, but the Nest Leader didn’t even twitch.
"How about you join the Human Protection Service? I think watching over a small planetary system will help you reorganize and rebalance your Essence." Selena offered, "I’m not forcing you to do something, but I think it would be the first step in the right direction – toward your family if you want to salvage your relationship with them…or what is left of the relationship – if you became part of the Human Protection Service."
Peter was about to cuss out the Nest Leader, but Selena raised her hands, stopping him before he could say something.
"It was merely an idea. Nobody is forcing you," Selena said before turning around to leave again, "Think carefully about it. Your life is not yet over. Do you really want to be alone for the next hundreds of years?"
Peter had a lot to say, but the somber tone in her voice stopped him. The Nest Leader talked like she was giving him good-meant advice…from her experiences.
"I…will think about it…" Peter grumbled, but the harshness in his voice was no more.
He returned to the ground, his sweat-drenched back pressed against the cold ground.
"Alone…I was always alone. So what if I stay alone for the rest of my life?" Peter grumbled, but the pictures of his life in Elyra flickered through his mind. Their life in the Golden Sun province made him smile. Raising the brothers and training tirelessly with Hesta had been great. There was no doubt about that.
He hadn’t been alone at that time.
He…had been with his family at that time.
But that was no more.
Would he go back to that time if he could? For sure.
Was that possible? Nope.
Nonetheless, Peter could still try to make amends. Maybe the others wouldn’t accept it, but he could try.
That was what Peter Fang did. His journey to reunite with his family began.

chapters.title: Chapter 1097: The Curses’ Desire IV - The Nest
chapters.content:
"Father is messaging me again. Does he have nothing else to do?!" Hesta sighed exasperatedly, but the corner of her lips twitched, hinting at a smile, "What a nuisance."
"He has been more active recently. The last year must have been nice for him," Evalynn commented while looking through a paper stash.
It had been one year since the Human Protection Service started, and it wasn’t exaggerated to say that it had been a wild mess. The protection start had been horrible because most human races had heard something about Hyumans and how they conquered weaker races to kidnap their prodigies. There had been many more rumors, but none of them was great, which made it increasingly more difficult to talk to the heads of the Lesser Human races.
Fortunately, after countless attempts to help and the first incidents requiring the help of the Human Protection Service members, the Lesser Humans warmed up to them. The problem was that the first attacks weren’t the last. The human races weren’t adored anymore, and it came as no surprise when the more powerful Awakened attacked them. The Lesser Humans would have loved to retaliate, but the members of the Human Protection Service advised them against taking revenge.
They shouldn’t go down on the same level as their enemies because that would instigate a downward spiral which would lead to death and destruction. The Human Protection Service was there to protect the human borders and repel their enemies. They made clear to announce their presence at every altercation and told the non-human lifeforms to retreat behind their borders if they did not wish to get attacked.
Defending was one of the most important roles of the Human Protection Service, but that was not all. They were supposed to be the role models of the Lesser Humans in the planetary system and were deployed to create a neutral ground for enemies to talk about the issues they had with each other. This didn’t work all the time, but being in the same room with someone several times stronger than everyone else in the planetary system ensured nobody would do anything stupid.
That was what the Human Protection Service made use of. They constructed a temporary peace treaty by force and showed how nice it would be to live next to each other. Of course, it would be even better if the enemies could change their stances and become neutral forces or allies, but the Human Protection Service didn’t force anything.
Important was only that everyone could see one thing; Now all Hyumans and Humans were bad. Not everyone deserved to be treated like shit only because the Supreme Human Alliance messed up.
"Still, father is doing too much. He is getting on my nerves. This week, he sent me like 20 messages when he didn’t even send half of that two years ago." Hesta grumbled, now also taking care of several pieces of paper. Mostly challenges of foreign beings wanting to fight some humans for whatever reason: it was either about territories in the Origin Expanse – some of these idiots landed in the same region or even ended up neighbors in the Origin Expanse – while others had some feud to take care of. Hesta didn’t care too much about their feuds and only paid more attention to them when it came to love triangles and issues of the same kind.
Those were the most interesting, after all!
"Apparently, he is doing very well taking care of three planets in the Unian Union. He is still training a lot, but the pressure weighing on him is no more. Maybe this was the right course of action for him," Evalynn smiled. She missed Peter but could also tell that her husband was doing fine. The messages between them showed that clearly.
Peter had never been the expressive kind of guy. He bottled up everything or unleashed his emotions while training, but that had changed. It was a slow process, but Peter revealed everything. How he felt when her father trained him up to everything he had done. Evalynn had known some of the things he told her, but she had never known it was this bad. Her father’s death had been hard on her, but it was only one year ago that Peter revealed the unspoken truth to her. He had killed her father.
Evalynn had been thinking about that and had already guessed it. That hadn’t been out of her expectations. It was only obvious that Peter was the one who had killed Paul Fang. Paul Fang had trained Peter to kill him, after all. He had trained the perfect man to take care of his little princess before he could finally leave this place forever.
Unfortunately, Peter broke apart. Paul’s expectations had been too much. The situation was much worse than expected, and everything escalated.
Evalynn was still sad about losing her father, but she understood that he wanted to be released from the burden. Paul Fang’s life had been strenuous, filled with pain and drama. He deserved to rest, knowing someone stronger than him protected his daughter. Peter Fang had been that man.
"He is liked among the people of the Unian Union," Hesta snorted, but Evalynn could only smile at that, "That makes sense. The Unian Humans like powerful Awakened. They’re like the Berserkers and the Warlock Centaurs of the Tritan Alliance."
Hesta looked at her mother, not quite sure what to think about her at this point.
"Did you know that we ended up in the Tritan Alliance because of your father? He always wanted to fight with the Berserkers and Warlock Centaurs. He respected them for their willpower and traditions. It doesn’t surprise me that your father is doing well in the Unian Union. I wish I could be with him."
"You know you can leave, right?" Hesta said lightly, but Evalynn shook her head. That was not surprising.
"You’ll have to learn to live without me at some point," Hesta pointed out the obvious, "I want to live with Evee, and we will probably adopt children as well. You can visit us often, but I want to live my life, too."
Evalynn’s expression worsened, but she nodded in agreement, "I know. Just…Just give me a little bit more time." Enjoy exclusive content from empire
"Once your father and I are better…Then we will leave you alone," Evalynn murmured, but the hesitation in her voice was easy to decipher.
"I hope Michael forgave us for being bad parents by then."
Hesta looked at her mother and patted her lightly. She didn’t dare to tell her mother the bitter truth. Reuniting with Michael was a nice dream, but it was just that. Hesta doubted Michael would accept his mother and father again. They weren’t there when they needed him, and they never truly apologised for their actions. More than half a century passed since that time, and Michael must have stopped thinking about them.
Or maybe she was wrong. Maybe, against all odds, Michael would meet his parents again.
Who knows?
Only the future could tell what awaited them. However, they could work toward that goal and hope their hard work and tireless efforts would be seen.

chapters.title: Chapter 1098: The Curses’ Desire V - The Nest
chapters.content:
[How are you doing?] Snievor, the Nine-headed Emperor Hydra, asked Selena in her mind.
"Why do you keep asking that?" Selena clicked her tongue in annoyance.
[Why do you think I’m asking you that?]
"Because you want to annoy me. You are the best at annoying people. Specifically me!" She snickered but clearly didn’t mean it seriously.
[I can leave you if you want me to. I left a trace of my Essence inside you to keep chatting with you. To make sure my little Nest Leader won’t be lonely.] Snievor commented sarcastically.
"Oh, well…you know. I think I was just joking," Selena sighed deeply.
[To think you aren’t busy enough controlling an entire galaxy alone. I still don’t know how you managed to ensure that those idiotic humans won’t be slaughtered by the next full moon.]
Selena was, just like Snievor said, in control of an entire galaxy. She managed the galaxy as part of the Human Protection Service. There were several human races, including some Hyumans, who’d escaped the control of the Supreme Human Alliance before it got too bad, but also other races. The human races weren’t a minority in the galaxy but were far from the control channels. That was probably why convincing everyone that the humans weren’t bad was so easy.
The humans there had never been in control of power and had been living nicely with their neighbors. Some Hyumans were powerful and possibly strong enough to attain more control, but they didn’t use their strength to acquire power. Instead, they tried to receive more votes for the upcoming election.
There were multiple interesting elections in the galaxy, but the one they talked about was the control of a planetary system. Humans mostly occupied the planetary system and could thus be considered part of the human territory. Still, the Planetary Mayor had been an Indguit, a member of another race in the galaxy.
The Hyuman was fighting with the Indguit to win the next election, but it wasn’t the average fight most people might think about. On the contrary, the fight was a debate to determine who was the better ruler. Their Awakened power didn’t matter. If anything, it mattered whether they still had a territory or how long they had been in control of a territory. After all, that determined their ’experience’ at the job. The size of their territory then determined the "Level" of their years-long experience.
Some other points had to be addressed before the debate and to determine the new position as a Planetary Mayor, but none of them were important to Selena. The humans had been integrated neatly into the galaxy long ago, and there were only a few issues for her to take care of.
She felt useless most of the time but was then reminded that she was the only one capable of traveling quickly through the entire galaxy if something were to happen. Other races may suddenly attack in an attempt to kill all humans in the galaxy. If she wasn’t present…what would happen? Everyone would die.
She didn’t want that to happen. Yet, at the same time, she was bored…and alone.
The Nest Leader lost everything to the Supreme Human Alliance a long – very long – time ago. She resented the Supreme Human Alliance for long and fought them to her heart’s content for centuries. She killed many Hyumans and probably far more innocent people than she wanted to acknowledge. But she was tired of it.
Now that the Supreme Human Alliance was defeated, she didn’t feel the need to kick them anymore. There was no need to kick the Supreme Human Alliance after their powerhouses were defeated and their treasuries plundered until nothing was left. The Supreme Human Alliance had enough enemies who wanted retribution and revenge but had nothing more to give to others.
It was already a wonder that the Supreme Human Alliance didn’t cease to exist. Well, somehow, it already did. Those freed of the Blood Incursion resented the Supreme Human Alliance. They didn’t use the name without cursing or crying ever again.
That didn’t make it better for the Nest Leader. She had also lost a lot, yet everyone expected her to be a good person. But then again… it wasn’t like she wanted to kick them anymore. She received her revenge even if it didn’t feel as good as Selena had hoped.
At this point, the Nest Leader hoped the innocent people would stay alive while the rest of the SHA would crumble and fall apart.
No one else should suffer because of the SHA anymore, not even the population of the Supreme Human Alliance. They were also victims.
But now that everything was over, Selena was just…lonely. The Nest wasn’t what it used to be after the Curses followed their desires and left. Some remained partially, like Snievor, while others returned in their true forms occasionally, like Eevee’s Rainbow Dragon. Still, it was not like it used to be. But it was also not like the Nest was still needed.
They were great prospects for the Human Protection Service, but others could do the same. The Nest’s Curse User didn’t need to do it, former or not.
However, it was a fact that the Curse Users of the Nest needed the love of other people the most. They lost the most from the Supreme Human Alliance. Therefore, they deserved some rest, love, and attention – if wanted.
Not every Nest member applied for the Human Protection Service, but most did after they thought about it for a while. And nobody regretted it. If anything, everyone enjoyed their new lives. They lost a part of their lives and maybe even the purpose of their lives after the endless fight with the Supreme Human Alliance ended, and their Curses were freed, but they received something much bigger in return.
They were pulled back into civilizations that accepted them for who they were. They could use their wisdom to help others and receive love, friendship, care, and much more. Enjoy more content from empire
It didn’t seem like much at first, but it was exactly what the Nest needed—what the Curses had been hoping for.
For their Masters to learn how to live independently and to love themselves again.
That was the Curses’ Desire.

chapters.title: Chapter 1099: Unknown Domain I - Daniel Fang
chapters.content:
"Since when have your parents been so active in your life? Didn’t you say they were deadbeats?" Rebecca asked Daniel Fang, who was busy responding to their messages.
They were seated on a lovely wooden porch made from the [Nature’s Love] Soultrait of a friendly Forest Elf. The porch’s main support pillars were four large tree trunks, whose roots and branches intertwined, forming a neat net, which worked out perfectly to create a ceiling and uneven floor of roots. It took some effort and Lucia’s Nature Divinity to transform the roots into a proper floor – the uneven portions were filled with resilient bushes that highlighted nature’s beauty.
Lucia went above and beyond to grow furniture from the ground and the ceiling, creating a swing of branches, vines, leaves, and several other customized pieces of furniture.
Thinking about Lucia, Daniel smiled vibrantly.
’Did she convince Michael, or is she still trying? Now that I think about it, Michael probably gave in faster than Alice. He’s a pushover when it comes to his daughter. That’s odd, given how powerful Michael is. But then again, being a New Primal doesn’t mean he can easily escape his wife and daughter’s wrath.’
He chuckled and shook his head. A daughter wasn’t easy to raise, especially if you had to do your utmost to make sure that your daughter didn’t turn into an arrogant little prick. Lucia was nice, but she was also powerful. She was aware of her power and had been seen using her power to suppress her peers. Her peers were fools who fell in love with the idiot after she beat the shit out of them.
Until now, Daniel and Michael had no clue how Lucia had done it. They spent countless hours, or it might as well have been days, trying to figure out what Lucia did to the boys for them to fall in love with them after she broke their arms and legs. Some were even beaten half to death, yet they still fell for her.
’Let’s not waste even more hours with that thought. Nobody knows, and we will probably never find out either way.’
Daniel returned his focus to the holographic screen with a thin smile on his lips as he answered all messages. He responded to the questions and went out of his way to answer them, but that much was obvious. After all, they asked about Michael. How could Daniel not answer them when it came to his brother?
"Yes, but no. My parents are weird," Daniel responded, still smiling smugly.
"Is that so? I think you are just as weird. Michael too. No. Michael is probably the weirdest," Rebecca snickered, "But then again…I think the universe would be a much better place with a few more weirdos like you and Michael."
"You think so? I wouldn’t be so sure about that. Too many of us, and we might accidentally destroy a bunch of galaxies. Especially Michael. My brother is a little insane if you know what I mean," He looked up and winked at Rebecca, whose cheeks turned red.
"I…don’t know, actually. But I’m not sure if I want to know. I think I will be better off not knowing anything."
"That’s probably for the best. Other than the news about–...." Daniel’s lips parted, but he shut them before too many important pieces of information left his mouth.
"News about what?" Rebecca asked. She approached Daniel, her eyes glimmering dangerously.
"News about what?!"
Daniel might have attained godhood and acquired the title of the Undefeatable Sword God, but if there was one person who could defeat him…it was definitely Rebecca. Her eyes bore deep into Daniel as she stepped before him. Her finger bore into his chest as she tapped him.
Daniel swallowed hard but didn’t say a word. Not until Rebecca turned away to leave.
"Where are you going?" He asked.
Rebecca grumbled, "You aren’t going to tell me, so I might as well make myself useful and help with the production of more Anti-Blood-I serum."
"But you are on vacation this week."
"They won’t complain if someone with paid time off comes to help," Rebecca shrugged and left. That was enough to break down Daniel’s last defense.
"Okay, okay. Come back, and I will tell you."
Rebecca was back on the porch even before the last word escaped Daniel’s lips.
"I’m good at that, ain’t I?" Rebecca giggled.
"At being a pain in the ass? That’s for sure."
"So what? Now tell me about the news!" Rebecca demanded, and Daniel obliged. He had already lost and there was no need to hide it anymore. In fact, the news would probably spread soon.
We found reason to believe that the Origin Universe has been connected to a much smaller universe, or a fragment of a universe, in the last Primal War. We are unsure if the death of one Primal caused this or if the birth of the New Primal triggered something within the Origin Universe. Either way, the weave is constantly changing and expanding, and we only found out why exactly it is doing so a few weeks ago.
Well, to be precise, Michael found out about it a few weeks ago, and he has been wondering what to do about it. The Guardians have already been informed as well and they decided to share news with the Pantheon. That’s how I ended up finding out a week ago or so."
"You’ve known about it for a week, and you are only telling me about it now?!" Rebecca asked in shock, "How could you do that to me?"
Daniel squinted his eyes. "Calm down. It has only been a week, and you told me not to bother you for the last four weeks because you were busy and that you could not concentrate when I was around. I just followed your order."
Rebecca snickered but she seemed to have calmed down a little.
"So, you found an entirely new part of the universe, which is possibly a fragment of another universe, or a whole universe, though a tiny one? That is lit." Rebecca’s eyes were bright like diamonds at this moment.
"When are we leaving?"
"What?" Daniel responded in confusion.
"Well…when are we leaving for the unknown?" Rebecca asked as if the answer was obvious.
"Michael asked me to check it out. I will be going to research the unknown, yeah. But you?"
"You’re not going to take me with you?"
"Aren’t you busy?"
"Nahhh, others can replace me easily. I was trying to get promoted but exploring the unknown sounds much better."
Daniel raised an eyebrow but nodded slowly. It didn’t sound too bad to be traveling around the unknown, exploring it, with Rebecca. He would love to do that.
"So, you’re coming with me?" Danny asked to ensure that he heard correctly.
"Of course. Who else is coming?" She asked excitedly.
"Nobody. Michael asked me to check it out first. I’m the first explorer."
"Oh…"
Realization struck Rebecca, but she quickly regained composure.
"That’s crazy! Let’s be the first to discover countless new life forms. That will be amazing!"
"Yes, it will be."
As long as they would be together, it would definitely be amazing.

chapters.title: Chapter 1100: Unknown Domain II - Daniel Fang
chapters.content:
"Are you ready?" Rebecca asked in excitement?
Daniel and Rebecca stood before a massive Bridge that would teleport them to the closest border to the unknown domain. After that, they had to travel via spaceship or travel to space like this. However, since Rebecca was not a god, and would probably never be, their traveling speed would be too slow.
In the first place, it was more relaxing to travel by spaceship. They wouldn’t have to waste much precious energy that way.
"I told everyone that it would be hard to contact me in the next…few years. So yeah, I’m ready. Finally, I can have some time for myself." Daniel mumbled, but he caught Rebecca’s gaze and quickly added, "Time for us."
Rebecca nodded and gave him a thumbs-up. She leaned closer to him and kissed Danny on the cheek. That was enough to stir something within Daniel.
"Let’s go!"
Daniel retrieved a small spaceship from his War Rune’s space and approached it to enter. The spaceship was approximately fifteen meters long and seven meters wide. It was flat with a roughly two-meter height and sometimes looked like paper planes. The first time Michael showed him the spaceship, Daniel was certain it was a failure. A spaceship-like that would never rival the large-scale spaceships that could travel at lightspeed through the galaxy.
Reaching the speed of light wasn’t easy and required tremendous amounts of energy. However, Skypiercer was a new creation, a small spaceship capable of reaching the speed of light, which was all they needed to travel through the unknown domain without any issues. At least, that was what they hoped.
Skypiercer would help them navigate the unknown domain, but Daniel and Rebecca would have to solve most other problems independently.
"I’m ready!" Rebecca shouted, charging toward the open gates of Skypiercer to sit down on the co-pilot’s seat and get started. She had used her Soultrait to analyze the spaceship before departure and was up-to-date at this point. It wouldn’t surprise Daniel if she knew more about the spaceship than he did.
That would be great.
He entered the spaceship and started the engine. His mana flooded the spaceship’s control panel, gaining full access to all configurations. His mana had been added to the authorities, allowing him to drive and configure the spaceship as he pleased. But the latter wasn’t necessary, fortunately.
Daniel started the engine and commanded Skypiercer to levitate above the ground.
"That’s not bad at all. Using mana to control everything. Michael did an amazing thing with the Robitcants," Rebecca murmured excitedly, her hands caressing the seamlessly connected metal plates.
"They did a great job, yep," Daniel added lightly before telling Skypiercer to move forward. A single mental command was all it took to shoot forward and charge into the Bridge. The world around Daniel and Rebecca twisted, and it didn’t take long before the harbor built around the Bridges disappeared.
The wide-open space appeared around them, revealing countless stars in the distance. However, Daniel and Rebecca were more focused on the situation ahead.
"Michael told me that the border to the unknown domain couldn’t be missed, but I did not expect it to be like this," Daniel murmured while Rebecca nodded absentmindedly. She used her Soultraits to analyze the situation unfolding ahead of her, but given the missing pieces of information, Analysis struggled to come up with a proper answer.
The unknown domain looked similar to the Origin Universe, but there were a few particular differences. First, the space was even darker than the Origin Universe’s space. It wasn’t eerily dark or anything like that, but it looked like the weave in the unknown domain – if they had something like the weave in the first place – was mixed with a different type of energy. No, not one energy. Different types of energy.
"Do you have enough energy stones to replenish your used-up energy a…bunch of times if you need to?" Rebecca asked at this moment.
"Yep. Michael gave me loads. I didn’t understand why at first, but I got his point. We will have to analyze these energies to find out how different they are from origin energy and if our Energy Pillars can use or convert them," Danny murmured while the spaceship traveled ahead.
The border to the unknown was even darker than the unknown’s space, and it clashed with the weave. At least, that was what it looked like to Daniel.
He hesitated for a moment when they were about to cross the border – the weave tried stopping him, almost like a mother trying to stop its child from moving out – but Daniel did it regardless. They crossed the border in one go and took in the changes.
First, Daniel noticed that his connection to the weave was temporarily severed. He could still access his Divinity, but it was more difficult to do so. On top of that, Daniel could only use the Essence accumulated within his Divinity since his access to the weave had been cut for the time being.
"So that’s why the Guardians didn’t come to check it out," Daniel nodded in understanding.
"What are you talking about?" Rebecca inquired.
"The weave is not in control of the unknown domain. For the time being, I’m not a god anymore. If anything, I’m more like a Demi-God with decent sword skills," Daniel teased, which earned a raised eyebrow from Rebecca.
"So, what you’re saying is that the unknown domain blocks your access to the weave AND weakens your Divinity? Because if the latter wasn’t the case, you would still be a full-fledged god."
Daniel nodded calmly. Something about his Divinity had been altered, preventing him from using its full potential.
"That is problematic," Rebecca mumbled, "If you encounter some sort of god using the powers of the unknown, we might die."
"It will be fine. I can protect you," Daniel winked at Rebecca, who scoffed, "I’m not that weak myself. I’m just telling you that fights against gods will be problematic. That means….you shouldn’t cause any trouble!"
Daniel rolled his eyes but proceeded to travel deeper into the unknown. It didn’t take long to locate some nearby planets, but Rebecca first wanted to scan them for intelligent life, unique plants, and so on. Daniel was certain there was some interesting plant life on all planets—if the right conditions were met—given the multitude of unique energy systems.
"I will analyze the energies. On the other hand, you can…do whatever you want, I guess," Rebecca shrugged.
Thus, that was what Daniel did. He stayed by Rebecca’s side and watched her intently as she released a few strands of origin energy to separate traces of the unknown energy systems from the domain.
It wasn’t easy, as the energies resisted her, but with enough origin energy, it worked, more or less.
Rebecca used her Soullife Arts with Analyzation to analyze the traces of energies and began mumbling in excitement.
"Neither of them have any, or many, characteristics of origin energy. But they all do something origin energy can do as well. One of the energies releases properties similar to the origin energy when used with a mind and soul refinement technique. They’re like spiritual waves if one uses old scriptures to determine what origin energy does in the mind and soul," Rebecca murmured in excitement.
"Then there is an energy that feels like a body refinement technique, after what it does to origin energy when it is altered to refine the body. The physical energy can be used to immediately refine the body by absorbing it. There is no need for a body refinement technique. That is interesting! But the last one is truly astounding as well. It releases a similar frequency as most magical phenomena. It is several times stronger and feels much more magical."
She looked at him, "I wonder if you can use it to unleash even more powerful moves.

chapters.title: Chapter 1101: Unknown Domain III - Daniel Fang
chapters.content:
Daniel was interested in the foreign energy systems. Rebecca was more excited but also vigilant of the energies around her. She sealed her body and covered her skin in an additional layer of origin energy to protect herself from potential injuries.
The three energies didn’t seem dangerous, but Rebecca didn’t want to absorb them accidentally in case her Analyzation was a mistake. Daniel, on the other hand, didn’t seal his pores. On the contrary, he opened his system to the three unknown energies. They didn’t seem dangerous to him, so he might as well experiment with them-
"This is interesting," Daniel muttered, attracting Rebecca’s attention. She turned around, only to scream at him, "Are you insane?!"
"What?" Daniel asked meekly. He was a god but Rebecca was capable of crushing his confidence instantly. All it took was a single scream.
"Why would you absorb the energies into your system if you don’t know what they may do to your energy system? I know they don’t seem dangerous, but your energy system is completely different from these three systems. What if the energies cling to your body while your energy system rejects them? This could lead to–...."
Rebecca was huffing and puffing, but Daniel could only smile faintly.
"The physical energy doesn’t do anything. I cannot absorb it. The same happens with this spiritual-attributed energy. They circulate through my energy system and can be expelled easily. It’s unfortunate that I cannot test their potency, though. I think it would be great to use those energies instead of the mind, soul, and body refinement techniques."
Rebecca sighed, "It’s good that you don’t have any issues. Still, you shouldn’t have acted so recklessly."
"I will be more careful when I do reckless things in the future," Danny smiled.
"That doesn’t reassure me, AT ALL," Rebecca cursed softly but nodded, "You’re telling me you will continue your reckless behavior. That’s okay…I guess I cannot change you either way. Let’s just say that you do this stuff out of my sight. Or…no, nevermind. Only do it when I’m there to help."
Danny’s smile widened, but Rebecca flicked his forehead.
"Let’s not talk about it. What is with this magical energy? You said the physical and spiritual ones aren’t accepted by your energy system. Does that mean the magical one has been accepted?"
"Yep. That’s about it," Daniel nodded.
The magical energy could be integrated into his energy system. It wasn’t like origin energy, but it worked decently. In fact, it didn’t work well to enhance his physical strength, not even when he used Foundation Break. That was weird, yet not really. Daniel used his Divinity with magical energy instead of Essence as an experiment. He conjured a blade with the magical energy and quickly realized that it was almost as powerful as his Essence-conjured blade.
Daniel shared his experience with Rebecca, who took note of everything in great detail.
"Tell me more about its properties. You should be able to tell me the faintest difference between origin energy, your Essence, and the magical energy. How potent is the magical energy, what is its greatest strength, and what is its biggest weakness? How can you utilize it in the most efficient way? Tell me everything, Daniel!" She exclaimed, forgetting about Danny’s reckless attitude.
She approached him with the holographic notepad in her hands. Her eyes glimmered in utter excitement, and she licked her lips as if she’d just found a delicacy.
"If you look at me like that, I won’t be able to concentrate. I’d rather tear your clothes apart and have some fun with you if you keep at it—..."
Daniel was not surprised when Rebecca punched him in the stomach. The punch wasn’t fierce, but it hurt regardless.
"Pervert," Rebecca snorted, her cheeks flushed red.
"That was a joke," He said hurriedly.
"No, it wasn’t. I know you’re not lying about stuff like that."
"Yeah. It wasn’t a joke," Danny laughed awkwardly.
"I know. So, tell me about the magical energy and its properties up to the finest detail, or there won’t be anything between us for a long time." She still blushed, but the look in her eyes told Danny how serious she was—dead serious.
That being said, Daniel focused on the serious part of their exploration mission. He told Rebecca everything he knew about the magical energy and focused on a few more aspects before she was certain the energy wouldn’t hurt her either. Rebecca proceeded to access the magical energy and absorbed it as well.
Her experiments lasted several hours, and she devised even more long-term experiments to determine how well the magical energy would integrate into the origin system if it was kept there for an extended period of time.
"Can we visit the planet now? I’m curious about the intelligent life here. Can they use all three systems, or did they awaken different energy systems? What about the monsters? How did they evolve with so many different energy systems?" Daniel asked after a while. He was truly curious. How strong were other lifeforms? Was their prowess higher if they only used one of those energies? How strong were they physically if they only used the spiritual and magical energy? What if they could only use the physical energy?
There were so many questions and only so few answers. However, Daniel was excited nonetheless. He was curious to find out more about the unknown.
"Since when have you been so excited about researching stuff? That doesn’t seem like you," Rebecca frowned deeply, but Danny only shrugged with a mysterious smile.
"Who knows? Maybe your weirdness is contagious."
"Now it is my fault you are weird? Forget it! You and Michael are much weirder than I am! Compared to you and your brother, I am an innocent lamb!"
"Innocent? Yesterday night, you were anything but innocent," Danny teased Rebecca, who punched him again.
Okay. That was deserved.
Daniel couldn’t help but smile seeing Rebecca blush like that.
He loved this woman way too much!

chapters.title: Chapter 1102: The Unknown IV - Daniel Fang
chapters.content:
Traveling to the closest planet didn’t take long. Skypiercer wasn’t stopped by any other spaceships, either, which made it even easier to enter the planet’s stratosphere and descend slowly. Daniel and Rebecca considered activating Skypiercer’s camouflage, but they decided against it when nobody stopped them.
Instead, they opened their radio for everyone. Their frequency could be accessed, allowing easy communication. However, nobody reached out to them. The unlike pair landed not long after but didn’t bother to descend right in front of the foreign intelligent lifeforms. There was no need to scare them like that.
They landed and stored Skypiercer in the War Rune storage.
"What now?" Daniel asked Rebecca, who’d already conjured the holographic notepad, to make some notes.
"Now we will research the plant life, atmosphere, and monsters. We will do the work you love so much," Rebecca winked in his direction before teasingly, "Or are you not excited anymore?"
"Oh, yeah. So…can I do the practical examination while you do the smartass part?"
"You only want to fight unknown monsters, don’t you?"
Danny shrugged, but the smile on his lips spoke more than a thousand words.
"Don’t rush into fighting Divine Beasts or the like. Who knows what will happen if the intelligent lifeforms of this planet worship these Divine Beasts? We don’t want to enrage the natives by accident."
"Our mission is to explore, not to conquer and enrage. I know that much," Daniel grumbled silently, but Rebecca glared at him again.
"Yeah, okay. I will stay here with you. If some monsters attack me, I will only defend us. Breaking a few bones is okay, but more than that is unacceptable."
"You’re a good boy~" Rebecca teased before returning her focus to work.
Daniel snickered but did the same. He inspected the trees and plant life in the surroundings and used origin energy to sense their energy systems.
"Almost all plants have one energy system, some have multiple ones," Daniel noted, "The magical energy system changes the properties of the plants, enhancing their magical nature. They evolve in a way that allows them to do ’unique’ things. That’s interesting."
"The physical energy system enhances the plants’ toughness, growth speed, and so forth. That’s not too bad either. Some plants that have both systems attain unique coping mechanisms to defend against natural predators. They’re stronger than the norm but also have unique magical abilities. Some are strong defenders, while others hide. But there are also carnivorous plants with strong abilities to attack. Following their coping mechanism, they use their attacks to intimidate enemies – or eat them right away – intimidating those around them."
"This is truly a different universe, isn’t it? Everything feels so different from the Origin Universe and the Origin Expanse," Daniel muttered, his attention pulling to a few plants with the spiritual energy system. There were only a handful of them and even fewer with multiple energy systems that contained spiritual energy. However, they felt the most unique to Daniel. It was almost like these plants were scared of him because they could sense his power and realize what it meant to be around someone powerful.
It was…like they were sentient.
"Are those…" Daniel asked, pointing at one particular flower, which seemed to writhe in agony and fear.
"Yes, it is a sentient plant. It’s incredibly rare to see something like that among low-ranked plants. In fact, I think I have never seen a sentient planet below the 4th Tier, except for Michael’s Nature Spirit. But even that was a unique find among Summons, mostly due to its connection to the Untamed Jungle’s Primordial Tree Spirit."
"This one doesn’t contain enough energy to be at the 1st Tier. Even as a Tierless plant, it would be considered rather weak," Daniel mumbled.
"Yup. That’s very interesting, isn’t it? The spiritual energy seemed to grant plants sentience and monsters more intelligence. It helps all lifeforms to develop their mind and soul much faster than the norm. The plants are still rather young but are smart enough to know how to behave around more powerful creatures. That is fascinating."
They continued testing for a while and encountered a bunch of monsters. It didn’t seem like a long time, but a day passed before they stopped their initial experiments.
"This is amazing! The energies restrain the variety of plants and monsters’ growth but allow rapid growth in specific paths. Spiritual energy allows the evolution and growth of the mind and spiritual powers, whereas physical energies do the same for the body. Physical mutations and evolutions aren’t rare. I wonder how many monsters are born and cease to exist in the following generations. This is a true treasure!"
"It’s quite interesting," Daniel agreed. They had seen many similar types of monsters, but some evolved by adapting to other energy systems. They mutated, surrendered their old energy systems, and accepted to survive. Some died, but others overcame all ordeals and procreated, creating numerous monsters from the same ancestry. The same happens to the plant life here."
"Nature here is rich in everything. This is a true heaven," Rebecca sighed. This place was extraordinary. Unfortunately, origin energy wouldn’t do this place any good. If anything, it would prevent the growth of an ecosystem with a rich variety of plants and monsters.
Origin energy was great for growing in all possible aspects, but it was much slower and didn’t allow unique mutations like the other energy systems. It was still possible to mutate in unique ways, yet the probability was much lower.
"I wonder if the unknown domain will cease to exist when the weave expands and claims this place," Daniel murmured, a tinge of sadness in his voice. Explore more stories at empire
"IF the weave manages to claim this place," Rebecca added, but Daniel could only look at her silently.
There was no ’If’. Except maybe for the weave, which did not wish to conquer the unknown domain.
"Maybe Michael can convince the weave to stay away from the unknown domain,"
"You think he will do that?"
Danny shrugged, "If the unknown domain is of no danger to the weave, he won’t do anything. The Guardians wouldn’t do anything either."
Rebecca nodded seriously.
"That means our mission is more important than expected. We have to find out whether the unknown domain is dangerous and has to be conquered or if there is no need to intercept."
"Let’s search for the natives then!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1103: The Unknown V - Daniel Fang
chapters.content:
Their first encounter with the natives of the unknown domain was unique, to put it into simple terms.
It was exhilarating when they thought about the difficulties of communicating with another race that didn’t know any of the Origin Tongues, learned more about their traditions, and how their appearance came to be – after all the three energy systems seemed to accelerate the mutation processes of all lifeforms –, and much more.
What they didn’t expect was to encounter rather ordinary-looking humanoids. The natives were taller than humans, and most of them were covered in mountains of muscles, but they didn’t look much different from Cyclops. Except maybe for the fact that they had two smaller eyes where their cheeks were. They had a massive eye with great vision, filled with the physical energy, whereas the two smaller eyes contained bits of the spiritual energy. That was interesting, but it didn’t attract their full attention.
However, what attracted their curiosity was the language they spoke.
"How mayeth we help you, straeunger?" One of the massive Cyclops, which Daniel called them in his mind, asked them as they arrived in front of their small village. A skinnier and slightly smaller young Cyclops walked to the entrance to the gate and checked on them. His eyes narrowed to tiny slits, but he nodded slowly.
"His energy system is full of the spiritual energies," Rebecca mumbled to Daniel, who nodded slowly. He sensed something washing over him when the young Cyclops looked at them. He’d used the spiritual energy to do…something.
"Our Shaman invites you to his chambre," the hulking Cyclops added without waiting for a response from them. He turned around and gestured to them to enter.
"I do not wish to be rude, but what language are you speaking?" Rebecca asked while following the Cyclops inside the tiny settlement. She, just like Danny, was much stronger than the Cyclops. There was no need to be scared of them. Even if all of them were to attack simultaneously, they wouldn’t be in danger.
Your journey continues on empire
"We speath Common. Everyone does," The Cyclops responded in confusion.
"Everyone of your kind, or…everyone on this planet?"
"All life understands Common in this realm. You speath and understandth Common as well, Sage," The Cyclops said as if it was commonly known by all beings.
Rebecca nodded slowly, ignoring the Cyclops comment about her being a ’Sage.’ Daniel had no idea what that meant, but he kept silent. He augmented his senses with Essence and checked everything and everyone thoroughly.
’There are only one hundred Cyclops in the settlement, and everyone has both the spiritual and physical energy system. However, only one of them has a more advanced spiritual system. His physical system lacks in comparison. That’s their shaman. He is the mind among the brawns,’
Daniel didn’t see more than two Cyclops with the power to rival High Awakened. Still, their physical prowess was likely to be much higher than the average High Awakened, given that they trained using physical energy only. It was more effective than origin energy in that regard.
"What do you call the energies in this…realm?" Daniel asked, interrupting Rebecca’s chat with the hulking Cyclops.
"The beings of this realm useth the earth and heaveth’s energies to pursue the pathes of Mana, Force, and Spirita." An unfamiliar voice rang out from the front. It was the Cyclops Shaman standing in the frame of his hut – the chambre – who spoke up.
"Mana, the magical energy. Force the physical energy, and Spirita for the spirutual energy," Daniel mumbled while Rebecca took some notes. The Cyclops stared at her holographic screen, their eyes widened in surprise. Given their settlement’s appearance, the Cyclops didn’t know much about technology. Daniel didn’t know if that was related to the unknown domain or if the lack of technology wasn’t as severe on other planets. It was probably the latter, as the unknown domain was much bigger than one mere planetary system.
Then again, the planetary system bordering the Origin Expanse was massive. It contained dozens of large, inhabitable, planets. There were probably hundreds of races spread across those inhabitable planets.
Still, it was important to note that the Cyclops looked ridiculous when shocked to the core. Their eyes bulged, and it looked like they were about to pop out at any moment.
"We are honored to welcometh two Sages to our humble abode," The Shaman made a weird gesture with his hands and bowed politely.
There was it again. The word. Sages
"Why do you call us ’Sages’? What do you mean by that?" Daniel asked.
"That is what you are, or am I mistaken, Your Excellency?" The Cyclops Shaman inquired, "You come from elsewhere, using foreign powers. Your power reserves arenth attunead to this placeth, creating ripples that can be sensedth all over the realm."
Daniel and Rebecca looked at each other for a moment. They understood something important at this point.
"Are there many ’Sages’? If so, are they all like us, or are they different?" Daniel asked even before Rebecca could say anything.
"I do not know abouth this, your excellency," The Cyclops Shaman said, and bowed deeply to apologize for his lack of knowledge, "Old Scripture speak of the foreign, the powerful. Howeveth, they speaketh of different powerful creatures over the courseth of the realm’s history. Many Sages cameth."
This was interesting, even if it didn’t make any sense. The unknown domain hadn’t been connected to the Origin Universe for long. There couldn’t have been any ’Sages’ from the Origin Universe. The Guardians would have known about the connection with the unknown domain.
That was how both Daniel and Rebecca concluded one thing.
Other universes were once connected to the unknown universes.
Or maybe…just maybe, they were still connected to other universes.
The unlike couple looked at each other again, a trace of worry filling their eyes.
At this point, they realized that their journey in the unknown domain had just begun.
This was just the beginning of something great.

chapters.title: Chapter 1104: Rise of the Forest Elven Tribe I
chapters.content:
"What can you tell us about your relationship with the New Primal?" A reporter of the Elven Union asked Lilica. Discover hidden tales at My Virtual Library Empire
She shifted uncomfortably on her chair and threw a glare at the Elven Elders. Until now, Lilica had no idea why they would force her to keep going with these types of interviews. Nobody was interested in them since the content of the interviews never changed. Years had passed since Michael ascended the Origin Expanse throne, yet they still asked about the New Primal.
"I have been working with the New Primal for almost one century now," Lilica sighed deeply while the Elven Elders behind the camera nodded vigorously, "I have been with him from the beginning. The EmeraldLeaf Adventurer team of the Forest Elven Tribe has been working for him since he was a Tier-1 Lord, and we established a business plan to help the New Primal valuable goods in exchange for weaponry and the like. You could say the Forest Elves were the first proper business channel of the New Primal."
Lilica cursed herself a little for almost everything she’d said but shrugged inwardly at the end. Her previous interviews hadn’t been much different than this, but she still couldn’t help but feel that they were taking advantage of Michael. And that those interviews were useless.
"Your relationship with the New Primal seems exciting. The Forest Elven Tribe must be glad to have a team like the EmeraldLeaf Adventurers in their rows," The reporter put on a professional smile, "If not for you and your colleagues, the Forest Elves would have never been able to increase their standing in the Elven Union. The New Primal’s supply of Soultrait Symbols and resources changed everything for the Forest Elven Tribe. What do you say about that? Do you think the Forest Elves deserve to be put on a pedestal with the High Elves?"
’What is wrong with that bastard?’ Lilica was having a hard time controlling her facial features. The reporter’s commentary changed from the script, his words hinting at something Lilica didn’t want to pick up.
"Would have never been able to? Deserve to be put on a pedestal?" Lilica asked in an icy tone, her eyes narrowed to tiny slits. She was still smiling professionally, but given the way the reporter flinched, Lilica must have looked scared for a moment.
The reporter didn’t say anything, but they kept recording.
"We fought with our lives on the line to protect Michael when he was still weak. He grew rapidly, but our help was essential nonetheless. Michael and the Forest Elven Tribe benefited from each other. The ’New Primal’ didn’t give us thousands of Soultrait Symbols without receiving anything in return. For the records, our trades were business-minded."
Lilica clicked her tongue and considered smashing the camera with the recording but decided against it.
"We deserve everything we’ve obtained. Many good people died fighting with Michael. Every one of the Forest Elven Adventurers knew what awaited us when we decided to fight for Michael, but we accepted the danger. The benefits of fighting for Michael were great. Of course, we accepted them. That being said, I tell you that we deserve everything we’ve acquired through our effort and the connections we’ve established with other forces throughout the last century.
The Forest Elven Tribe is, for the records, not the only race who had been in contact with Michael early on. He also worked with the Berserkers and Warlock Centaurs, helping them grow much stronger. However, not everyone gains anything from Michael. He was also in a business-minded relationship with the Valyr. They had a great relationship for a while, and Michael sold them a Beginner Region called the "Savannah." Yet, instead of working with Michael on equal standing, they tried taking advantage of his generosity."
Lilica took a deep breath, trying to control her anger.
"Since you haven’t heard of the Valyr yet, given the disgusting expression on your face, you should be smart enough to visualize that Michael’s relationship with the Valyr ended. They didn’t treat him well and demanded impossible things without giving him anything in return. In contrast, Michael likes the Forest Elves and often visits us. We are still on equal standing, according to Michael. That was literally what he said the last time he visited us. So…why are you telling us that we would have never achieved anything without his Soultrait Symbols and resources? We worked hard to achieve so much in the last century, and your words make it sound like our accomplishments aren’t worth a dime."
The reporter’s lips parted, but Lilica lifted her hand.
"As for standing on a pedestal with the High Elves. I couldn’t care less. I am not in a competition with the other Elven races of the Elven Union. They can do whatever they want if they don’t annoy me like…" She didn’t speak the last words aloud, but that wasn’t necessary. The reporter was well aware that she meant him.
***
"Don’t you think you went a little bit too far?" Elder Silram asked Lilica, who shrugged nonchalantly.
"I don’t really care. These reporters are slowly transforming into fierce flies. They’re still shitty and hover around dung but started to approach the dung of the nearby dragon just because he is hibernating."
"Calling yourself a dragon," Elder Silram clicked his tongue but smiled faintly.
He had been annoyed at the insinuations made by the last few reporters, just like his grand granddaughter.
"We have our copy of the recordings, so we shouldn’t be in trouble when someone comes visiting us to tell us off about how we’re treating the Elven Union’s reporters, but this will be annoying.
"’When’ and not ’if’?" Lilica asked, the corner of her lips curling upward.
"Yes, when. Because I know the Elven Union has been waiting for an opportunity like this. To be precise, their heads, the High Elves, have been waiting for an opportunity to crush us."
Lilica was now smiling like someone had given her a precious gift.
"They’re scared of us. Scared of getting replaced."

chapters.title: Chapter 1105: Rise of the Forest Elven Tribe II
chapters.content:
The legends of the Forest Elven Tribe spread far. They reached the outskirts of the Elven Union’s borders and reached even further. Every Elf knew about the Forest Elves’ actions and the record-breaking speed with which dozens of Forest Elves advanced to Divine Lifeforms.
Some were already powerful Forest Elves before encountering Michael, but everything changed once they received Artifacts, Soultrait Symbols, and resources of higher quality. They started progressing rapidly while their combat prowess increased exponentially. The higher their Tier, the higher the potency of their Soultrait Symbols.
That being said, gaining better technique, more resources, and Artifacts – boosting the combat prowess drastically instantly –and Soultrait Symbols boosted the Forest Elves considerably. They quickly bypassed other lower sub-races of the Elves and attained the same standing as the Common Elves. Their numbers were still much lower than the average elven race, but the average Tier and prowess of the Forest Elven was exceptional.
Many elven races ever wondered how long it would take before the Forest Elves would replace the High Elves. Nobody questioned IF the Forest Elves had the means to replace the High Elves’ position at the top of the Elven Union. No. They wondered WHEN that would be the case.
The High Elves didn’t like this. What used to be rumors about their beauty and unparalleled power among all elven races transformed into gossip about the High Elves’ replacement.
The High Elves could not accept this.
That was how an embassy of the High Elves ended up in Yggdrasil.
**
"The production of your Mangunias, Lilituthyn, and Bloodwelk is not up to standard. I know you are struggling because your neighbors are being a hassle, but we deployed a force of Super Awakened to help you with that. The Super Awakened reported to me that the neighbors aren’t as powerful as you described them to be and that they are also not violent. They were more than willing to talk to the Super Awakened even before they released their energy," Lilica commented in displeasure. Continue your saga on .Côm
Her expression was filled with frustration while the Forest Elven Lord pressed his lips together. The young Lord didn’t even dare to look into Lilica’s face. He stared at the ground as if the weed before him could cover his shame.
"There is no need to be afraid of me or anyone here. But you shouldn’t lie to me. Nobody likes liars. In the first place, lying to us even after I told you that I would deploy the Super Awakened is not the smartest move." She sighed deeply. You will have to cover the cost of the Teleportation Tokens. Our treasury won’t cover the cost of wasted resources, and you know that."
The young Lord paled and was about to say something when someone appeared before her. Another forest elf, a young woman, emerged from a small portal, her face covered in thick beads of sweat.
"What is wrong, Elenia?" Lilica turned away from the young Elven Lord, who breathed in relief. It might be bad to be forced to pay back the cost of the Teleportation Tokens, but Lilica’s judgmental gaze was several times worse, "Did something happen?"
"The High Elves are here," Elenia, the female Forest Elves, said between two breaths, "They’ve challenged us for the position of the trading representative of the Elven Union!"
Lilica tilted her head, trying to digest what was going on.
"Lilica, get your act together, please!" Elenia exclaimed, seeing Lilica like that, "The High Elves issued and challenged us officially. Elder Silram and the other Elven Elders accepted the challenge. If we lose, we won’t be allowed to trade with the New Primal anymore. The High Elves will replace us in the trading business with Michael Fang and everyone else."
"Why in the Devil’s name would my grandfather and the Elders accept this?!" Lilica couldn’t control the outburst of her emotions for a moment.
A shockwave of origin energy splashed into Elenia’s face while the young Elven Lord was hurled backward, but Lilica didn’t notice that.
