"Calm down for a second. Please!" Elenia squealed. She took a deep breath and explained everything important, "The Elders accepted the deal because the wager was the seat at the top of the Elven Union. We will replace the High Elves if we win this challenge."
Lilica cursed, "So the Elders accepted, thinking we will never receive an opportunity like this again? Are they stupid?! They know better than anyone that we need more time…"
Elenia shrugged, but her expression told us that she understood the situation as well as Lilica. They were in trouble.
"What kind of challenge is it? Is it a one versus one, a raid, a multi-combat challenge?" Lilica asked, while pointing to the portal, "Whatever it is, let’s go first… before we’re too late."
Elenia nodded. She turned to the portal, reached for Lilica’s hand, and grasped it tightly before jumping through it.
The space around them twisted, and they appeared before Yggdrasil, where all official challenges of the Forest Elves were held.
"It’s a best of five," Elenia said when they emerged from the portal.
’A best of five isn’t too bad. If I can call Mika and…,’ Lilica could think no more because her mind went blank.
Lilica could see Fineon, one of the stronger Forest Elves, lying on the ground in a small arena that must have been created a few minutes ago. He was writhing in pain and was having a hard time breathing. His arms and legs were mangled, and blood gushed out of a large cut in his stomach. If Fineon wasn’t a Divine Lifeform, he would be as good as dead at this point.
However, nobody stepped forward to say anything. A young-looking woman put her foot on Fineon’s chest and pressed her heel deep into it.
"Are you giving up?" The woman asked coldly, but Fineon didn’t utter a word. His lips parted, but no word escaped his lips.
The others couldn’t see much, but Lilica frowned deeply when she discovered threads of lifeforce getting pulled out of Fineon. Michael had done something similar in the past. He extracted the lifeforce of his enemies and absorbed it. The woman did the same.
She had flawless skin, was as fair as a fairy, and had familiar silky, silver hair, vibrant emerald-colored eyes, and long, pointed ears. She looked like the perfect example of a High Elf—after all, the woman was a High Elf.
Fineon was on the verge of dying, but nobody seemed to notice that. All the spectators could tell was that Fineon struggled to stay in the arena, trying to fight for his people.
"He’s surrendering. You can stop now," Lilica intervened. The Elven Elders said something, but Lilica’s deadly glare was enough to seal their lips.
The woman looked at her momentarily and nodded, "That was a good decision. It would have been a shame to kill one of your few Divine Lifeforms."
Lilica ignored the High Elf and gestured to the Forest Elven healer to tend to Fineon and bring him back to the infirmary.
"Will you be my next opponent?" The High Elf asked Lilica.
"You can fight again?" Lilica asked? "Don’t tell me you want to fight three times in a row?"
The High Elf smiled lightly.
"I don’t know. Do I want to fight that often? No. Do I think I’m strong enough to beat the shit out of the Forest Elves who have been too full of themselves for a while now? Definitely."
The other High Elves – Lilica hadn’t noticed them until now – laughed and made a few more jokes, but Lilica merely nodded.
"That’s good then," She stepped into the arena, "There is no need to waste more time than necessary. Taking out trash like you shouldn’t take long."

chapters.title: Chapter 1106: Rise of the Forest Elven Tribe III
chapters.content:
The fight between the High Elf, Belleanis – also known as Bella –, and Lilica started immediately. They were roughly at the same Tier, but Bella was much faster than Lilica.
She conjured two Dagger Artifacts in her hands and charged forward. Her feet didn’t even touch the ground anymore when she used her Soultrait to accelerate. Gusts of wind swirled around Bella’s feet, allowing her to walk on the wind, just like a windwalker.
’So one Soultrait is Windwalker or something eerily similar to such a Soultrait.’ Lilica noted. She was already aware that Bella had at least two Soultraits. One that allowed her to drain the lifeforce of her targets and Windwalker. That wasn’t too great, given that the High Elf seemed to possess a Soullife Arts and Soul Techniques for both Soultraits. She was still a Lord, whereas Lilica was a Subordinate.
She twisted her body to an uncomfortable degree, evading a series of attacks, and summoned a shortsword in her hand when Bella’s dagger was about to stab her in the neck. That was a little deadlier than Lilica had hoped, but it was still fine.
She released a burst of energy and exerted both Silent Reaper and Invisibility. Silent Reaper didn’t evolve even after it was upgraded to 7-Star. It grew a lot stronger, but that was about it. However, Invisible Projectiles evolved into Invisibility once it reached 8-Star. Lilica had been worried that upgrading Invisible Projectiles would waste time and resources, but Michael was certain the Soultrait would transform into something incredibly powerful.
That was exactly what happened. Invisibility could be applied to her body, clothes, and almost everything else, including her Artifacts and projectiles. Combined with Silent Reaper, which concealed her energy fluctuations, vibrations, and sounds, and once upgraded to 7-Star, even her scent.
Her invisibility allowed her to skulk throughout the arena, retrieving her Legendary Bow Artifact and quiver filled with rare, high-quality arrows. Lilica was calm and composed, which was the complete opposite of Bella. Bella charged around the arena, trying to find Lilica. She released bursts of energy in all directions, trying to find the faintest hints of her presence.
"Show yourself, you forest whore!!!" Bella roared when she couldn’t find Lilica right away. Her cheeks flushed red in anger, and her energy burst out even stronger and farther.
’Does she really think something like that will work, or is she worked up that easily? Maybe she is just scared of me? Of the rumors about me and my people? The legends revolving around the Super Awakened Michael has trained. Even if we, Forest Elves, aren’t that well known, everyone knows the Super Awakened created by Michael. Everyone knows what the New Primal has achieved.’
At last, Bella’s energy shockwaves located Lilica, but it was already too late.
Lilica finished her preparations a few seconds prior and was ready to release it all.
Weakness Detection, which evolved into Weakness Exploitation once it was upgraded a few times, had been activated, locating six weak spots in Bella’s defense. Lilica nocked a strong arrow on the bow, pulled the string back, and activated Bullseye and Rupture. Bullseye’s potency skyrocketed after it was upgraded. It was even stronger than it used to be. In the meantime, Rupture was a powerful Soultrait that applied to blades or sharp objects. Once applied, the wounds inflicted through the blades and sharp objects would rupture, inflicting even more damage than usual.
Lilica replicated Mika’s Rapid Fire Soultrait by using Foundation Break – a gift from Michael – to increase her physical characteristics drastically for a moment. That was enough to release a series of six invisible arrows.
Lilica undid her invisibility and stored the Legendary Bow Artifact the instant the arrows left the bowstring. She waved happily and looked around with a smirk as the invisible projectiles found their target. They collided with the High Elf’s skin, pierced her wrists, elbows, and what Lilica presumed to be old wounds picked up by Weakness Exploitation and inflicted great damage.
The High Elf screamed in pain as Rupture did its wonders. The arrows ruptured through the High Elf, forcing her to the ground the instant her weak spots were hit. She screamed like there was no tomorrow as Lilica approached her. Bella used her Drain Soultrait, but it was to no avail.
"I figured your lifeforce draining Soultrait required you to injure me. Sorry, but that doesn’t work for me," Lilica said while releasing her energy to crush the High Elf. It was interesting how easily some Divine Lifeforms could be defeated. Lilica didn’t expect all six arrows to hit the target. Then again, her Legendary Bow Artifact had several enchantments and a special feature that increased the projectiles’ velocity by a few times as long as enough energy was supplemented.
That was what Lilica had done to quickly release a series of six arrows. It worked out well, and Bella was done. Threads of energy pulled the arrows out, but Lilica wasn’t careful. She used as much force as possible to worse the damage to Bella as she pulled the arrows out.
"The arrows are poisoned. If you don’t drink the antidote within half an hour, you will be dead. You better give up now," Lilica said lightly, but the fear in Bella’s eyes was real.
"I…I surrender…"
She stuttered while raising her hands to plead for the antidote. Lilica snickered and retrieved a glass vial filled with water. Bella took it in a hurry and swallowed the content. She didn’t feel anything, but it wasn’t like she had been feeling sick or poisoned in the first place.
That was because Bella was never poisoned in the first place. Lilica said she would make sure Bella surrendered and warned her friends.
Read new adventures at .Côm
Lilica reached for Bella’s collar and hurled her across the arena without care. She landed heavily before her friends, who threw a descending look at the woman they’d praised and joked with just a minute ago.
"Who is next? I don’t have all day to finish this nonsense."

chapters.title: Chapter 1107: Rise of the Forest Elven Tribe IV
chapters.content:
Defeating a Divine Lifeform was never supposed to be easy. It was even less likely for a greater race to lose to an inferior race when they were at the same rank.
Forest Elves were always known as a superior race. They weren’t even stronger than Lesser Humans. On the contrary, High Elves were on par with Hyumans. Some of them were strong enough to reach the threshold of a god. They formed a Divinity and left the realm of the High Elves to pursue greater goals.
Everyone had always said that. The truth, however, was that the High Elven gods were too afraid to stay with their race. They left their people because they were afraid of the Primal. Even now that the Primal had returned to their original purpose and form as the Guardians of the Origin, the High Elven Gods never returned.
Either they were dead or hiding somewhere, still afraid of potential trouble. What IF someone like the Primal would return or the Guardians would transform into the Primal again? The High Elven Gods didn’t want to take the risk.
Lilica had known about that for a while. She knew everything about the High Elven Gods because Michael told her everything. She had asked Michael about the High Elven Gods, who asked other Gods about it. Yet, nobody had ever heard of the High Elven Gods. It was almost like they never existed in the first place. Like…they ceased to exist moments after attaining godhood.
The High Elves wanted to distract from the loss of their gods or their disappearance by ruling the Elven Union with a strong hand. They wanted to dominate the Elven Union and crush everyone threatening their control. The Forest Elves weren’t even trying to usurp the High Elves’ position at the throne of the Elven Union, but the Elven Elders were at an all-time high. The Forest Elves were stronger than ever and wanted to pursue greater heights.
That was how everything ended in this mess. It was troublesome. Lilica didn’t like that the High Elves came to challenge them officially or that the Elven Elders accepted the challenge and the wager. The Elven Elders were full of themselves after everything Lilica and her people had achieved and desired more.
"If you wish to end the challenge, we can do that too. We can end the challenge in a draw and develop a better solution," Lilica said.
Stay connected with .Côm
"What are you talking about?" One of the Elven Elders thundered, but Lilica didn’t allow anyone to speak with her like that. A quarter of a second passed, and Lilica retrieved a spear and hurled it between the Elven Elder’s legs with great force. The spear disappeared into the ground until only a few centimeters of its shaft jut from the ground.
"Shut up and listen carefully, Giltor," Lilica growled, "We didn’t sacrifice our lives to claim the Elven Union’s throne. We did so to improve our lives and grow strong enough to protect this place. I don’t care how selfish you are and that you ’want’ to be at the top of the Elven Union. You should keep your lips sealed if you cannot fight for it on your own, which you can’t because you are the weakest among the Elven Elders. Or I will shut your mouth for you!"
She didn’t turn around right away, "As for the spear. You know damn well that I missed intentionally. The next time you talk nonsense around me, the spear will hit. I don’t care if you die. Maybe that would make my life a lot easier!"
Elder Giltor swallowed hard. His cheeks were beet-red, but he dared not utter a single sound. Lilica was dead serious. Everyone was aware of that. Even the High Elves could tell that Lilica wasn’t joking around.
She turned to the High Elves with a heavy sigh, "Do you want to keep going? If you lose, you will lose your spot at the top of the Elven Union."
She looked at one of them, "You must be the crown prince. Did you know that bringing the Empyreal Sigil during an official match means that you possess the authority of the High Elven Empress? You must have known about that, otherwise, you wouldn’t have come here to claim our trading rights with the New Primal. Or did you think your mother would come to your rescue if you were to lose this official challenge, which you didn’t expect until I turned up."
The High Elves present weren’t the strongest among their people. They were youngsters who had advanced to Divine Lifeforms only a few decades ago. Most were still Tier-7 Awakened and far away from becoming Demi Gods. The Empress was already a Demi-God and would have been a much better choice if they challenged any elven races for anything. But she wasn’t present. However, the crown prince and his ’friends’ were present wit the Empyreal Sigil. That was why the Elven Elders of the Forest Elven Tribe accepted the challenge in the first place.
They were confident Llica and her people could deal with the Tier-7 High Elves and claim the throne while the Empress wasn’t present.
"What would happen if I were to inform the High Elven Empress about your actions?"
The crown prince paled. The last traces of color in his face were drained, and his eyes bulged in terror as the words streamed out of Lilica’s lips.
"Your mother knows nothing about this," Lilica sighed deeply and turned to the Elven Elders, "What do you think the High Elf Empress would say about this? Would she be like, ’Ohh, my son stole my Empyreal Seal and challenged you officially? Do I have to give up my throne now? Of course, I will surrender my throne to you guys. I don’t care.’ Don’t kid yourself. She will be furious and would much rather eliminate the Forest Elven Tribe before she would be willing to surrender her throne."
Suddenly, a silver portal opened behind the High Elves, and a middle-aged High Elf stepped out. She looked just like the crown prince and smiled at Lilica.
"You are a smart woman. Unfortunately, you’re not a High Elf, otherwise, I would have made you my daughter-in-law," She said, still smiling vibrantly.
But at the same time, a heavy fist crashed into the crown prince’s face, crushing his nose and jaw simultaneously.
"You’re too good to marry an idiot like this, though. What a shame."

chapters.title: Chapter 1108: Rise of the Forest Elven Tribe V
chapters.content:
"The High Elf Queen is in Ygdra? What is she doing here?" Mika’s eyes narrowed to tiny slits when Elenia appeared before him. Mika had no idea what Elenia wanted from him since it was not like he could defeat a Demi-God with his power. He was a powerful Divine Lifeform, but that was about it. No matter how much he wanted to defeat the High Elven Queen, Mika was too weak.
"She…She’s with Lilica!" Elenia exclaimed, and her facial features didn’t leave any doubt that something bad was about to happen or that it had already happened.
"Let’s go!" Mika shouted, reaching for Elenia’s hand before dragging her through her portal.
Elenia was about to say something else, but they had already emerged on the other side. They arrived on a higher plateau of Yggdrasil, which Mika ignored as he spread his senses into the surroundings. His energy flooded in all directions, engulfing a portion of the world tree – that was a taboo, but Mika couldn’t care less at this moment – and found Lilica, the Elven Elders, and the High Elves in no time.
He rushed down a small staircase that spiraled around the world tree, rushed over a massive branch, and entered the world tree without hesitation. Mika reached the royal guest chamber of Yggdrasil in no time and smashed the door open.
Lilica and the Forest Elven Elders looked around to surprise, and a dark cloud shrouded Lilica’s eyes when she saw Mika, who’d already summoned his bow and several arrows. Mika was ready to fight with his life on the line if that was necessary to rescue Lilica.
’Was that a mistake?’ He wondered momentarily and stored the bow and arrow in a hurry when Lilica’s gaze fell upon him.
"You have loyal friends. I’m not sure if I would have been brave enough to charge into the royal chambers of a Demi-God when I was his age or Tier. He sure holds you dearly," The High Elven Queen said to Lilica after taking a sip of Arcane Nectar Tea.
Mika’s lips parted but closed quickly when he sensed looming around him. Lilica didn’t like what he had done. That much was certain.
"Eh…I…I apologize for interrupting your…tea time(?)" Mika stuttered, his attention diverting to the Elven Elders as if trying to say What the hell is going on here?
However, the Elven Elders weren’t very helpful either. If anything, they were even worse off than Mika.
"There is no need to apologize. I was praising you for trying to protect your friend. I would have loved to have friends like you when I was younger. No, it would have been great if I still had friends like you," She glared at the crown prince and added with some venom, "Or a son like you. Someone ready to jump into danger for the sake of his beloved. That is much better than having an idiot as a son."
She shook her head and sighed again. A sip of the Arcane Nectar Tea helped her calm but didn’t disperse the turmoil of emotions sweeping through her body. She was too agitated about her son’s actions and attitude to leave like this, not without punishing him first.
"My son stole the Empyreal Seal and used it to authorize an official challenge, which I never agreed to," She cleared her throat and smiled at Lilica, "How about we end this challenge in a draw?"
The Elven Elders were about to say something, but Lilica raised her hand and cut them off before they could utter a single noise.
"I would like to end the challenge, yes. There is no need for any more bloodshed among the elven races. We should work together against our enemies…together to improve our lives and regain the former glory of the Ancient Elves."
The High Elven Queen smiled at that, "You are every mother-in-law’s dream. I agree with you. Combining our forces again has been overdue for a long time. The last Queens and Kings were a little bit…old-fashioned, but I hope you don’t think badly of me because of their actions."
Neither Lilica nor Mika and most other Divine Lifeforms of the Forest Elves had been around the old High Elven Kings and Queens, but that mattered little. Important was only that the current Queen was more than willing to reunite the Elves.
Continue your adventure at .Côm
"How about this…" The High Elven Queen thought about it briefly and added, "I will give you these idiots to do whatever you need them to do for the next….two decades? No, for the next 50 years. That should be enough time for them to realize how stupid their actions were."
The crown prince and his entourage wanted to say something, but they didn’t dare. The Queen had full control of them, just like Lilica controlled the Forest Elven Elders.
"In exchange, I would like to start with the reunification," She cleared her throat and stretched out one hand to Lilica, "Do you want to become my right hand? Are you willing to work with me for a better livelihood for all Elves across the universe?"
The crown prince and his entourage jumped up from their seats, and even the Forest Elven Elders stared in shock at the High Elven Queen.
Even Mika was surprised, but he looked at Lilica instead.
Lilica should have been surprised—even more shocked than everyone else—but the contrary was the case. Lilica was eerily calm and nodded slowly.
"I agree," She answered simply, reaching out to the High Elven Queen’s hand to shake it.
The deal was sealed, and both women were more than satisfied with the outcome.
They understood the meaning of today’s deal.
It was the beginning of something great.
The beginning of a chance.
A change that would alter the future of all elves forever.
Lilica would be known as the first Queen of the United Elves not even a century later. The first Elven Queen who wasn’t born a High Elf.

chapters.title: Chapter 1109: Rise of a New Era I
chapters.content:
"Is it really okay if we leave?" Tiara asked Michael, tears welling in her eyes.
Michael looked at the Silverfang Princess and smiled at her. Tiara had been with him from the day he entered the Origin Expanse. She stood by his side and fought with her life on the line. There was no hesitation in her actions, no matter how dangerous the given task had been.
She was a truly precious person to Michael. That was even more reason why he couldn’t keep her in the Untamed Jungle. Tiara deserved to be free. She deserved to take care of her people and rule them.
"My decision didn’t change in the last two decades," Michael snickered, "You and the Silverfangs are free to go. It won’t be possible to release the Silverfang Summons because they died once and won’t be allowed back into the weave – the weave would repel them, destroying them once and for all – but the Awakened can return to the cosmos."
Michael had been discussing this day with Tiara, Caesus, and the Silverfangs for a while now. Now that Caesus and Tiara accepted each other—that was about time—they could rule together. Of course, it was difficult to rule an entire race as siblings, and it was obvious that there would be many difficulties, but Michael helped the siblings come to a satisfying solution. Stay connected via .Côm
Only approximately 14,000 Silverfangs were left, most of which were children or youngsters who had been given birth to in the last two decades. The rest were already older and stronger. Some were already too old and would probably die of old age, but that was the curse of a mortal life.
Either way, the 14,000 Silverfang Awakened – some weren’t properly Awakened but had been forced to awaken their Energy Pillars to remain in the Origin Expanse – would be allowed to leave the Origin Expanse. They would return to the cosmos, where Kaleb Zenovia had already found a suitable planet. The planet wasn’t massive, but it could be inhabited by more than three billion Silverfangs, according to the HSOL(Human Standard Of Living).
It was likely the Silverfangs would have more issues inhabiting the planet with three billion of their kin, but it would take a very long time to reach that number in the first place. The surrounding planets of the small planetary system were also not inhabited by intelligent life and thus perfect for the Silverfangs. No other Demi-Human races would attack them, exiling them from their homes. It was perfect.
It would be difficult to leave the Untamed Jungle and build your own lives as a community of the Silverfangs on a foreign planet, but 14,000 Silverfangs, most with great experience and wisdom, would make it happen. Michael never doubted that, especially with Tiara following them to take care of everything. She would protect her people and ensure everyone would have a great life.
In the worst-case scenario, Tiara and the Silverfangs could always tap into their resources within the Origin Expanse. They weren’t exiled from the Origin Expanse, and Michael reassured them that they could take as many resources as needed to establish their first town. In the first place, using the Origin Expanse’s resources was a must. It would cut so much wasted time and allow everyone to focus on the most important tasks.
However, at the same time, Michael didn’t allow them to do as they pleased. There were more than a hundred thousand Silverfang Summons at this point, yet they didn’t have a territory in the Origin Expanse. They would have to request resources from Michael if they needed help. Tiara and the others didn’t pay that much attention because they liked working for him and thought it was only obvious that they had to keep working for him as a sign of gratitude. However, Michael didn’t think like that.
If the Silverfangs desired independence, they had to leave the Untamed Jungle and establish their own territory. That was what Caesus would do. He, his children, and the Silverfang Summons would leave the Untamed Jungle to establish a Silverfang territory. The Silverfang Awakened would erect their anchors in the Silverfang territory. Tiara would gain more access to all systems than anyone else since Caesus and Tiara would rule together, but Michael wouldn’t do much more.
This was a new beginning for the Silverfangs, and Michael wanted to ensure that the Silverfang Tigerfolk would make it happen. They wouldn’t have to depend on him to live their own lives anymore!
"You want us to leave, don’t you?" Tiara grumbled, but Michael shook his head.
"I don’t want you to leave, but I can tell that you are not fully happy with your life," Michael said while raising his hand to stop Tiara from responding, "I know you are happy, and I can tell that you are satisfied with your life as it is. However, I can also see the longing in your eyes and the desires within the Links of Loyalty. Your Link of Loyalty is even stronger than the others, so please don’t start lying to me. That wouldn’t help anyone. If anything, it would pain me."
Tiara winced, the hair of her fluffy tail standing up to its end.
"I shouldn’t lie…I know. I also know you don’t want us to leave. I don’t want to leave either…" Tiara mumbled.
"Buuut," Michael added, putting on a nice smile.
"But, I am also responsible for my people. I should leave…and I think I’m up for it. I think I can do it," Tiara added, her voice slowly gaining confidence, "and I think I would be good at it."
Michael nodded, "I know you will be a good Queen. You have what it takes to rule an entire race. You always had it within you."
Tears trickled down Tiara’s face, and she rushed forward to embrace him tightly.
Michael returned the tight hug and patted the back of her head.
"You will be a great Queen. Just make sure you won’t bully your people too much!"
"I’m not a bully!"
"Yes, yes. You’re the best!"

chapters.title: Chapter 1110: Rise of a New Era II
chapters.content:
"So…what’s the grand plan?" Legion tapped his feet impatiently as he looked around. He tried to tone down his voice, but the excitement filling his entire being was too much. He could hardly control himself at this point.
He looked left and right but didn’t see anything amiss. At the horizon in the north, he could pinpoint a forest with mostly white trees and golden leaves. South was a small elevation leading up to a massive mountain range. The mountain range attracted Legion because he saw several monsters climbing it—they had to be massive for him to pinpoint them from his location, yet Tiara didn’t allow him to leave the others behind and go hunt.
Other than the mountain range, a large sea, maybe even an ocean, connected the forest and the mountain range in the west, whereas the east was a massive plains region.
"First, we must pick a proper location to establish the town. It needs to be big enough to expand into a city and maybe even the capital of our kingdom," Tiara murmured.
It had only been a few hours since Michael brought them to Tiagro, a medium-sized planet in a small planetary system, in a backwater galaxy, yet everyone was already nervous. Everyone knew what they had to do since everyone had been given multiple tasks to complete in the first few days of their arrival, but nobody had moved away from their current location.
Instead, they gathered and emptied their War Rune storages to double, triple, and quadruple-check if everything they needed was there. It was only obvious, but they didn’t forget anything important. Even if they did, they could enter the Origin Expanse, anchor in Tiagro, and get what they’d forgotten.
"The location is crucial. We need a water source for drinking, farming, and possibly even transportation. The latter is not crucial in the early stages of our development, but it will be necessary in a few centuries. The sea, or ocean over there, seems like a good source for transportation and probably fishing. We have purification stones to put into barrels and purify contaminated water sources as well. That being said, the sea shouldn’t be an ocean. If it is an ocean, we can procure everything necessary to transform the salty ocean into drinkable water," An elderly Silverfang, Elder Tigris, clarified.
It should have been simple, but this was different from the Origin Expanse. Their future progress depended on this decision.
"The plains should be fertile enough for agriculture. We shouldn’t have a problem procuring food in the near future, though I hope Caesus won’t have many issues finding a suitable piece of land in the Origin Expanse. It would be best if we could feed our children mana-rich food. They will grow up much better, and more children will manifest a War Rune."
Tiara nodded slowly. She couldn’t tell how fast her brother would be, but she trusted him. No matter how much she hated him, Tiara knew that he would keep his word. He would much rather die than be the reason his people starved to death. There might still be some problems between them, but they could solve everything in the near future.
"We can procure wood, stone, and different metals from the mountain range and the woods as well. The mountain range and woods might be a little bit far apart, but we have many High Awakened with speed-boosting Soultraits. In the worst case, they can transform into their Animus shape and have some fun traveling across the plains. Their War Rune storages will be more than enough to store lots of wood and stone. As for the ores that can be found in the mountain range…the future will tell us."
"That means we already have the resources to expand the town with more buildings and tools and to construct various defenses. The only problem is…" Legion tilted his head, "We have little to no natural protection. The mountain range and ocean can protect us from two sides, but the mountain range has massive monsters, and we don’t know much about the dangers of the water. There might be an Ocean Dragon or something along those lines."
Tiara raised an eyebrow, "There is no Divine Beast on Tiagro or the entire planetary system, as a matter of fact. Michael scanned the entire planet while Kaleb quadruple-checked everything. It old him that won’t be necessary, but who am I to tell him what to do."
Master Tigris sighed deeply, "Who are you to tell him what he’s supposed to do? Well, you are the woman he loves."
"I don’t love him and never will!" Tiara hissed, but she turned around and nibbled on her lower lip a moment later. She had no time for a romantic fairytale. There was no time for love. Not right now, at least.
"Just think about it and tell him how you truly feel when you’re ready," Master Tigris added, "Your excellency."
Tiara was about to say something but shook her head.
"We’re going to settle down here. Michael and…Kaleb…picked a good starting position for our new home. For the New Era of the Silverfangs Tigerfolk!"
"They sure did," Legion nodded, "The energy density here is excellent, and we have everything we need nearby. They did a great job."
He cleared his throat, "Kaleb is such a nice guy…"
"Shut up and get to work! Search the water for dangers and check the monsters in the mountain range," Tiara hissed. Your next journey awaits at .Côm
"But-..."
"NOW!"
"Yes, Your Highness…"
"Do you have something else to say, Master Tigris?!" Tiara’s head flicked to the old Silverfang, who snickered in response.
"I know you will do fine. Let’s make sure we have everything we need to defend those who can’t protect themselves. Constructing the settlement will take a while, but we should have no problem erecting the defenses you and Michael’s subjects prepared before the departure."
Tiara nodded slowly, half-relieved that Master Tigris didn’t mention anything about Kaleb, half-worried that she wanted to hear others talk more about the young patriarch of the Zenovia house.

chapters.title: Chapter 1111: Rise of a New Era III
chapters.content:
It felt a little weird to build a massive palisade around the settlement when there was not yet a single building to protect. Thousands of tents had been erected in no time. Enjoy new adventures from .Côm
Tiara and the Silverfangs might have the resources to build all necessary structures to create a properly working settlement, but it wasn’t like they had enough space to store hundreds if not more than a thousand buildings, in their War Rune storages. That was also why they ended up building only the most important structures in the Origin Expanse before they stored them in the War Rune storages. They retrieved them to establish the smithy, a stone quarry, an infirmary, and so forth as quickly as possible.
There was no need for them to rush into anything, but the Silverfang Tigerfolk wanted to push their development past the Bronze Age on day two. They wanted to be on the same level as the Tritan Alliance within a few months.
That wasn’t going to be easy, but they had the means. It was only a matter of effort, teamwork, and a trace of luck needed to finish everything.
"Did you finish measuring the settlement?" Tiara asked a young Silverfang, who had been running around with his 1-Star Soultrait, [Number Genius]. Michael had offered to remove the Soultrait Symbol, but the young Silverfang embraced his Soultrait. It was only a 1-Star Soultrait and already had the ’Genius’ term in its name. Maybe it would evolve into a more powerful Soultrait in the future, which could then be fused with another Soultrait…or act as the foundation of other Soultraits that required calculations.
The young Awakened nodded, but he tilted his head at some point, "Some measurements are a little bit odd, like the mana density, but that is probably owed to the natural treasures underground. It could also be because of some underground monsters. We might have to pay more attention to the measurements in the near future, Your Highness."
The Silverfang bowed deeply toward Tiara, who ruffled through the kid’s hair, "Don’t be so stiff. I am still the same woman as before, even though I am now officially your Queen. You’re still the same annoying brat."
The kid stiffened for a moment but raised his upper body again and smiled shyly.
"Tell Master Tigris about your discovery and help him expand the defense system. We need to be prepared for the worst-case scenario, though I don’t think anything bad will happen," Tiara said, still smiling, "I think we’re living on a great star. Tiagro will be our greatest fortune!"
The young Silverfang nodded vigorously and disappeared behind a few tents.
Tiara smiled at that but turned around quickly, her expression furrowed.
"The sightlines around the settlement are clear. There shouldn’t be anything to worry about with discovering avian monsters and land-based monsters early on. But underground…that sounds like a hassle," She scratched the back of her head but nodded again as if to reassure herself, "Master Tigris will install more defensive measurements, and he’s smart enough to configure the radars as well. The defense shouldn’t be an issue. None of my subjects will die here!"
Tiara cleared her mind and moved onward. Now that the defense had been taken care of and a location to establish the settlement had been chosen, she could take care of the next point on her to-do list: the food supply.
Since the settlement’s survival depended on a steady food source, Tiara had to take care of that soon enough. Of course, the Origin Expanse would become their best source of food in the future, but Tiara wanted to leave the option to supply their needs with goods on Tiagro open. If Caesus was too slow to produce food for them, they would have to take care of that issue on their own…or ask Michael.
The latter was still an option, but Tiara would much rather take care of that issue on her own rather than request aid from Michael a few weeks after leaving him. Michael prepared enough food for the Silverfang Tigerfolk to last two months. Their War Rune Storages were filled to the brim with delicacies – food that was not only rich in mana, but also nutrients, and other useful properties(including illness-repelling properties)
She didn’t want to be a loser before Michael. Thus, it was time to deal with the food supply.
"Should we first clear land for farming and then plant wheat and barley crops? No, we need to analyze the soil first and find out what season it is. We also need to find out more about Tiagro’s seasons. Maybe it has more or different seasons as the Origin Expanse," Tiara mumbled, "That is a bit troublesome. We might not be able to start with farming until we’ve analyzed everything of importance. Or we do it nonetheless and try our best to adapt to the situation, but that isn’t ideal."
There was also the possibility of establishing livestock farms for meat, milk, wool, and the like. There were more than enough monsters in the vicinity, but they didn’t have the means to feed them just yet. Or they would have to feed them with the resources prepared by Michael and have less for themselves to use.
"We can start hunting and fishing. That leaves more important facilities to construct to preserve everything. Granaries are the easiest to build for the foods we want to preserve, and we can use the emergency energy-fueled fridges and freezers for medicine and the like…"
Tiara nodded slowly. The conditions weren’t perfect, given that they lacked knowledge and understanding of Tiagro and their current location, but Legion would solve some issues by researching the mountain range and sea. If there were some massive monsters that could be hunted, they shouldn’t have any issues feeding 14,000 Silverfangs.
Tiara forwarded a few commands and moved on to the next step on her to-do list.
It was not yet late in the day. Therefore, they could start building the most basic infrastructure. Some more complex structures had already been pre-manufactured and placed once the palisades were anchored in the ground, but the basics had to be constructed first.
Tiara joined the construction, though she struggled a lot.
She was great at commanding, planning, and, most importantly, fighting, but she wasn’t good at building things.
Destruction was her fort, not creation.

chapters.title: Chapter 1112: Rise of a New Era IV
chapters.content:
One of the most important basic structures that had yet to be built was the settlement’s manor. It acted as the center of the government, where all authorities would meet to discuss important decisions and various other crucial topics.
The Silverfangs weren’t fans of a manor and desired to brag about a palace built for their Queen with their hands. To their misfortune, constructing a massive, majestic palace wasn’t feasible at this point. Therefore, the small and cozy manor was built within a few hours.
Most basic structures were made from stone and wooden logs. They would last decades if necessary, which wouldn’t be the case. The Silverfangs would soon expand their settlement and tear down the old manor to replace it with something much greater. The same could be said about the homes of settlers. All Silverfangs needed housing.
They had tents to sleep in for a while, which wasn’t too bad given the cozy beds and the surrounding environment’s conditions. It was summoner and fairly warm even as the suns disappeared behind the horizon. Most High Awakened weren’t sleepy even after the sun had disappeared for hours. They didn’t go to sleep right away. Instead, they used illumination stones to light the entire settlement and continued constructing wooden huts.
The smithy, which had already been built beforehand, was also put to use. Tiara and others brought some ores and ingots from the Origin Expanse to shape into nails, pikes, hinges, and so forth. A mill to process grain was also constructed, even though the Silverfangs knew it wouldn’t be used for a while. Still, they followed a rough lineout to create a fully functioning and highly efficient infrastructure right from the start.
Even if that wasn’t necessary since most buildings would be torn down in the future, everyone felt more comfortable knowing where certain buildings had to go and how much space they had to leave to avoid obstructing others with noises and the like.
Stay tuned for updates on .Côm
Roads were also necessary, but two Silverfang Awakened with Earth-attributed Soultraits dealt with that easily. One of them could control and shape stones to a certain degree, which created a great symbiosis. One of the Silverfangs created the streets’ frames by compressing the earth where the streets were supposed to be, while the other Silverfang retrieved countless cobblestone bricks, which he shapeshifted slightly to fit perfectly into the street cove, created by compressing earth.
The streets weren’t perfect just yet, but they were quickly constructed and highly efficient. There have been no issues with the streets in Tiagro for a while now.
"Your Highness!" Legion returned from his trip to the sea and the mountain range early in the morning. He was tired and covered in crimson blood – not his – and smiled vibrantly, "I return with great news."
Tiara raised her eyebrow but gestured to him to continue.
"There seem to be Behemoth Goats or something that looks just like them in the mountain ranges. I killed two and had great difficulties carrying them until I was forced to store them in the War Rune. They’re really heavy and can probably feed everyone for a week. They’ll probably taste amazing grilled with some vegetables."
’I sure hope that’s not the only thing you have to say to me,’ Tiara’s gaze told Legion, who was still smiling.
"The sea over there is not an ocean as we’d feared. We can use it to supply everything with water in the near future. But that leads me to an interesting point," Legion grinned like a Silverfang cub, "The mountain range is much bigger than we’d anticipated, and behind it, we can find a proper ocean. Once the space in the plains and the surrounding area isn’t big enough, we can expand by traveling through the ocean. The mountain range can also deliver enough stone and hopefully some high-quality ores."
Tiara didn’t quite understand why Legion was this excited, but she nodded. It was good that the mountain range was massive and that the water vessel wasn’t seawater. That would have been a little bit more annoying to deal with. But then again, they could have created their lakes and seas with their one and only Divine Silverfang, who had a powerful Soultrait with which he could control and conjure water.
Still, the sea saved them lots of trouble.
"There you are, your highness!" Master Tigris approached Tiara with a smile. He retrieved a hardcover book and handed it to the queen, "I just recalled that we didn’t finish our talk about the Silver Constitution. We need to declare the Silver Constitution soonish to handle the settlement’s disputes, crimes, and responsibilities. I know you said there wouldn’t be any disputes and crimes in your kingdom, but…you can never be certain. There is no way to be certain about something like that."
Tiara growled inward but nodded slowly.
It was important to keep a sense of order as the population grew.
Of course, it would take a while before the population exceeded the threshold that could be controlled easily. Still, it was best to establish laws and rules early on to give everyone enough time to study them or ask questions if something was uncertain.
"Okay. Let’s talk about the Silver Constitution, then. How about we bless the manor with our first visit?" Tiara asked lightly, to which Master Tigris responded with a bright smile.
"I’d be honored!"
Master Tigris and Tiara disappeared in the manor for a few days. Countless Silverfangs visited them to inquire about their next tasks, but the odd pair didn’t leave until they finished the last edits of the Silver Constitution.
Once the odd pair left the manor to spread the word of the Silver Constitution, many things changed. The first stage of the settlement’s construction had been completed, and the others were just about to get started on the second stage.
They had already planned the future of the settlement from scratch to the modern technological era.
Everything had been planned. The only issue was whether Caesus could find and claim a suitable piece of land for the Silverfang territory.
His battle in the Origin Expanse was the biggest unknown factor in the Silverfands’ grand plan.
However, the Silverfangs were certain their King would emerge victorious.
All they had to do was wait for their King’s return.

chapters.title: Chapter 1113: Rise of a New Era V
chapters.content:
"We left the Untamed Jungle…for this?" One of the Silverfang Champions asked Caesus, his eyes squinted to tiny slits.
"What’s the issue with this place?" Caesus grinned back, ignoring the Summon’s doubts.
In fact, most of the Summons doubted Caesus’ actions at this point, but nobody dared to say anything aloud. Until now, at least.
Caesus and his people, including the millions of offspring his Goblins, Spiders, and other tamed creatures had given birth to, had been traveling for more than a month at this point. They evaded the most powerful enemies and sustained only a few hundred casualties in the meantime. Even those casualties could be considered stupidish because some tamed monsters and Summons entered the territory of creatures even after Caesus warned them.
Find more chapters on .Côm
Fortunately, there weren’t any major altercations. There had been some more issues, but most had been dealt with easily.
Michael teleported them to the border of the Untamed Jungle before leaving Caesus and his people to fend for themselves. He offered some guidance, but Caesus rejected anymore help. He was thankful for the help he and his people had received from Michael for the last few decades and wished to stop receiving constant aid from the New Primal.
That was how they ended up traveling for a long time throughout the Origin Expanse without a destination.
"This place has almost nothing to offer," The Silverfang Champion grumbled, but Caesus shook his head.
"You are terribly mistaken about that," He smiled at the Champion.
They were currently at a beach connected to a massive flat plains area. While it was true that there weren’t any mountains and only a few forests nearby, it was also a fact that there were many energy-dense dens and caves nearby. Caesus had already deployed his children to inspect the caves and dense to research their future territory.
Other than the clear lack of resources like wood, one of the farmers mentioned that the plains was far from perfect for agriculture. It would be difficult to transform the lacklustre soil into fertile land to harvest all year. But that was fine.
Why was that fine, though?
Caesus had been studying a lot about monsters to understand which type of monster he could/should tame to grow even stronger. That was also how he discovered various maritime monsters that were useful for his Soultrait. However, he also learned about the most valuable parts of certain monsters, their rarity, and where to find them.
Caesus didn’t know everything about the regions some monsters could be found but he located various powerful monsters near the beach and plains. Monsters that hunted other monsters in the ocean.
That was how his attention got pulled to the massive gulf near the beach. The and shrouded the gulf like pincers, covering a massive area, which could transform into a farm of maritime monsters within a few months or years depending on the difficulty level. One way or another, Caesus discovered several incredibly rare types of fishes.
First, there was the Origin Syphon, a type of fish monster with an extraordinarily high amount of origin energy that was further refined and compressed. The older the Origin Syphon, the higher the purity level of origin energy within them. This type of monster was even more valuable than high-level Energy Stones. In fact, they were perfect to be mixed into food for Non-Awakened to develop their energy systems from a young age.
It was a well-known fact that the Origin Syphon was perfect to nurture young prodigies from a young age. Their energy systems would be several times stronger than the norm while children would also grow accustomed to containing and controlling origin energy. Most children nurtured with Origin Syphon would grow into High Awakened within a few years, no matter how talentless they would have been without Origin Syphon.
Origin Syphon lost its precious potency the older the consumer was, but Caesus didn’t care about that. He didn’t want to use Origin Syphon for himself or his older combatants. He’d use it for the children of the Silverfangs in Tiagro and sell the rest for an exorbitant price in the Cosmic Shop.
The Cosmic Shop, for the records, was a parting gift from Michael, along with a bunch of Coins to purchase various goods. Caesus didn’t wish to use the Cosmic Shop this early on, but if they decided to transform their kingdom in the Origin Expanse into a fishing-focused business, they would have to use the Cosmic Shop right away. They would need durable wood and other resources until the plains’ soil would be transformed into fertile soil.
’Michael will definitely trade Origin Syphon for a great price. He will provide us with enough resources to establish the settlement and get started with everything,’ Caesus thought. Even though he didn’t feel like using the Cosmic Shop to trade with Michael, it was a fact that the Silverfang Summons were the most accustomed to using the massive jungle woods and other materials of the Untamed Jungle for constructs. Michael was also more generous than business-minded Lords. It was easier to convince him to give him more goods in exchange for Origin Syphon.
"Are we really going to stay here?" Another Summon asked, and Caesus nodded.
The Origin Syphon were only one of many monsters that could be found in the gulf. One of the Goblin Shamans just told him that there were several underground lakes with different types of carp and other types of maritime monsters. There was even a massive crystal cave, which had to be researched first in one of the many caves.
That lead Caesus to an early conclusion; the plains was filled with crystal, which contaminated the soil above.
Of course, that might not be the case, but Caesus didn’t care. The Origin Syphon, given that his avian children were located thousands of them from the sky was enough reason to settle down here. They could always expand and explore the ocean to find more precious targets.
Furthermore…fish tasted excellent. Every Silverfang loved fish. Why would they not settle down here where fish was ever present?
Caesus retrieved the Lord Sigil – a special emblem, which could also be considered an advanced version of the Lord Token as it contained everything a Lord needed to settle down wherever he wanted – and placed it down in the plains, far enough to expand in all directions without affecting the beach and ocean gulf, but close enough to shroud a small portion of the gulf in the 10-day Protection Barrier, which he obtained as a newly appointed Lord.
"Oh damn…" Some Summons said in unison, but Caesus only smiled as the wooden manor and Summoning Gate conjured before him.
"Let’s get to work!

chapters.title: Chapter 1114: Rise of a New Era VI
chapters.content:
Caesus didn’t use the Summoning Gate right away. In fact, he wouldn’t have to use the Summoning Gate for a while now. There were more than 100,000 Silverfang Summons under him, and only a few would fit into the wooden manor.
"Please start with the construction of the tents and the distribution of mattresses," Caesus ordered the Silverfang Summons. He then added, "And prepare several large pots. I will return with some fish for dinner."
They were forced to eat small rations of food after traveling for several weeks straight. Of course, they’d hunted a bunch of monsters for their meat, and Caesus had some leftover food in his War Rune storage, but the leftovers wouldn’t last long, whereas the meat had been eaten entirely.
There were simply too many people to feed for several weeks, especially with Caesus being the only one owning a War Rune Storage. He was the only Awakened who’d stayed behind in the Origin Expanse to take care of the Summons and establish the Silverfang territory for the remaining Awakened. Still, it would take a while before the Awakened would reach out for the Origin Expanse. They were busy enough with the workload on Tiagro.
Caesus’ children were still busy roaming around, exploring the surrounding lands, but they’d also informed Caesus about a bunch of big fish roaming around the ocean. That was why Caesus ended up retrieving dozens of massive bots, energy-ignitable campfires, and so forth.
The Summons looked at him for a while but nodded and jumped into action. Even if they wondered what exactly Caesus was doing at times, they had learned a lot about him in the last few weeks and the decades before that. Caesus might not be a god, but he was the strongest Silverfang they’d ever seen. That was enough reason to trust in his reasoning.
Caesus left the safety of the Protection Barrier and circulated some energy through his legs to run around the ocean gulf. He slowed before the massive ocean, which was known as the Azure Ocean, and smiled faintly at the sight unfolding before him. The Azure Ocean was as long and wide as the ocean. Caesus couldn’t pinpoint where it ended in any direction. That was shocking, but it was also exciting. The ocean protected them from the attacks of other Lords in that direction, though it left them wide open for attacks from the ocean world.
But that wasn’t what Caesus was worried about. The Azure Ocean was their treasure trove. It would be why the Silverfang Tigerfolk would shoot to the peak of all races in the future. It might take thousands of years, but Caesus was not in a rush. He was more than willing to take one step after another at a decent pace. They weren’t in a rush like Michael had been in the past.
’I am enjoying this.’ Caesus thought and circulated energy through his feet. He created thin energy barriers underfoot and walked on the ocean’s surface.
The monster he was targeting was a Titan Whale, a creature with a length of more than two hundred meters.
He could have rushed forward to attack the Titan Whale, but there was no need to go that far. Furthermore, Caesus wanted to enjoy himself a little.
The Giant Sharks thought similarly. The avian children had already informed Caesus that there would be enemies in the ocean, but he only got a good picture of the enemies’ numbers and sizes now that they attacked him.
They didn’t want someone else to take their prey – the Titan Whale – and attacked him. One of the Giant Sharks burst out of the water from underneath. Its maw was wide enough to wallow six or seven humanoid creatures of Caesus’ size, but the Giant Shark couldn’t even shut its maw and swallow Caesus whole when its body split apart.
A fountain of blood spurted through the air before the cleaved-through body crashed heavily onto the ocean’s surface. The ocean around him was dyed red, attracting the surrounding Giant Shards. Some more burst out of the water, but they didn’t target Caesus. They wanted to feast on their fallen brethren.
Caesus, however, wasn’t willing to surrender the Giant Shark corpse to them. His hand, transformed into the Silver Tiger’s claws, swept through the air, creating massive arcs of energy that cut through the air. The corpse was cut into several pieces, and the Giant Sharks, trying to feast on their fallen brethren, received the same fate.
The energy arcs cut tens of meters through the ocean before they dispersed at Caesus’ command. He then released his energy to store the Giant Shark corpses while more of their brethren – a bunch of bigger guys – burst through the water to attack him from the side. One of them even released a burst of electricity, which would have been enough to paralyze a High Awakened, but Caesus merely smiled. His claw swept through the air again, killing six out of seven massive Giant Sharks.
Only the mutated Giant Shark was left behind.
"You can either become my child and serve me until death or die. You are not yet a Divine Beast, but I can help you breakthrough," Caesus said calmly while collecting the remaining corpses of the Giant Shark.
The mutated Giant Shark didn’t move and looked at Caesus, but all he could sense was bloodlust.
"You can’t understand me? That’s a shame. I expected a creature on the verge of becoming a Divine Beast would be smarter than this," Caesus snickered and was about to deal the finishing blow to kill the mutant when a massive tail emerged from the water. The tail was dozens of meters wide and even longer. It covered the sun, shrouding the mutant Giant Shark in shadows before crashing down like a hammer. The massive tail crushed the Giant Shark, killing it on the spot.
At the same time, it missed Caesus by a hair’s breadth.
Large waves swept in all directions after the tail hit the water, but Caesus protected himself with a layer of origin energy.
Still, the waves engulfed Caesus for a second, covering his sight.
Caesus considered escaping the water to find out what was happening, but he stopped. Something urged him to stay here.
It took Caesus only a few seconds to realize what it was. The water walls disappeared, revealing a ginormous eye, an eye filled with intelligence and great wisdom. The Titan Whale’s head had emerged from the water, and it looked straight at him.
"You killed the shark," Caesus commented on the obvious. The Titan Whale could have remained silent, but it released a fountain of water and a wave of emotions. Caesus sensed joy and gratitude.
"You can understand me. That…shouldn’t have been a surprise, I guess. You must be a Mythical Creature if you can defeat a Tier-6 Mutant Giant Shark with a tailsweep just like that. You are far from becoming a Divine Beast, but you show potential."
Caesus forgot about hunting the Titan Whale for food. They had more than a dozen Giant Sharks to feast on for a day or two.
Enjoy exclusive adventures from .Côm
Still, he hasn’t left the ocean just yet.
’What if I pay even more attention to the ocean? There aren’t many Lords in the ocean, and only a few dared to explore it. Every new discovery will elevate the Silverfang Tigerfolk’s status drastically.’ Caesus swallowed hard, but a smile formed on his lips.
"Do you want to work for me?"

chapters.title: Chapter 1115: Rise of a New Era VII
chapters.content:
Taming the Titan Whale didn’t take long, but connecting to the Titan Whale’s offspring wasn’t completed quickly. It took several days to locate all offspring of the Titan Whale, but once that was done, everything improved. Not that there was an issue in the first place, but with the Titan Whales being under Caesus’ control, he had a much easier time controlling everything.
The old Titan Whale Caesus had been protected from the hungry Giant Sharks, and hundreds of Titan Whale children had spread across the bay of the Azure Ocean. Due to their massive size and lackluster defenses, they had a harder time surviving in the deeper parts of the Azure Ocean, but they had a pleasant time near the bays. Still, despite their lackluster defenses, they weren’t weak. They were massive creatures, weighing more than a thousand tons each, and they could crush their enemies with their tails or swallow them whole.
Not many monsters near the outskirts of the Azure Ocean dared attack Titan Whales, which was why countless smaller creatures stayed near Titan Whales for protection. Only starving creatures from the deeper parts of the Azure Ocean, or monsters like Giant Sharks, which could be found everywhere in the Azure Ocean, dared attack Titan Whales.
In the old Titan Whale’s cave, the Giant Sharks had been waiting for the Titan Whale to grow tired. It had been injured after a monster from the Deep Ocean attacked it, and the Giant Sharks smelled its blood. They hadn’t been starving but were impatient creatures who tried to eliminate the old and injured Titan Whale several times.
They would have succeeded if Caesus had not appeared out of nowhere. They were dead and had been transformed into a delicacy for a hundred thousand Silverfangs.
After a few days of hard work, the first port had already been constructed at the beach. One batch of Origin Syphon fish had already been collected, and it was only a matter of time before the second and third batches were pulled out of the ocean.
The Cosmic Shop had been established and configured and was in full use. Dozens of Summons entered and left the Cosmic Shop at a time to do trades, carry all kinds of resources around, and organize the stream of Summons and materials.
Keeping track of everything was difficult, but they had enough people to care for everything. The Origin Syphon fishes were sold for a much higher price than initially expected. That was great, but even better was that the Titan Whales had been sharing their knowledge about the Azure Ocean and its treasures. Caesus learned about a dozen maritime creatures as valuable as Origin Syphon fishes, if not more valuable. That was great, even if it was only something he could pay more attention to in the future.
For the time being, they would be busy enough with the Origin Syphon fishes and establish a proper port in the Azure Ocean’s gulf. Claiming the entire gulf was necessary, but they needed three to five settlements to claim the entire territory. Of course, they could travel around the gulf daily, but it was too big for ordinary Tierless or Tier-1 Summons to waste their precious time traveling for hours to reach their workplace.
Therefore, they finished the ’main’ settlement where more than 100,000 Summons could reside with enough living space before adding a few smaller villages for the working force.
Defending the entire gulf was another issue but Caesus’ children were doing a good job at locating all threats and taking them out. There were millions of Goblins, Spiders, avian monsters, and the like to remove all threats. Of course, it wasn’t always easy but Caesus was glad he and his people could focus on the myriad of construction sites that had to be completed first.
Several weeks passed in the blink of an eye, but it felt like a day to Caesus. He didn’t sleep once because he was too busy devising hundreds of plans to solve various future problems. The Silverfangs were wealthy at this point – they quadrupled the price for Origin Syphon because the demand was too high to supply – but the lack of workforce was their greatest problem.
Therefore, Caesus started using Ordinary Summoning Scrolls, Mythic Scrolls, and Named Scrolls to summon batches of thousands of Silverfangs in one go.
’This is exciting. Summoning new Summons feels like I’m finally at the starting line. The starting line of the New Era. The era of the Silverfang Empire!’ Caesus chuckled. He smiled from one ear to another and watched his more experienced Summons do the same thing they’d already done in Michael’s territory. They welcomed the new Summons, introduced them to the Silverfang territory and explained to them everything they had to know.
Caesus did the same, but something was different this time.
Caesus was the Lord of the territory this time around. He wasn’t Michael’s Subordinate anymore. He was his own ruler and had to act accordingly to gain the new Summons’ trust and loyalty. The Links of Loyalty were quickly established, but some Summons seemed displeased with the situation. They were thrown into a new territory and would have to work tirelessly to expand and grow the territory.
The only advantages were that they weren’t the first Summons. Caesus had more than 100,000 loyal and trustworthy Summons who praised him thoroughly. They made sure everyone would know what kind of person Caesus was. Of course, they also bragged about his power, saying that he was the strongest Silverfang the Tigerfolk had ever seen.
That, for the records, was a fact. Caesus was the strongest King who had ever risen among the Silverfang Tigerfolk. However, at the same time, Tiara was the strongest Queen. They never fought it out for real, but the siblings knew that it would be a pyrrhic victory no matter who would emerge victorious at the end of a life-and-death battle.
But there was no need to worry about that. Caesus and Tiara were done fighting against each other. Read exclusive content at .Côm
If anything, they would fight together to defend their people as the strongest Silverfangs in the history of the Tigerfolk.

chapters.title: Chapter 1116: Rise of a New Era VIII
chapters.content:
It was no surprise that the Silverfang territory expanded in the following months. Everything worked much better than expected, and it was a great surprise to everyone when nobody stopped their expansion. There were a few Lords in the surroundings, but none of them had been bothered to initiate communication.
If anything, they’d avoided Caesus and the Silverfang Tigerfolk to the best of their capabilities. That should have been warning enough, but Caesus and his people had been too excited.
They didn’t realize what was happening until it was already too late.
One day, the ground in the massive ocean gulf tremored violently. The tremors were strong enough to shake some buildings and push them until they collapsed. That was enough to put everyone on guard.
"We receive hostile signals from the ocean. Maritime monsters are emerging from the gulf and the surroundings!" A Champion shouted at the top of his lungs when he rushed past the Orb of Hostiltiy.
"How many are there?" Caesus asked in a hurry, even though he could already sense the number.
"Hundreds of thousands, maybe even more!" Someone else responded, but Caesus had already turned to the gulf. Something humongous stirred in the gulf…something powerful enough to make his hair stand up to its end.
Caesus nibbled on his lower lip and disappeared through the Runic Gate for a moment. He emerged in Tiagro, retrieved a red crystal, and crushed it. A moment later, he returned to the Origin Expanse, where the massive head of a mighty creature emerged from the gulf.
The head was the first Caesus saw, but he could instantly tell what the creature was. The heavy presence filling the air showed Caesus what kind of enemy he would have to fight.
"I cannot protect you guys. Take care of the maritime monsters…and survive," Caesus ordered with as much confidence as possible. A moment later, he transformed into a white flash. The Soullife Arts, Foundation Break, and the Soul Technique, Children of a God, were activated simultaneously, pushing his Soultrait and body to their limits.
Energy circulated through his body as he shot through the air. He reached the gulf, smashed heavily into the emerging head of the Ocean Dragon, whose body filled the gulf, and grasped its scales tightly.
Caesus might not be as heavy as the Ocean Dragon, but he was certainly strong enough to carry it through the air while it was still tired. The Ocean Dragon had yet to fully awake, which was Caesus greatest advantage. He carried the Ocean Dragon out of the ocean gulf and dragged it as deep into the wide-open ocean where they could wreak as much havoc as they wanted.
The Ocean Dragon was still tired but didn’t like being dragged around. It liked even less than an Awakened had crushed one of its scales with brute force. It roared aloud, stirring more maritime monsters awake. However, it was to no avail. The Titan Whales protected the bay. They restrained as many maritime monsters from following the Ocean Dragon’s order as possible. That was the least they could do after everything Caesus had done to protect them.
"This is a battle between us. You versus me!" Caesus roared, transforming his hands into claws right before they dug deep into the Ocean Dragon’s eyes. The Dragon retaliated with a horrifying roar. It unleashed its presence and altered energy which smashed heavily into Caesus.
He was hurled through the air and felt like his insides were being crushed, but Caesus wasn’t dead just yet. He was still alive and more than willing to fight the Ocean Dragon until one of them took the last breath.
"If you don’t leave my people alone, I will end you today!" He roared at the top of his lungs, to which the Ocean Dragon responded with another roar. However, this roar accompanied the Dragon’s Draconic Essence. It was unwilling to end this battle in a draw, either.
How could it? They woke it from its several hundred years of hibernation! They deserved to die. All of them!
***
Crab monsters, serpents, and humanoid maritime creatures emerged from the ocean. The Ocean Dragon stirred them awake and filled them with fear. They fled and reached the land, unlike the other maritime monsters, which tried to escape the Ocean Dragon’s wrath only to dive straight onto the sand beach, where they wiggled around helplessly. Some elemental creatures used their powers to escape death on land, but others were bound to die helplessly.
Yet, nobody cared about them. The Silverfangs were too busy with preparing their defenses. The villages of the fishing crews were deserted and ordered to return to the main settlements, which they reached just in time by using three Behemoth Goats. Caesus tamed them without using his powers. He used the abilities he had learned through decades of handling animals and trained them with the help of some Beast Trainers. This was a job for which only a few Silverfang Summons were granted. In fact, Caesus had never seen anyone else with a job like this in the time he worked with – for – Michael.
The Beast Trainers had tamed various monsters, mostly livestock, since they arrived in their new home. Unfortunately, none of them were combat mounts. That would have made many things easier.
But since that wasn’t the case, the Silverfang Tigerfolk had to fight on their own. Their Lord was busy wrestling a Divine Beast, a fully-grown Dragon who had been hibernating for centuries – probably to attain godhood or to rest even longer for whatever purpose.
The hordes of Elemental Crabs, Metal-covered Crabs, and tens of thousands of serpents, several nests of them with tens of varieties – mutations and evolution –, each more dangerous than the other, charged ahead.
They crushed the ports, the boats, and the tiny villages before making their way to the main settlement. Most monsters didn’t even want to move to the settlement, but the strongest had received a command from the Ocean Dragon.
They were told to destroy everything to return the well-deserved silence in the Ocean Dragon’s land.
The maritime monsters followed the Ocean Dragon’s will and charged at the main settlement. Your next read awaits at .Côm
For the first time since the Silverfang territory had been established, their existence was in danger.
They had to fight with their lives on the line, or everything would be over.

chapters.title: Chapter 1117: Rise of a New Era IX
chapters.content:
"Prepare the defenses!" A middle-aged Silverfang shouted across the settlement walls. He pointed at the ballistae, raised his hands as the massive bolts were pulled back, and cleaved downward when the crab monsters entered the ballistae’s range. The massive bolts whizzed through the air and entered their targets with a crunch.
Several crabs squealed in pain, but most hit targets collapsed to the ground. The ballistae bolts did their work and pierced through the crab’s thick shells and penetrated their soft flesh. The crunching noise filled the air for a moment, but that was about it. The cacophony created by more than a hundred thousand frightened monsters was worse.
"Reload and fire!" The man shouted again while retrieving a bow alongside the remaining archers. He nocked an arrow on the bowstring, pulled back, and fired. The other Archers followed his action. They filled the bow and arrow with as much energy as they could contain without breaking apart and released a hail of energy-infused arrows. The arrows propelled through the air in a beautiful arc until they struck the serpents. The arrows exploded upon collision, the energy infused into the arrows was unstable after hitting the monsters, and killed the creatures.
Hundreds of monsters died in the next few seconds, but that wasn’t enough. There were too many monsters to deal with at once.
"Silvarean Tigers!" Someone shouted, and the Summons, who had already advanced to Tier-4, moved out right away. They didn’t hesitate in the slightest and jumped across the settlement wall to charge the monster horde. They shot forward, hair growing from all over their body. Their bodies expanded and elongated, and their hands transformed into large claws.
Some Summons expanded and remained bi-pedal, whereas others transformed into full-fledged Tigers the size of an average car. A handful of Summons transformed into larger Tigers. They were more than two meters tall and six meters long. However, their fangs were the most terrifying. They had two elongated, razor-sharp fangs that tore through the crab’s shell like a hot knife cut through butter.
They were the Silvarean Sabertooth Tigers, a superior kind of the average Silvarean Tiger. Their muscles bulged as they shot forward, evading the initial lunges of serpents shooting forward to cleave through the serpents with their claws. Their claws cut deep into the enemies, killing them in a single blow, which was expected when Higher Lifeforms fought hordes of Lesser Lifeforms.
There were only a few High Beasts among the maritime creatures attacking them. Still, some of them were truly powerful. They used their innate advantages, evaded the Silvarean Tigers, and reached the settlement walls, where they were welcomed by a series of arrows, crossbow bolts, and ballistae bolts.
Even though most Silverfang Summons weren’t combatants, everyone could do something. Nobody wanted to stay behind while their combatants did something. Therefore, the warehouse filled with crossbows, bolts, and other tools was opened. The crossbows were brought to the walls, where they released a salve of crossbow bolts before the crossbow would be replaced with a loaded one. The empty crossbow cartridge would be filled once the crossbow’s string was pulled back and locked in place.
Even some youngsters helped by catching tools, weapons, and other goods required from the warehouses. They ran back and forth to supply everyone and helped out where they could. In the meantime, the combatants killed enemies in the thousands. Unfortunately, that wasn’t enough.
Before they reached the settlement walls, more than 20,000 maritime monsters had been killed, leaving them with 80,000 or more to attack.
"Open the gates and charge ahead!" A Silverfang Champion shouted, and the guards obeyed. They were scared about what would happen once the gates opened, but more than three thousand Silverfangs were ready to charge out of the settlement.
The gates opened, which led to a massive brawl between the maritime monsters and the Silverfang Summons.
Neither side seemed to be on the winning side. The Silverfang Summons pushed the enemies away, killing dozens of crabs and serpents, but some monsters managed to bypass the pile of monster carcasses forming in the entrance. That was not all. More monsters climbed the settlement walls. They were shot, arrows and crossbow bolts piercing their eyes and vital points, but fear was instilled in their hearts.
Some defenders screamed in fright rather than pain as more and more monsters reached the settlement. One of the screaming defenders was about to be struck by a crab monster’s pincers when a squeal filled the air. A blue shadow descended from the sky, picked up the crab with mighty talons that crushed the monster’s shell at once, and carried it into the air. A freezing breeze brushed through the air before a dead – frozen to death – crab crashed to the ground on top of another crab. The frozen crab crushed its brethren and crumbled into countless pieces.
In the meantime, the young defender, who had been screaming until a moment ago, looked up. There he saw the children of Caesus. The Frostglider Eagle with his children.
"Our Lord is still with us!" He shouted at the top of his lungs.
Even though their Lord was brawling with the Ocean Dragon, it didn’t mean their Lord left them unprotected.
The Lord’s children were still there to protect them.
They were coming.
And they were angry. Read latest chapters at .Côm
A horde of Goblins charged across the plains. Their cackling filled the silence of the night in the plains until the cacophony of sounds collided with the noises made by the maritime monsters.
The Goblin horde was fast and would soon reach the settlement, but the Frostglider Eagles and Shadowbane Spiders were faster.
They were already present, the spiders appearing in the shadows of their enemies to kill them before they realized what was going on.
The Shadowbane Spiders were fast and deadly, slaying their enemies at once, whereas the Frostglider Eagles made fun of the High Beasts. They carried them high up into the air, froze them with their deadly freezing breath, and released them on top of the other enemies, crushing them to death.
That was fun.
However, it was still not over. More enemies emerged from the ocean.
But that was good. The Goblins had yet to taste their enemies’ blood.

chapters.title: Chapter 1118: Rise of a New Era X
chapters.content:
The Goblin Shamans released a series of lightning bolts into the masses of enemies. They didn’t even have to aim well to hit an enemy. Unfortunately, the lightning bolts weren’t lethal enough to kill the enemies immediately. Still, the damage was considerable, and the paralysis properties of the Goblin Shaman’s lightning couldn’t be underestimated.
The hit targets were stunned for a second, which granted the Silverfang Archers enough time to aim and strike. The arrows hit the unmoving targets, killing them on the spot.
The Shadowbane Spiders were also nearly struck by a bunch of lightning bolts, but they merged with the shadows around them and changed their targets to fight closer to the ocean. The area was also more dangerous, but the shadows of the creatures emerging from the ocean helped them move around as they pleased.
Find adventures at .Côm
