The Shadowbane Spiders had pointy and highly durable legs with which they punctured the vital spots of maritime creatures fleeing from the ocean. They might be Lesser Lifeforms and of the smaller kind, but they had poison sacs that created numbing poison that could be secreted through their legs. That being said, every wound inflicted by the Shadowbane Spiders would numb the maritime creatures.
One hit was not enough to slow the monsters, but with tens of thousands of Shadowbane Spiders spread across the beach of the ocean gulf, it wasn’t more difficult to hit the larger creature tens of times. They quickly collapsed to the ground, where a Frostglider Eagle tore them apart or froze them on the spot.
Their freezing breath was a true menace. It inflicted considerable damage and would kill any creature that was either too physically weak to break through the layers of ice forming on their skin or didn’t use enough energy to protect their bodies. Many maritime creatures were huge and physically strong, but they didn’t have a high proficiency at controlling energy. They were less intelligent land-based monsters. At least, that was what it looked like to the Silverfang Summons.
A Goblin Emperor, a mutant with four arms, wielded two war axes and two thin longswords. The longswords whirled through the air in beautiful arcs, mana coursing through them, while the war axes smashed upon the massive creatures, tearing them apart without any resistance.
Dozens of venomous serpents tried injuring the Goblin Emperor, but his hide was too tough to be penetrated easily. He crushed the horde before him and created a large opening for his children to charge through. A Goblin Prince, hundreds of Hobgoblin Champions, Hobgoblin Berserkers, and tens of thousands of Goblins pushed through the gap and widened it, creating even more space for the Goblin Shamans, Archers, and Goblin Elementalists to wreak havoc.
It didn’t take long before the only remnants of enemies before the Silverfang settlement were their corpses. The strongest maritime creatures attacked the Frostglider Eagles, The Shadowbane Queen Spider, and the Goblin Emperor, but it was to no avail.
Dozens of Frostglider Eagles descended from the sky, releasing their fury upon the Lesser Lifeforms fighting underneath them. Their freezing breath was like the Arctic Breath of a Glacier Dragon. It might not be as powerful and massive in comparison, but it was certainly the lesser version. Still, it was powerful enough to damage the Lesser Lifeforms and freeze them alive.
The Frostglider Eagles may not be strong enough to kill the strongest High Beasts of the ocean, but they were fast enough to evade their attacks. Two Frostglider Eagles were hit by rocks mid-air, but the Silvarean Tigers were ready to catch them before the crabs could cut them into pieces. The tigers pounced through the air, caught the Eagles in their mouths, and charged back to the settlement. They jumped on top of the settlement walls, put down the injured Eagles, and had the Healers tend to their wounds.
The Silvarean Tigers returned to the battlefield and attacked the stronger High Beasts of the ocean. They inflicted smaller injuries at first, analyzing the ocean beast’s regeneration and other characteristics with claw strikes and bone-crunching bites before they geared up by a notch or two by applying energy onto their fangs and claws.
They ripped through the beasts and killed the first High Beast even before the Goblin Emperor and Queen Spider finished their masterpiece. Still, the Silvarean Tigers weren’t unscathed. Some had been injured, and one Silvarean Tiger had been killed. Hundreds of Goblins were dying, and the Shadowbane Spiders weren’t impossible to defeat either. Every jump through the shadows consumed a considerable portion of their power. It drained them to step through the shadows more than four times. The maritime beasts didn’t pay much attention to that, but they sensed the exhaustion level of their enemies.
Their perception was great enough to pick on the exhausted enemies and kill them.
However, something interesting happened once more. High Beasts of the ocean had been defeated. First, the formation of maritime monsters – if one could call it that in the first place – tore apart. The High Beasts of the ocean had been controlling the Lesser Lifeforms, luring them to the Silverfang settlement as the Ocean Dragon had ordered them.
With the High Beasts’ death, the command disappeared, and the maritime creatures retrieved control of their own fate. They charged past the Silverfangs in the desperate hope of escaping the Ocean Dragon’s wrath.
But, at the same time, something happened within the Silverfang territory. Newcomers had arrived.
The Queen and her escort came to the rescue.
It was just that they were a little late.
Tiara and her people killed the remaining maritime beasts emerging from the ocean. They spent a few minutes annihilating more than a quarter of a million maritime creatures, including some High Beasts, before splitting up to check on the Silverfang territory, the injured, and…Caesus.
Nobody could sense Caesus, but the pained roars of the Ocean Dragon reverberated throughout the outskirts of the Azure Ocean.
Tiara was just about to move out when Caesus’ children raised their hands to stop her. She glared at them, but the Goblins pointed at something in the sky. It was a falling star.
No, it was Caesus!
Caeuss crashed heavily into the sand before Tiara, splattering warm blood everywhere.
"Brother, are you fine?" Tiara asked upon sensing the weak fluctuations from Caesus.
He tried to say something and get up, but the strength left his body. Thus, he grinned like a fool, wincing a few times in pain, and remained on the ground.
"I did it," Caesus mumbled, his body covered in blood.
One of his arms was missing, while the rest of his body was mangled. His hair, clothes, and skin was burned until nothing was left. It was only because of his connection to his children and their bestial regeneration transferring to him that he was still alive.
"I protected our people," Caesus issued between two heavy breaths.
Tiara bent down and smiled proudly at her brother.
"You did great. I’m proud of you," Tears welled in her eyes, "We will fix you. Don’t worry about anything, okay?"
Caesus just smiled, but thinking about his fight with the Ocean Dragon made him shudder.
He forced the Ocean Dragon to leave, but it was dead.
Still, Caesus was proud of himself. The Ocean Dragon had been stronger than him. Or it should have been stronger as a creature on the verge of attaining godhood.
Yet, he prevailed. He survived. He did it.
Caesus protected the Silverfangs.
He protected the New Era!

chapters.title: Chapter 1119: Supreme Lord I
chapters.content:
"What are you doing there?" Alice walked up to Michael and embraced him from behind. She gently leaned against his back while Michael continued working. He smiled from one ear to another, his golden eyes glowing vibrantly as the pictures before him changed.
"I’m watching our friends. Well, not only them. I’m watching…everyone, if you want me to be precise," He muttered while using his Essence to shape the bowl field with water before him. The bowl transformed into a mirror’s frame, and the water rippled as it transformed into liquid glass. At least, that was what it looked like to Alice. But only for a moment as countless pictures appeared before her.
"Isn’t that Sun Demos?" She asked, and the pictures slowed down. They showed Frederik Kolbenheim and Jacqueline Orlando spending time at their home in the Tritan Alliance before returning to the images revealing Sun Demos and his little kingdom in the Untamed Jungle.
Sun Demos was still one of Michael’s tamed monsters, but it was not like Michael told the Monkey King to do anything. He could do as he pleased as long as he didn’t try to go against Michael or his friends.
Sun Demos evolved and mutated several times over the course of the last few decades. He was now a Blazing Sun Monkey King, a Mythical Existence at the 7th Tier. The little troublemaker was now a Divine Beast!
Michael hadn’t been around Sun Demos often in the last few decades. In fact, he was aware of how negligent he had been with the Monkey King, but Sun Demos didn’t hold him accountable. If anything, Sun Demos was happy Michael didn’t pay much attention to him. The Monkey King never felt like Michael’s subordinate. If anything, fighting side by side felt more like the alliance of two kings rather than an Emperor commanding his lowly subjects.
Sun Demos liked that about Michael the most. They worked together for a few years before going their separate ways.
The Monkey King was a lot stronger than he used to be, and he used that strength to create his own territory, where he lived with his children, as well as the other Blood Oath Demon Monkeys. This included the monkeys that were given birth through evolutions, mutations, and the like.
However, the Blazing Sun Monkey King ruled them all. He was the ruler of the Monkey Kingdom.
"Are you watching everyone like that? How did you manage to create such a scrying bowl – or should I call it a mirror? – in the first place? I can understand you seeing everything that’s happening in the Origin Expanse, but how did you stalk Jac and Frederik? They’re not in the Origin Expanse right now, or are they?" Alice inquired.
She didn’t talk down to him, but her choice of words hurt a little.
"Stalking? I am just checking on my friends…" Michael responded a little down.
Alice ruffled through his long, silky hair with a smug smile, "Of course you are. You’re just a bit overprotective. Yes, yes. That’s it."
Michael snickered in his mind, but he knew better than to say anything aloud.
"What about Zeroa? I haven’t seen her for a while now. She hasn’t been in the Elemental Empire either. I visited it two weeks ago, but they haven’t seen her for a few years now. I was going to ask you, but I forgot about it," Alice asked, a trace of worry returning to her voice.
"Zeroa is fine," Michael smiled and changed the picture to the Elemental Empress and the Red Dragon enjoying their lives on a tiny island, "Before you ask… Yes, that is an active volcano. Yes, they’re both at fault for its eruption… and yes, they are both still in the Origin Expanse."
Alice raised an eyebrow, the worry replaced by confusion and curiosity.
"Where are they? Is that the…"
"The Azure Ocean? Yeah, it is. I don’t know what they’re planning, but I sure hope they won’t tear apart the Azure Ocean with their actions. Caesus has already done enough damage to the Azure Ocean ecosystem. There is no need to create PyroWyrms in the middle of the Azure Ocean. This would be a catastrophe."
"How would they…" Alice asked, but she sealed her lips before the full sentence could escape her mouth. She knew better than to keep asking stupid questions. It was just that she was curious, and her hormones were going crazy these days.
"Please, do not ask me how they make Wyrms. Nobody should be forced to learn or see anything about this…method," Michael shuddered and turned to his wife. He pinched her cheeks before kissing her on the forehead.
"Either way," Trying to change the topic, Alice cleared her throat and moved forward, "What exactly did Caesus do?"
Michael chuckled and turned back to the scrying mirror. He recreated the images of Caesus battle with the Ocean Dragon.
"The Ocean Dragon was supposed to be hibernating until ascending godhood. That was the plan. Unfortunately, this didn’t work well. Caesus established his settlement less than two kilometers from the Ocean Dragon’s residency and chose to use its bay as a port to collect the fish eating its…poop."
Alice burst into laughter, and she didn’t stop for a good minute or two. She only noticed that Michael wasn’t joking when he kept looking at her, his lips pressed into a fine line.
"Wait! You are not serious, right? No. That cannot be. You can’t be serious."
"Well, that is a serious matter. He was earning a fortune from the fishes evolving through the Ocean Dragon’s excrements. Unfortunately, they were too loud and woke the Ocean Dragon. To be loud enough to wake a dragon in everlasting slumber is quite an achievement," Michael sighed deeply.
"But they’re fine, right? Caesus…Nothing happened to him, right?"
"Yes, he is fine. He was close to death, but he went above and beyond, breaking through his limit a few times – which was quite impressive – and forced the Ocean Dragon to depart. The Ocean Dragon used too much power and will probably take even longer to attain godhood. Its centuries-long slumber was for naught all because it engaged in a life-and-death battle with Caesus," Michael said with a note of pride in his voice, "Caesus is as good as new, and he should be stronger than ever. He has to be careful, or he might accidentally accept a Law or Authority and attain godhood if he keeps going like that."
"You look like a proud father," Alice teased Mciahel, who could only shrug.
Read latest chapters at .Côm
"I am proud of Caesus. And Tiara, as a matter of fact," He showed Alice everything the Silverfang siblings had achieved. Their development plants progressed much faster than they were devised. They might have told everyone their progress would be slow and that they didn’t want to rush anything, but the truth was that the siblings were competitive and ambitious. If it was possible to progress faster and grow rapidly into a first-rate race…why shouldn’t they give it a try?
Michael could only agree with that.
Why wouldn’t they try their best if they had the means to?
’Maybe being around me during their time in the Untamed Jungle didn’t do them well. I might have influenced them too much,’ Michael realized, but the smug smile on his face never disappeared.

chapters.title: Chapter 1120: Supreme Lord II
chapters.content:
"Lucia is having fun with her friends, isn’t she?" Alice asked a moment later, her hand resting on her belly.
Michael embraced her tightly and switched the image to show what their daughter and the other children had been up to.
First, Michael and Alice watched Lucia roaming through the Origin Expanse. Michael teleported them to a Beginner Region far away from the Untamed Jungle without any items. Their War Rune storages had been emptied, their Artifacts removed, and even their Energy Pillar was crushed, removed, and only put back together when no energy was left within them. The process took a few months to avoid further problems, but Lucia and her friends returned to Tierless Awakened without benefits other than their Soultraits.
Michael didn’t understand why Lucia and her friends wanted to be Tierless Awakened or why they wished to leave, but apparently Alice understood their intentions very well.
"All they want is to live their lives to the fullest. They could become Gods by staying in your territory, given their talent, but it is very boring. Nobody dares to think about claiming or attacking the Untamed Jungle since everyone knows that the Untamed Jungle belongs to you. You also told everyone to stop fighting the Lords outside the Untamed Jungle, which destroys all of the youths’ competition.
They can only fight each other since you’ve also urged the Untamed Jungle to stop expanding now that it is a Primal Region again. I understand that they want some challenge and that they want to go through the same exciting times as you – or we – did," Alice explained to Michael, who looked at his lover deep in thought.
"Is that also why they went to the Tritan Alliance? Because they want to go through the same as we did?" Michael asked, even though he knew the answer already.
Lucia had always been an energetic child. However, the last few years had been too boring for her. That was how she devised the "Zero to Hero" plan. That was what she called it, though Michael was unsure if he could call it that. It was more of an ’early grave’ plan, given the way Lucia treated the dangers of the cosmos and Origin Expanse.
She didn’t take the threats of the Origin Expanse seriously because she had always been around the strongest entities of the Origin Expanse. She was raised in a Primal Region by the New Primal, alongside Divine Beasts and the like. Of course, she wouldn’t take this seriously, especially with her lack of finances, planning, and ruling knowledge.
Michael had been unsure what to do about Lucia for a while but acknowledged her drive to independence. He didn’t intervene and watched her from the sidelines instead. That hurt his heart at times because Lucia told him not to contact him while she was busy. She was worried that she would ask him for help if they were to talk and decided it was best to contact each other only after the foundation of her territory had been completed.
Lucia messed up a few times. She used her entire fortune for things they didn’t need and built structures like Alchemy Towers long before they summoned an Alchemist while also neglecting the three Blacksmiths they’d summoned. Lucia struggled for a long time but didn’t hate it. On the contrary, she was happy with the new responsibilities and tasks ahead.
That was also why Michael liked watching her. It was nice to see his daughter smile like that.
She was happy.
The same applied to Hiraku and his wife, the fiance he had left long ago – before joining Michael. Hiraku and his wife were happy parents of 21 children and a grand total of 85 grandchildren.
Michael switched the mirror images to show Hiraku, his wife, and his family as they gathered for one of the grandchildren’s birthdays. In Hiraku’s family no week passed without a birthday or celebration. Their family consisted of way too many children to go through weeks without celebrations. But that was what made it special. Their lives were filled with joyous celebrations and happiness.
"Is Hellen pregnant again?" Alice asked in surprise as her attention drifted to Hiraku’s wife. Her belly, to be precise.
"It looks like it," Michael responded while also examining the other women in the family. At least three more women were pregnant in the images. That was…interesting.
"They’re doing a good job at fixing the low birthrate of the last century," Michael chuckled, which resulted in a pinch in his sides.
"You shouldn’t make fun of them," Alice snickered, her eyes glowing in excitement as she looked at the children roaming around.
He smiled at Alice and pulled her closer to him.
Even though they had only given birth to one child, Michael and Alice were satisfied. Alice would have been happy with a few more children, but it was not easy for a Goddess and a Primal to give birth to a child. In the first place, the Guardians were known for being too powerful to impregnate someone. That was what most people said, at least. It was a good explanation as to why no more Primal and Guardians emerged out of nowhere. Experience exclusive tales on .Côm
However, the truth was that the Primal weren’t made to reproduce. They were made of Essence of the Origin and were made for the sole purpose of protecting the Origin Universe. They didn’t have the means to reproduce. On the other hand, Michael was an ordinary human before becoming the New Primal. Nobody knew whether Michael and Alice could get pregnant with another child.
However, one thing was certain: If Alice got pregnant, the child would be unique. At the incredibly low chance of Alice getting pregnant, the child would be the product of the New Primal and a Goddess. The baby was likely to be an even greater troublemaker than Lucia had been.
Michael held Alice tightly and switched the picture to show Frederik and Jacqueline in the Tritan Alliance. They had given birth to a few more children over the last few decades, but it was growing increasingly more difficult for them to get pregnant again. After all, their bodies’ drive to reproduce dwindled as their Tier increased.
Still, Frederik and Jacqueline were happy. They spent their days in the Tritan Alliance, protecting it – even if that wasn’t necessary – and stayed with their families. The couple considered leaving the Tritan Alliance in a few years to join Daniel and Rebecca’s expedition but they were still uncertain. They had yet to make their final decision.
It was the exact same in Kaleb’s situation.
He was also unsure what he was supposed to do now that he was the head of the Zenovia house.

chapters.title: Chapter 1121: Supreme Lord III
chapters.content:
Kaleb was probably the most troublesome friend and family member. Taking care of him may not be necessary, but Kaleb Zenovia was still hopelessly in love with Tiara. If it had only been a crush, everything would have been fine, but Kaleb’s love for Tiara was more than a mere crush. He was deeply in love with Tiara, enough to overcome hundreds of rejections.
At this point neither Michael nor Alice could tell how often Tiara had rejected Kaleb.
Alice sighed deeply, seeing the pictures of her brother and her parents, "I thought Mother would punch some sense into his mind, but it looks like his stubbornness has grown exponentially. Not even Mother can handle this brat anymore."
"Well, he is in love," Michael responded and shrugged when Alice glared at him. It’s not his fault to fall in love with Tiara, and it’s not Tiara’s fault that she cannot accept him."
"Cannot? You mean to say that she does not want to accept him," Tiara corrected her lover, but Michael shook his head, "I’ve spoken about it with Tiara a few times in the past. I was curious about what she thought of Kaleb and why she didn’t beat the shit out of him since he never stopped pursuing her. Don’t look at me like that. Tiara beat the shit out of a lot more people than you may think. And those pursuers asked her out only twice, maybe three times when she felt generous."
"So…" Alice tilted her head, "You think Tiara likes Kaleb as well? What did she say?" Continue your journey on .Côm
Michael sighed, "Tiara told me she likes Kaleb but doesn’t think there is more to their friendship than friendship. Even now, Kaleb and Tiara are still in contact. She hopes Kaleb will understand his misunderstanding in the future, whereas Kaleb is certain their friendship is more than just that."
"And what do you think?" Alice inquired.
"I think Tiara is too busy with the Silverfangs to think about love, let alone being with someone and making a family with that special someone. She tries not to think about Kaleb and what ’might’ happen if she were to accept him because she won’t be able to handle it for the time being. Tiara is certain she only exists for her people. That is why she never accepted anyone," He sighed deeply, "But once the Silverfangs have a proper foundation in Tiagro and the Origin Expanse…who knows what will happen? Maybe Kaleb will break through Tiara’s defenses if he continues…or everything will break apart."
The sadness in Alice’s eyes was apparent. She didn’t want her brother to suffer any longer, but it was not like she could change anything. If anything, her interference might destroy everything Kaleb had worked for. That was the last thing Alice wanted. She nodded slowly and breathed out heavily.
"You want to stay out of their business and leave them be, right?" Alice asked, to which Michael nodded.
"If possible, I would have brought them together, but I fear that pushing them together will destroy everything. We must let them be and watch from the sidelines, no matter how much it hurts."
Alice didn’t like that. Like, at all. Nonetheless, she was not naive enough to believe everything could be solved with a few words. Too many responsibilities shackled Tiara, preventing her from discovering how she truly felt. Maybe she liked Kaleb. Maybe not. It was for them to find out what would happen in the future.
Alice was sure Kaleb wouldn’t fall easily out of love, but after more than a hundred rejections, even the greatest crush would start crumbling.
Time will tell whether Kaleb and Tiara have a future or if all of this is just wishful thinking.
"Let’s not talk about it anymore. Kaleb is old enough to decide what he wants to do," Alice decided, which Michael took as a sign to change the topic.
He changed the images on the liquid mirror and diverted his attention to some of the people he hadn’t met for a long time. People who had an impact on his life only went down different paths after a while.
The first was Zeke Lavita. Just like Frederik, Jacqueline, and Kaleb, Zeke Lavita was back in the Tritan Alliance. He’d returned a long time ago, but it was nice to see Zeke with his family spending time with Lincoln’s family. To be precise, the families had combined their forces. Zeke Lavita married Lincoln’s younger sister to combine the Piedra and Lavita families and because they fell in love with each other.
Zeke and Lincoln’s sister mourned Lincoln’s death together. At first, they spent only a few hours together to mourn Lincoln’s death, but their presence consoled each other. The hours turned into days, which quickly developed into weeks and months. They fell in love and united their families. They married within one year and gave birth to a baby boy not even nine months later.
Zeke was still an Awakened but didn’t focus on growing stronger anymore. He spent most of his time with his beloved and enjoyed every day of his life. Maybe he would die in a few centuries if he didn’t focus on growing stronger, but so be it. Not everyone wanted to be immortal. There was no need to live forever as long as they could be together.
Michael didn’t hate his immortality since he wasn’t alone, but he understood Zeke’s point of view. He enjoyed every day much more than those who were immortal because he knew that his life would eventually end.
Gods could live forever, but they could also be killed in about. What if someone didn’t enjoy their lives and worked for centuries to grow stronger, only to die? Just like that, dead, without having lived a proper life.
That wasn’t something Zeke wanted to happen.
Fortunately, Michael didn’t have issues with that. He and Alice were immortal, and nothing would happen to them. He was certain of their bright future and enjoyed every day of it.
Especially the days he spent watching his friends. It was the most enjoyable.

chapters.title: Chapter 1122 Chapter 1122: Supreme Lord IV
chapters.content:
The image of a tall man with a scarred face appeared in the liquid mirror. His features were distorted into a devilish grimace, which resembled his former nickname as the Demonic Combat Instructor. However, there was another nickname he'd received after training Michael and his friends for a while. He was known as the Saint of the Training Hall.
The mixture of nicknames came into existence because he trained everyone with devilish methods to ensure everyone he trained would survive the dangers of the Origin Expanse. Of course, not everyone survived, but far more Lords and Rogues training under him survived than those who didn't acknowledge the importance of training under him.
"Isn't that Silverian Schild? He's older now…but that's him, right?" Alice asked in surprise. Her eyes widened while Michael smiled gently at the image.
"Yeah, that's Silverian," He mumbled before showing pictures of a massive structure on a planet belonging to the Tritan Alliance. The infrastructure of the massive structure encompassed an entire province, but that was necessary.
After all, the structure was none other than the EmeraldShield Academy. It was an educational institution created after the Saphirelake Military Academy had been destroyed, with Silverian Schild's iron-like voice ruling everything.
He was the director of the EmeraldShield Academy but didn't act differently than before. He was still the same devilish instructor. That was great. Thanks to Silverian Schild, more students of the EmeraldShield Academy would survive in the Origin Expanse and make it big.
"Do you want to visit him? I'd love to talk to him and find out what happened to him in the last few decades. We could also give him a bunch of Energy Stones or a droplet of Origin Liquid. He deserves that much!" Alice exclaimed.
Michael nodded, "We can visit him in the future. As for the gifts, I already tried them. He didn't accept anything I tried giving to him. The only thing I could do was to invest – anonymously, of course – in creating the EmeraldShield Academy. I don't think he would have accepted my investment if I'd revealed myself. But then again, he is not stupid. He probably knows I'm the investor."
He shrugged and smiled again while paying attention to the struggling students suffering under Silverian Schild's tutelage. They were either going to make it big or break. Their willpower was the determining factor of their future.
Michael's attention drifted to someone else who was training students in archery in a different complex of the same building. Silverian Schild was known for training stamina, endurance, and willpower, but that was now all that could be studied in the EmeraldShield Academy. Archery was also one of the greatest subjects in the academy.
"That…is Annabelle Claire," Michael recalled the young Awakened. Michael fought her during the first assessment exam of the Saphirelake Military Academy. They talked only a few times, but she had always been nice. She was a decently powerful Awakened then and known for her great Soultrait Symbol called [Spirit Archer]. She didn't keep up with Lincoln, Zeke, Kaleb, or Michael, but she was at the Peak of the 6th Tier at this point.
Her growth was rapid compared to most of her peers, but instead of continuing her grind, Annabelle switched to teaching students.
"I think I remember her. Didn't she like you?" Alice asked, but Michael could only shrug, "I don't think she liked me. If anything, she liked Kaleb."
"Kaleb? Are you sure?" Alice asked before studying Annabelle again, "She's cute. Maybe Kaleb would have it easier…No nevermind. Let's forget about that."
Michael knew exactly what Alice was thinking about and smiled at her. Thus, he switched to another familiar face, an elderly man, who changed Michael's life forever.
Kraft Viton.
"Oh! What is Kraft Viton up to these days?" Alice asked, which was enough to make Michael smile, "He is still doing the same as always. If anything has changed, it would probably be that Kraft Viton is more energetic since he consumed the Origin Liquid droplet. You could say he is in full control of the Tritan Alliance now. Sometimes, you can see him beat the shit out of idiotic politicians. Those parts are the funniest."
"You can't be serious," Alice chuckled, only to burst into a full-blown laughter when Michael replayed the scenes from his memories in the liquid mirror. Kraft Viton beating the crap out of more than a dozen politicians, who'd considered themselves far more important than they truly were, had been beaten black and blue by an old man.
He slapped them a few times in the face, kicked them in the crotch, and had a lot more fun beating up weaklings than expected.
"He is a bully!" Alice exclaimed, but rather than considering that a bad thing, she enjoyed herself thoroughly
"As long as he only bullies the bad people, that's fine," Michael said, his expression turning somber as he recalled something else. A bad person who'd changed his life.
The liquid mirror switched to Quinn Karta.
"Oh shit! You know where Quinn is?" Alice asked, and Michael sighed deeply. Still, he nodded.
"He has been on the run for a few decades now, but the Guardians know where everyone connected to the weave is located. It didn't take long to find him. In fact, a few seconds was all it took for me to locate him," Michael sighed deeply. Quinn Karta destroyed the lives of many people in the Tritan Alliance. He was a traitor, a killer.
Still, Michael didn't pursue him to attack and eliminate him. No, that wasn't his task.
"I will give Zeke a hint, allowing him to hunt him down once he's ready for it."
"Zeke? Are you sure? Why not Killian? Or is Killian still troubled rebuilding the house of Zeus?"
"KIllian Zeus?" Michael asked, sighing once again, "He disappeared. I don't know where he is. That means…"
"Is he dead?" Alice asked, a wave of sadness overcoming her.
"No. Well, saying that I don't know where he is is not exactly the full truth. I know where he could be," Michael said, pointing at the border to the Unknown Domain, "He left the Origin Universe."

chapters.title: Chapter 1123 Supreme Lord V
chapters.content:
1123  Supreme Lord V
"He left the Origin Universe?" Alice asked, flabbergasted, "I thought he was struggling to advance to a Divine Lifeform for a while. He only managed to do it after you gave him a Origin Liquid droplet. So why would he leave the Origin Universe now?"
Michael sighed, "He didn't like that he could only advance with my help. Maybe it wasn't the best move to offer him my help when he was desperate to not fall behind. I could have been more considerate."
"You were already–..."
"I know, but it is never easy to understand how others are feeling. You might think I was considerable, but Killian considered me a rival in the past. He doesn't hate me or anything but I can clearly tell that he feels like a…loser. I shouldn't have given him the Origin Liquid droplet," He ruffled through his hair but calmed down after a moment, "But then again, maybe the Unknown Domain is the perfect place for killian. I read the first few reports made by Rebecca and Daniel and its promising. It is very interesting to think that there are more energies than origin energy."
Mana, Force, and Spirita. Michael visited the border to the Unknown Domain and tried scanning the energies once. He expected to be able to extract something out of them, but Extraction didn't work on them. The energy streams dispersed the moment Extraction tried grasping them. Something like that had never happened.
Yet, instead of being afraid of the unknown and the incapability of extracting it, Michael was excited. Unfortunately, the Guardians told him to stay in the Origin Universe. He could have ignored them but their point was valid.
Michael had no idea what enemies awaited him in the Unknown Domain and if there were Void Creatures. If there were Void Creatures in the Unknown Domain, Michael wouldn't be able to defeat them. After all, he was a Primal and the Supreme Lord, not a Guardian who had been created to fight Void Creatures.
He was probably fast and strong enough to make a run or seal some Void Creatures in the Void of the Expanse, but what if he died? The Origin Expanse would collapse, the economy and training ground of the entire cosmos would cease to exist, and it was unknown what would happen to the Expanse. After all, the Expanse was bound to him first. It might be attached to the Guardians, but they don't have a firm connection to it. They merely received as much Expanse Essence as they needed to retain stability with Origin Essence.
Michael's death might actually mean the end of the Origin Universe as it was known. The Guardians would become Primal again, and there would be nothing to defeat Void Creatures.
That being said, Michael decided to follow the Guardians' advice. He didn't like it, but their points were too good. That was unfortunate.
"You're thinking about the Unknown Domain again?" Alice asked in an icy tone. Michael pressed his lips together and didn't say anything for a few seconds. Alice sighed and patted his back, "I can tell how you're feeling, but you should stay by my side if you want to be there when–...." Alice shut her lips and smiled at Michael, whose expression twisted in confusion. "Oh, look. Isn't that Mekhaz, Thaor, and Lokai? They have been doing great! They started with the colonization of a new planet… When did they start with that?" Alice asked, trying her utmost to ignore Michael's burning gaze. He could tell Alice was hiding something, but there was no ill intention. If anything, Michael could sense excitement and happiness spurting out of her. He smiled at his lover and nodded.
"They have been busy with paperwork and training the young folk for a while now," Michael mumbled, "But I didn't know they were itching for a bloody battle this much. They must have been itching for a fight to lead the conquest of another planet. But then again…that suits Thaor and Lokai."
"That's true. They love fighting way too much," Alice chuckled, "I don't want to know what they will do after attaining godhood."
Michael shuddered, imagining Thaor and Lokai fighting other gods after stalking them for years to challenge them. That was going to be a nightmare.
"It's a good thing it will take a while before they can acquire their first combat Laws and Authorities," Michael added, and Alice nodded.
"That's for sure."
Alice looked at him and smiled again. She had something to say but decided against it. There was something else she wanted to mention first.
"Have you been talking to Maria Seraph lately?" She asked.
"No. Why are you asking?" It had been decades since Michael talked with Maria. In fact, it had been eons since he thought about her.
"I have no particular reason. Do you know what she is up to?" Alice continued inquiring, but Michael shook his head again.
"We can check on her if you want," Michael responded with a shrug, ready to configure the liquid mirror, but Alice stopped him mid-way.
She hesitated for a moment and tip-toed around for a good minute before finally gathering enough courage to speak up.
"Do you think I should talk to Maria to tell her about my baby? The last time I spoke to her, she told me how hurt she was about being left out when Lucia was born…"
"You want to visi–...your baby? Wait what?!" Michael's eyes widened and nearly popped out as he realized what Alice was talking about.
"You are pregnant again?" He asked, and Alice nodded faintly.
She rubbed her belly, and it was only now that Michael noticed something he hadn't realized before. Alice's connection to him and the weave had been covering a minuscule thread connecting to the Expanse and the Weave.
The baby growing in Alice's belly was connected to Essences already. It was overflowing with Essence.
A New Primal was growing within her.
Michael swallowed hard.
His life was not yet over. If anything, the joy of living in the Origin Universe was just about to descend upon him.
[The End]
